action.tip_zh: 第一音節 [æk] 常被唸成 [ɛk]，嘴巴張得太小；[æ] 要把下巴往下拉、嘴角往兩邊開，像說 apple 的開頭。第二音節 [ʃən] 的 [ʃ] 不是注音的ㄒ，要把嘴唇嘟出去、舌頭往後收一點。字尾 [n] 要用舌尖頂住上排牙齦收尾，不要唸成 [ŋ]。
action.tip_en: The first syllable [æk] is often said as [ɛk], with the mouth too closed; for [æ], drop the jaw and spread the corners of the mouth, like the start of apple. In the second syllable [ʃən], [ʃ] is not Mandarin ㄒ: push the lips forward and pull the tongue back a little. Finish [n] with the tongue tip pressed on the upper gum ridge; don't turn it into [ŋ].

examples.en: Our class took action to save water at school.
examples.zh: 我們班採取行動，在學校節約用水。

examples.en: We need to take action and clean up the park.
examples.zh: 我們需要採取行動，把公園打掃乾淨。

actor.tip_zh: 字尾的 -or 不是唸 [ɔr]，而是輕輕的 [tɚ]，舌頭往後捲、不碰任何地方。另一個常見問題是在 [k] 後面多加一個母音，變成三個音節。[k] 只要舌根頂一下就直接接 [t]，兩個子音緊緊相連，整個字只有 [æk] 和 [tɚ] 兩拍，重音在 [æk]。
actor.tip_en: The final -or is not said [ɔr] but as a light [tɚ]: curl the tongue back without touching anything. Another common problem is adding a vowel after [k], which makes three syllables. The back of the tongue only taps for [k] and goes straight into [t], two consonants tightly joined, so the word has just two beats, [æk] and [tɚ], with the stress on [æk].

examples.en: My cousin wants to be an actor someday.
examples.zh: 我表哥以後想當演員。

examples.en: The actor waved to the kids after the show.
examples.zh: 表演結束後，那位演員向小朋友揮手。

actually.tip_zh: 常見的錯誤是每個音節都唸得一樣重，或把重音放錯在第二音節 [tʃʊ]。這個字只有第一音節 [æk] 重讀，嘴巴張大；後面的 [tʃʊəlɪ] 要又輕又快地帶過。[tʃ] 要把嘴唇嘟出去，跟 chew 的開頭一樣，不是注音的ㄑ。
actually.tip_en: A common mistake is giving every syllable the same weight, or wrongly stressing the second syllable [tʃʊ]. Only the first syllable [æk] is stressed, with the mouth open wide; the rest, [tʃʊəlɪ], should be light and quick. For [tʃ], push the lips forward as at the start of chew; it is not Mandarin ㄑ.

examples.en: Actually, I like math more than art.
examples.zh: 其實，比起美術我更喜歡數學。

examples.en: The test was actually easier than I thought.
examples.zh: 考試其實比我想的還簡單。

actually.variant_en: In fast speech it often shrinks to [ˈæktʃəlɪ] or [ˈækʃəlɪ].
actually.kk_flag: The secondary-stress mark before tʃu is unusual: General American actually has only the primary stress on the first syllable, [ˈæktʃuəlɪ].

after.tip_zh: 美式發音的 [æ] 要把嘴巴張大，學生卻容易唸成英式的 [ɑ] 或太扁的 [ɛ]。[f] 是上排牙齒輕碰下唇吹氣，吹完直接接 [t]，中間不要多一個母音，否則會變成三個音節。字尾 [tɚ] 舌頭往後捲，不要唸成沒有捲舌的「特」。
after.tip_en: American [æ] needs a wide-open mouth, but learners tend to say British-style [ɑ] or a too-flat [ɛ]. For [f], the upper teeth touch the lower lip lightly and blow; then go straight into [t] with no vowel in between, or the word turns into three syllables. In the ending [tɚ], curl the tongue back; don't say an un-curled 特.

examples.en: We play basketball after school.
examples.zh: 我們放學後打籃球。

examples.en: Please wash your hands after you eat.
examples.zh: 吃完東西後請洗手。

afternoon.tip_zh: 因為 after 的重音在前面，學生常把 afternoon 的重音也放在第一音節。其實主要重音在最後的 [nun]，要唸得最長、最響；[æf] 只是次重音，中間的 [tɚ] 輕輕帶過。結尾的 [n] 舌尖要頂住上排牙齦停住，不要變成 [ŋ]。
afternoon.tip_en: Because after is stressed at the front, learners often stress afternoon on the first syllable too. In fact the main stress is on the last syllable [nun], which should be the longest and loudest; [æf] only gets secondary stress, and the middle [tɚ] is passed over lightly. For the final [n], hold the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge; don't let it become [ŋ].

examples.en: We have art class on Monday afternoon.
examples.zh: 我們星期一下午有美術課。

examples.en: My grandma takes a nap every afternoon.
examples.zh: 我奶奶每天下午都會睡午覺。

already.tip_zh: already 是一個字，重音在第二音節 [ˈrɛ]，和 ready 押韻；學生常把重音放在開頭，聽起來像兩個字 all ready（全都準備好）。第一音節 [ɔl] 要短一點、輕一點。[rɛ] 的母音是 [ɛ]，跟 red 的母音一樣，不要唸成會滑動的 [e]，像 rain 那樣。
already.tip_en: Already is one word stressed on the second syllable [ˈrɛ], and it rhymes with ready; learners often stress the start, which makes it sound like the two words all ready (all prepared). Keep the first syllable [ɔl] shorter and lighter. The vowel in [rɛ] is [ɛ], the same as in red; don't say the gliding [e], as in rain.

examples.en: I already finished my homework.
examples.zh: 我已經寫完功課了。

examples.en: It's already eight o'clock, so let's go.
examples.zh: 已經八點了，我們走吧。

america.tip_zh: 受中文「美國」影響，學生常把 [mɛ] 唸成「美」那樣的 [me]，嘴型太扁還會滑動。KK 是 [ɛ]，跟 men 的母音一樣，短而不滑。重音在第二音節 [ˈmɛ]，開頭的 [ə] 只是輕輕一聲，不要唸成響亮的「阿」；最後的 [kə] 也要放輕，不要唸成重重的 [kɑ]。
america.tip_en: Influenced by the Chinese 美國, learners often say [mɛ] like 美, i.e. [me], too flat and gliding. The KK is [ɛ], the vowel of men, short and steady. The stress is on the second syllable [ˈmɛ]; the opening [ə] is just a light sound, not a loud ah, and the last [kə] stays light too, not a heavy [kɑ].

examples.en: My uncle lives in America.
examples.zh: 我叔叔住在美國。

examples.en: We learned about North America in class today.
examples.zh: 我們今天上課學了北美洲。

american.tip_zh: 字尾的 [kən] 常被唸成響亮的 [kæn]，聽起來像 can，或是收成 [kəŋ]。這個字的重音在 [ˈmɛ]，[kən] 是最輕的一拍：[ə] 幾乎一帶而過，最後舌尖頂住上排牙齦收 [n]，不要讓舌根抬起變成 [ŋ]。開頭的 [ə] 也要輕，不要唸成「阿」。
american.tip_en: The ending [kən] is often said as a loud [kæn], like can, or closed as [kəŋ]. The stress is on [ˈmɛ], and [kən] is the lightest beat: pass over [ə] almost instantly, then finish [n] with the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge; don't let the back of the tongue rise into [ŋ]. The opening [ə] is light too, not a full ah.

examples.en: Our new teacher is American.
examples.zh: 我們的新老師是美國人。

examples.en: We ate American pancakes for breakfast.
examples.zh: 我們早餐吃了美式鬆餅。

angle.tip_zh: angle 常和 angel（天使）搞混，被唸成 [ˈendʒəl]。angle 的 [æ] 嘴巴要張大，接著舌根抬起發 [ŋ]，再直接接 [g]，是硬的 [g]，不是 [dʒ]。字尾 [ḷ] 舌尖要頂住上排牙齦，不要在 [g] 後面加一個像 [o] 的母音。重音在第一音節，[gḷ] 輕輕收尾。
angle.tip_en: Angle is often confused with angel (天使) and said as [ˈendʒəl]. In angle, open the mouth wide for [æ], lift the back of the tongue for [ŋ], and go straight into [g], a hard [g], not [dʒ]. For the final [ḷ], put the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge; don't add an [o]-like vowel after [g]. The stress is on the first syllable, and [gḷ] closes the word lightly.

examples.en: Use your ruler to draw an angle.
examples.zh: 用你的尺畫一個角。

examples.en: Let's take a photo from a different angle.
examples.zh: 我們換個角度拍照吧。

angle.spelling_zh: angle 和 angel 只差 l、e 的順序，發音卻完全不同。
angle.spelling_en: Angle and angel differ only in the order of l and e, but sound completely different.

angry.tip_zh: angry 常和 hungry 搞混。angry 是 [ˈæŋgrɪ]，開頭沒有 [h]，母音是嘴巴張大的 [æ]；hungry 則是 [ˈhʌŋgrɪ]。另外 [ŋ] 後面要接一個清楚的 [g]，再馬上接捲舌的 [r]，[g] 和 [r] 中間不要加母音，整個字只有兩拍。練習時可以先說 hungry，再拿掉 [h]，把嘴巴張大換成 [æ]。
angry.tip_en: Angry is often confused with hungry. Angry is [ˈæŋgrɪ], with no [h] and the wide-open vowel [æ]; hungry is [ˈhʌŋgrɪ]. Also, after [ŋ] there must be a clear [g], followed at once by a curled [r]; don't put a vowel between [g] and [r]. The whole word has only two beats. To practice, say hungry, then drop the [h] and open the mouth wide to switch to [æ].

examples.en: My little brother gets angry when he loses a game.
examples.zh: 我弟弟輸了遊戲就會生氣。

examples.en: Please don't be angry with me.
examples.zh: 請不要生我的氣。

animal.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [ˈæ]，嘴巴張大；中間的 [nə] 要輕而短，不要唸成清楚的 [ni]。最難的是結尾 [mḷ]：雙唇閉起來發 [m] 之後，舌尖直接頂到上排牙齦發 [ḷ]，中間不要多加一個像「歐」的母音，舌頭也不要整個放掉。
animal.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [ˈæ] with the mouth wide open; the middle [nə] is light and short, not a clear [ni]. The hardest part is the ending [mḷ]: close the lips for [m], then put the tongue tip straight up on the upper gum ridge for [ḷ]. Don't add an oh-like vowel in between, and don't let the tongue drop away.

examples.en: My favorite animal is the panda.
examples.zh: 我最喜歡的動物是貓熊。

examples.en: What animal can you see in this picture?
examples.zh: 你在這張圖裡看到什麼動物？

another.tip_zh: [ð] 常被換成 [d]、[z] 或 [l]。發 [ð] 時舌尖輕放在上下牙齒之間，喉嚨要振動，讓氣從舌頭旁邊出來。another 就是 a 加上 nother，和 mother 押韻；重音在 [ˈnʌ]，[ʌ] 嘴巴微開、短促，不要唸成 [ɑ]。字尾 [ðɚ] 舌尖從牙齒間收回，再往後捲。
another.tip_en: [ð] is often replaced with [d], [z], or [l]. For [ð], rest the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower teeth and make the throat vibrate, letting the air pass beside the tongue. Another is a plus nother, rhyming with mother; the stress is on [ˈnʌ], and [ʌ] is short with the mouth slightly open, not [ɑ]. For the ending [ðɚ], pull the tongue tip back from the teeth and curl it.

examples.en: Can I have another cookie, please?
examples.zh: 我可以再吃一塊餅乾嗎？

examples.en: We will read another story tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我們明天會再讀另一個故事。

answer.tip_zh: 拼字裡的 w 不發音，學生卻常把它唸出來，變成「安斯威爾」。answer 只有兩個音節：[æn] 嘴巴張大，舌尖頂住上排牙齦收 [n]，再接 [sɚ]。它和 dancer [ˈdænsɚ] 押韻，把 dancer 去掉 [d] 來練就對了。字尾 [ɚ] 要捲舌，重音在第一音節。
answer.tip_en: The w in the spelling is silent, yet learners often pronounce it, saying something like an-swi-er. Answer has only two syllables: [æn] with the mouth wide open and the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n], then [sɚ]. It rhymes with dancer [ˈdænsɚ]; practice by saying dancer without the [d]. Curl the tongue for the final [ɚ]; the stress is on the first syllable.

examples.en: Raise your hand if you know the answer.
examples.zh: 如果你知道答案，請舉手。

examples.en: Can you answer this question?
examples.zh: 你可以回答這個問題嗎？

answer.spelling_en: The w is silent; sw is pronounced just [s].

anyone.tip_zh: 看到開頭的 a，學生常唸成 [æ]，但 any 的 a 唸 [ɛ]，跟 penny 去掉 [p] 一樣。後半的 one 唸 [wʌn]，拼字雖然沒有 w，開頭卻要先圓唇發 [w]；[ʌ] 短而放鬆，不要唸成像「萬」的 [wɑn]。重音在第一音節 [ˈɛ]。和 everyone、someone 一樣，結尾的 one 都唸 [wʌn]，舌尖頂住上排牙齦收 [n]。
anyone.tip_en: Seeing the a at the start, learners often say [æ], but the a in any is [ɛ], like penny without the [p]. The second half, one, is [wʌn]: there is no w in the spelling, but you start by rounding the lips for [w]; [ʌ] is short and relaxed, not the [wɑn] of 萬. The stress is on the first syllable [ˈɛ]. As in everyone and someone, the final one is [wʌn], ending with the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n].

examples.en: Does anyone have an extra pencil?
examples.zh: 有人有多的鉛筆嗎？

examples.en: Did anyone see my blue jacket?
examples.zh: 有人看到我的藍色外套嗎？

anyone.spelling_zh: any 的 a 唸 [ɛ]；one 沒有 w，卻唸 [wʌn]。
anyone.spelling_en: The a in any is [ɛ]; one has no w but is said [wʌn].

anything.tip_zh: 第三音節的 [θ] 常被唸成 [s]，anything 就變成 anysing。發 [θ] 時舌尖伸到上下牙齒之間，只吹氣、喉嚨不振動。字尾 [ŋ] 是舌根貼住軟顎、讓氣從鼻子出來，不要換成 [n]，也不要在後面多加 [g] 或 [k]。和 everything 一樣，重音在第一音節。
anything.tip_en: The [θ] in the third syllable is often said as [s], turning anything into anysing. For [θ], put the tongue tip between the upper and lower teeth and just blow air, with no throat vibration. The final [ŋ] is made with the back of the tongue against the soft palate and air through the nose; don't swap it for [n] or add a [g] or [k] after it. Like everything, it is stressed on the first syllable.

examples.en: Do you need anything from the store?
examples.zh: 你需要從店裡買什麼東西嗎？

examples.en: I can't find anything in my messy bag.
examples.zh: 我在亂七八糟的包包裡什麼都找不到。

apartment.tip_zh: 重音在第二音節 [ˈpɑrt]，學生常把重音放錯在開頭。[ɑrt] 要先把嘴巴張大發 [ɑ]，再往後捲舌。[t] 接 [m] 的地方，舌尖碰一下上排牙齦就直接閉唇發 [m]，中間不要加母音。字尾 [mənt] 輕輕帶過，[n] 和 [t] 的舌尖位置一樣，舌頭不用移動。
apartment.tip_en: The stress is on the second syllable [ˈpɑrt]; learners often wrongly stress the beginning. For [ɑrt], open the mouth wide for [ɑ], then curl the tongue back. Where [t] meets [m], the tongue tip just touches the upper gum ridge and the lips close straight into [m], with no vowel in between. The ending [mənt] is light; [n] and [t] use the same tongue-tip position, so the tongue doesn't move.

examples.en: We live in an apartment on the fifth floor.
examples.zh: 我們住在五樓的公寓。

examples.en: Her apartment is next to the park.
examples.zh: 她的公寓就在公園旁邊。

apple.tip_zh: 常見的錯誤是把結尾唸成「阿婆」那樣，在 [p] 後面加一個像「ㄛ」的母音。正確的 [pḷ] 是發完 [p] 後，舌尖立刻頂住上排牙齦，讓聲音從舌頭兩側出來。開頭的 [æ] 嘴巴要張得比「ㄟ」大，下巴往下拉、嘴角往兩邊開。
apple.tip_en: A common mistake is ending the word like 阿婆, adding an ㄛ-like vowel after [p]. For a correct [pḷ], right after [p] raise the tongue tip to the upper gum ridge and let the sound flow out past the sides of the tongue. For the opening [æ], open the mouth wider than ㄟ: drop the jaw and spread the corners of the mouth.

examples.en: I eat an apple every morning.
examples.zh: 我每天早上吃一顆蘋果。

examples.en: This apple is red and sweet.
examples.zh: 這顆蘋果又紅又甜。

area.tip_zh: area 有三個音節，重音在第一音節 [ˈɛ]。學生常照著拼字用 [ɑ] 開頭，或把 [ɛr] 唸成不捲舌的 [e]。其實開頭聽起來就是 air [ɛr]，接著是輕輕的 [ɪ]，最後是非常弱的 [ə]。可以先說 air，再接上 [ɪə]，三拍一重兩輕。
area.tip_en: Area has three syllables, stressed on the first, [ˈɛ]. Learners often follow the spelling and start with [ɑ], or say [ɛr] as an un-curled [e]. In fact the start sounds just like air [ɛr], followed by a light [ɪ] and finally a very weak [ə]. Say air first and then add [ɪə]; the three beats go strong, weak, weak.

examples.en: This area of the park is for picnics.
examples.zh: 公園的這一區是野餐用的。

examples.en: Our library has a quiet reading area.
examples.zh: 我們的圖書館有一個安靜的閱讀區。

around.tip_zh: 開頭的 [ə] 又輕又短，學生常唸成響亮的「阿」，或乾脆省略。重音在後面的 [ˈraʊnd]：舌頭先捲好發 [r]，嘴巴再從 [a] 張大，滑到圓唇的 [ʊ]，和 round、sound 押韻。字尾 [nd] 舌尖先頂住上排牙齦發 [n]，原地輕輕放開帶出 [d]，不要多加一個「的」的母音。
around.tip_en: The opening [ə] is light and short; learners often make it a loud ah or drop it. The stress is on the second part [ˈraʊnd]: curl the tongue for [r] first, then open wide for [a] and glide to rounded [ʊ]; it rhymes with round and sound. For the final [nd], press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n], then release it in place for [d]; don't add a vowel like 的.

examples.en: We walked around the lake after dinner.
examples.zh: 我們晚餐後繞著湖散步。

examples.en: There are trees all around our school.
examples.zh: 我們學校四周都是樹。

around.kk_flag: Taiwan KK dictionaries write [əˈraʊnd], with r starting the stressed syllable; this CMU-derived [ɚˈaʊnd] puts the r in the unstressed syllable. The sound is nearly the same, but the split ɚ·aʊnd may look odd to teachers.

arrive.tip_zh: 結尾的 [v] 常被唸成 [f] 或 [b]，或在後面多加一個母音。發 [v] 時上排牙齒輕碰下唇，喉嚨要振動，像蜜蜂嗡嗡的聲音，振動結束就收尾。重音在後面的 [ˈraɪv]，和 five、drive 押韻；開頭的 [ə] 輕輕帶過就好。
arrive.tip_en: The final [v] is often said as [f] or [b], or followed by an extra vowel. For [v], rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and make the throat vibrate, like a buzzing bee, and stop when the buzz ends. The stress is on [ˈraɪv], which rhymes with five and drive; the opening [ə] is passed over lightly.

examples.en: The bus will arrive at seven.
examples.zh: 公車七點會到。

examples.en: What time did you arrive at school today?
examples.zh: 你今天幾點到學校？

arrive.kk_flag: Taiwan KK dictionaries write [əˈraɪv]; this CMU-derived [ɚˈaɪv] puts the r in the unstressed syllable instead of starting the stressed one, so the split ɚ·aɪv may look odd to teachers.

as.tip_zh: as 和 at 只差最後一個音。[z] 要讓喉嚨振動，學生常唸成無聲的 [s]，聽起來像「ㄟ斯」。練習時把手放在喉嚨上，要感覺到振動。[æ] 嘴巴要張大，不要唸成 [ɛ]。在句子裡 as 常常輕讀，但結尾的 [z] 一樣要有振動。
as.tip_en: As and at differ only in the last sound. [z] needs a vibrating throat; learners often say a voiceless [s], something like ehs. When practicing, put a hand on your throat and feel the vibration. Open the mouth wide for [æ], not [ɛ]. In sentences as is often said lightly, but the final [z] must still vibrate.

examples.en: My brother is as tall as my dad.
examples.zh: 我哥哥跟我爸爸一樣高。

examples.en: Run as fast as you can!
examples.zh: 用你最快的速度跑！

as.variant_zh: 在句子中不強調時，常弱讀成 [əz]，例如 as tall as。
as.variant_en: When unstressed in a sentence it is often reduced to [əz], e.g. as tall as.

aunt.tip_zh: 因為拼字有 au，學生常唸成 [ɔnt]，像 August 的開頭那樣。美式發音最常見的是 [ænt]，和 ant（螞蟻）完全同音，嘴巴要張大。結尾 [nt] 舌尖頂住上排牙齦先發 [n]，舌頭不移動，直接放出 [t]，不要加一個「特」的母音。
aunt.tip_en: Because of the au spelling, learners often say [ɔnt], like the start of August. The most common American pronunciation is [ænt], exactly the same as ant (螞蟻), with the mouth open wide. For the final [nt], put the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n], then release [t] without moving the tongue; don't add a vowel like 特.

examples.en: My aunt lives in Taichung.
examples.zh: 我阿姨住在台中。

examples.en: We visit my aunt every Chinese New Year.
examples.zh: 我們每年過年都會去拜訪阿姨。

aunt.variant_zh: 也有美國人唸 [ɑnt]，但 [ænt] 最常見。
aunt.variant_en: Some Americans say [ɑnt], but [ænt] is the most common.
aunt.spelling_zh: au 在這裡不唸 [ɔ]，aunt 和 ant 同音。
aunt.spelling_en: Here au is not [ɔ]; aunt sounds the same as ant.

autumn.tip_zh: 結尾的 n 不發音，autumn 只唸到 [təm] 為止，學生卻常把 n 也唸出來。最後的 [m] 一定要雙唇閉緊，不要唸成嘴巴開著的「恩」。開頭的 [ɔ] 嘴巴張開、稍微圓唇，不要唸成嘴型很小的 [o]。重音在第一音節，[təm] 輕輕帶過。
autumn.tip_en: The final n is silent; autumn ends at [təm], yet learners often pronounce the n as well. The final [m] must be made with the lips firmly closed, not an open-mouthed 恩. For the opening [ɔ], open the mouth and round the lips slightly; don't use the small-mouthed [o]. The stress is on the first syllable; [təm] is light.

examples.en: The leaves turn red and yellow in autumn.
examples.zh: 秋天時，樹葉會變紅、變黃。

examples.en: Autumn is my favorite season.
examples.zh: 秋天是我最喜歡的季節。

autumn.spelling_zh: 字尾 mn 的 n 不發音，和 column 一樣。
autumn.spelling_en: The n in the final mn is silent, as in column.

badminton.tip_zh: 學生常把開頭唸成 [bɛd] 或 [bɑd]，其實 badminton 的開頭就是 bad [bæd]，嘴巴張大，[d] 也要保留。重音只在第一音節，[mɪn] 輕輕帶過。結尾 [tṇ] 不要唸成像「頓」的 [tən] 或 [tɑn]：舌尖頂住上排牙齦發 [t] 後不放開，直接讓氣從鼻子出來發 [ṇ]。
badminton.tip_en: Learners often start the word with [bɛd] or [bɑd], but badminton begins exactly like bad [bæd]: open the mouth wide and keep the [d]. Only the first syllable is stressed; [mɪn] is passed over lightly. Don't end with a [tən] or [tɑn] like 頓: put the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [t], keep it there, and let the air out through the nose for [ṇ].

examples.en: We play badminton in the park on Sundays.
examples.zh: 我們星期天在公園打羽毛球。

examples.en: My sister is really good at badminton.
examples.zh: 我姊姊羽毛球打得很好。

bakery.tip_zh: bakery 就是 bake 加上 -ry，第一音節和 bake 一樣是 [be]，學生卻常唸成短促的 [bɛ]。[e] 是會滑動的母音，嘴型從 [e] 微微滑向 [ɪ]，嘴角往兩邊拉。重音在 [ˈbe]；後面的 [kərɪ] 要輕：[kə] 輕輕帶過，再把舌頭往後捲，唸短短的 [rɪ]。
bakery.tip_en: Bakery is just bake plus -ry; the first syllable is [be], the same as in bake, but learners often say a short [bɛ]. [e] is a gliding vowel: the mouth moves slightly from [e] toward [ɪ], with the lip corners pulled back. The stress is on [ˈbe]; keep the following [kərɪ] light: pass over [kə] quickly, then curl the tongue back for a short [rɪ].

examples.en: The bakery near my school sells yummy bread.
examples.zh: 我學校附近的麵包店賣好吃的麵包。

examples.en: Let's buy a birthday cake at the bakery.
examples.zh: 我們去麵包店買生日蛋糕吧。

bakery.variant_zh: 說快時常縮成兩個音節 [ˈbekrɪ]。
bakery.variant_en: In fast speech it often shrinks to two syllables, [ˈbekrɪ].

balcony.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [bæl]，不是 bal-CO-ny。[æ] 嘴巴要張大、嘴角往兩旁拉，不要唸成 [ɛ]。學生常把 [l] 吞掉，聽起來像 back-ony；唸完 [æ] 後，舌尖要先頂住上排牙齒後方的牙齦，停一下再接 [k]。後面的 [kə] 和 [nɪ] 都輕輕帶過，不要每個音節一樣重。
balcony.tip_en: The stress is on the first syllable [bæl], not bal-CO-ny. For [æ], open the mouth wide and pull the lip corners sideways; don't say [ɛ]. Students often swallow the [l], so it sounds like 'back-ony'; after [æ], press the tongue tip on the gum ridge behind the upper teeth, hold it briefly, then go to [k]. The following [kə] and [nɪ] are both said lightly — don't make every syllable equally strong.

examples.en: Grandma grows flowers on her balcony.
examples.zh: 奶奶在她的陽台上種花。

examples.en: Our cat likes to sleep on the balcony.
examples.zh: 我們家的貓喜歡在陽台上睡覺。

banana.tip_zh: 重音在中間的 [næ]，不是第一個音節。學生常唸成三個一樣重、嘴巴都張很大的「巴娜娜」。正確唸法：頭尾兩個 [ə] 都很短，嘴巴放鬆、幾乎不用力；中間的 [næ] 唸得又長又響，嘴巴張大、嘴角往兩旁拉。可以邊拍手邊練習：小、大、小。
banana.tip_en: The stress is on the middle [næ], not the first syllable. Students often say 'ba-na-na' with three equally strong, wide-open syllables. The right way: the [ə] at the start and at the end are both very short, with a relaxed mouth and almost no effort; the middle [næ] is long and loud, with the mouth wide open and the lip corners pulled sideways. Practice while clapping: small, BIG, small.

examples.en: I eat a banana with my breakfast every morning.
examples.zh: 我每天早上吃早餐時都會配一根香蕉。

examples.en: The monkey is holding a yellow banana.
examples.zh: 那隻猴子拿著一根黃色的香蕉。

basketball.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [bæs]，[æ] 嘴巴張大，不要唸成 [ɛ]。中間 [kət] 的 [t] 後面緊接著 [b]，舌尖頂住牙齦就好，不要多唸出一個「特」。最後的 [bɔl] 學生常只唸成「波」，把 [l] 漏掉；唸完 [ɔ] 舌尖要往上頂住上排牙齦，這個字才算唸完。
basketball.tip_en: The stress is on the first syllable [bæs]; open the mouth wide for [æ] and don't say [ɛ]. In the middle part [kət], the [t] is followed right away by [b]: just press the tongue tip on the gum ridge, without adding an extra 'tuh'. Students often say the last part [bɔl] as just 'bo' and leave out the [l]; after [ɔ], lift the tongue tip to the upper gum ridge — only then is the word finished.

examples.en: My brother plays basketball after school.
examples.zh: 我哥哥放學後會去打籃球。

examples.en: Can you throw the basketball to me?
examples.zh: 你可以把籃球丟給我嗎？

bath.tip_zh: 字尾的 [θ] 是這個字最難的地方。學生常唸成 [s]，變成 [bæs]，或唸成 [f]。中文沒有這個音：舌尖輕輕伸到上下牙齒中間，用力吹氣，喉嚨不震動。前面的 [æ] 嘴巴要張大，不然聽起來會像人名 Beth。唸完 [θ] 就停，不要再多加一個母音。
bath.tip_en: The final [θ] is the hardest part of this word. Students often say [s], making it [bæs], or say [f]. Mandarin has no such sound: put the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower teeth and blow air, with no vibration in the throat. Open the mouth wide for the [æ] before it, or it will sound like the name Beth. Stop right after [θ] — don't add another vowel.

examples.en: I take a bath before I go to bed.
examples.zh: 我睡覺前會洗澡。

examples.en: Our dog doesn't like to take a bath.
examples.zh: 我們家的狗不喜歡洗澡。

bathroom.tip_zh: 難點在中間 [θ] 緊接著 [r]。學生常把 [θ] 唸成 [s] 或 [f]，或在兩個音中間多加一個母音。練法：先把舌尖放在上下牙齒之間吹氣發 [θ]，再把舌頭往後縮、舌尖捲起來接 [r]，中間不要停頓。第一音節 [bæ] 是重音，嘴巴要張大。
bathroom.tip_en: The hard part is the [θ] followed right away by [r] in the middle. Students often turn [θ] into [s] or [f], or add an extra vowel between the two sounds. Practice: put the tongue tip between the upper and lower teeth and blow air for [θ], then pull the tongue back and curl the tip up for [r], without pausing in between. The first syllable [bæ] carries the stress — open the mouth wide.

examples.en: Please wash your hands in the bathroom before dinner.
examples.zh: 吃晚餐前請先去浴室洗手。

examples.en: Mom is cleaning the bathroom this morning.
examples.zh: 媽媽今天早上在打掃浴室。

bathroom.variant_zh: room 也常唸成短一點的 [rʊm]，[ˈbæθrʊm] 一樣正確。
bathroom.variant_en: room is also often said with the shorter [rʊm]; [ˈbæθrʊm] is just as correct.

beautiful.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [bju]，記得 [b] 後面有 [j]，不是 [bu]。中間的 [t] 美國人常唸成很快的輕 d 音，舌尖在牙齦上輕彈一下就好，不要唸成重重的「特」。最後的 [fḷ] 學生常唸成「佛」，把 [l] 漏掉：上排牙齒碰下唇發 [f]，接著舌尖往上頂住牙齦，中間不要另外加母音。
beautiful.tip_en: The stress is on the first syllable [bju]; remember there is a [j] after [b] — it's not [bu]. Americans often say the middle [t] as a quick, light d sound: just flick the tongue tip once on the gum ridge, not a heavy 'tuh'. Students often say the last part [fḷ] like 'fo' and drop the [l]: touch the upper teeth to the lower lip for [f], then raise the tongue tip to the gum ridge, without adding a vowel in between.

examples.en: The flowers in the park are beautiful today.
examples.zh: 今天公園裡的花好漂亮。

examples.en: My sister drew a beautiful picture of our house.
examples.zh: 我妹妹畫了一張很漂亮的圖，畫的是我們家。

bed.tip_zh: [ɛ] 嘴巴半開，比 [e] 張大一點、比 [æ] 小一點；張太大就會變成 bad。字尾的 [d] 是另一個難點：中文沒有子音結尾，學生常把它吞掉，或多唸成「貝德」。唸完 [ɛ] 後舌尖頂住上排牙齦、喉嚨震動，短短收住就好。[d] 前面的 [ɛ] 可以拉長一點，才不會聽起來像 bet。
bed.tip_en: For [ɛ], the mouth is half open — a little wider than [e] and a little smaller than [æ]; open too wide and it becomes 'bad'. The final [d] is the other hard part: Mandarin has no consonant endings, so students often swallow it, or add a vowel and say 'beh-duh'. After [ɛ], press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge with the throat vibrating, and close it off short. The [ɛ] before [d] can be a little longer, so it doesn't sound like 'bet'.

examples.en: It's nine o'clock, time for bed!
examples.zh: 九點了，該上床睡覺囉！

examples.en: I make my bed every morning.
examples.zh: 我每天早上都會整理床鋪。

bicycle.tip_zh: 學生知道 cycle 唸 [saɪ]，就把第二音節也唸成 [saɪ]，甚至把重音移到後面。其實 bicycle 只有第一音節 [baɪ] 是重音，第二音節是短短的 [sɪ]，嘴巴不要再張開滑成 [aɪ]。最後的 [kḷ] 不要唸成「扣」：舌根發完 [k] 後，舌尖直接往上頂住牙齦接 [l]。
bicycle.tip_en: Students know 'cycle' is said with [saɪ], so they say the second syllable as [saɪ] too, and even move the stress back. In fact, only the first syllable [baɪ] of bicycle is stressed; the second syllable is a short [sɪ] — don't open the mouth again and glide into [aɪ]. Don't say the last part [kḷ] like 'ko': after the back of the tongue makes [k], raise the tongue tip straight to the gum ridge for [l].

examples.en: I ride my bicycle to school.
examples.zh: 我騎腳踏車上學。

examples.en: Dad bought me a new red bicycle.
examples.zh: 爸爸買了一台新的紅色腳踏車給我。

bicycle.spelling_zh: 中間的 cy 唸短的 [sɪ]，跟 cycle 的 [saɪ] 不一樣。
bicycle.spelling_en: The cy in the middle is a short [sɪ], not the [saɪ] of 'cycle'.

bird.tip_zh: [ɝ] 是整個母音都要捲舌的音，學生常唸成「伯」，或只發 [ə] 沒捲舌，聽起來像 bud。練法：舌尖往上捲但不碰到上顎，嘴唇微微噘起，[b] 一放開就開始捲舌，一直維持到最後。字尾的 [d] 要收住，舌尖頂住牙齦，不要變成「伯德」。可以和 bed、bad 對照練習。
bird.tip_en: [ɝ] is a vowel with the tongue curled the whole way through. Students often say it like 'bo', or just say [ə] without curling, so it sounds like 'bud'. Practice: curl the tongue tip up without touching the roof of the mouth and round the lips slightly; start curling the moment [b] opens and hold it to the end. Close off the final [d] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge — don't make it 'bo-duh'. Practice it against 'bed' and 'bad'.

examples.en: A little bird is singing in the tree.
examples.zh: 一隻小鳥在樹上唱歌。

examples.en: Look! That bird has blue feathers.
examples.zh: 你看！那隻鳥有藍色的羽毛。

birthday.tip_zh: 第一音節 [bɝθ] 連著兩個難音：先捲舌的 [ɝ]，再把舌尖伸到上下牙齒中間吹氣發 [θ]。學生常把 [θ] 唸成 [s] 或 [f]，變成 burs-day，或者根本沒有捲舌。練法：捲舌唸 [ɝ]，接著舌頭往前伸出牙齒，再把舌尖收回頂住牙齦接 [d]。第二音節 [de] 是次重音，母音要唸完整。
birthday.tip_en: The first syllable [bɝθ] has two hard sounds in a row: first the curled [ɝ], then the tongue tip out between the teeth, blowing air for [θ]. Students often turn [θ] into [s] or [f], making it 'burs-day', or don't curl the tongue at all. Practice: curl for [ɝ], then push the tongue forward past the teeth, then pull the tip back onto the gum ridge for [d]. The second syllable [de] has secondary stress, so say its vowel fully.

examples.en: Today is my best friend's birthday.
examples.zh: 今天是我最好的朋友的生日。

examples.en: We made a card for Mom's birthday.
examples.zh: 我們為媽媽的生日做了一張卡片。

blackboard.tip_zh: 開頭的 [bl] 中間不能加母音，學生常唸成「布萊克」；嘴唇閉起來發 [b] 的時候，舌尖就要先頂好牙齦，一放開就是 [l]。[æ] 嘴巴要張大。[k] 後面直接接 [b]，舌根把氣堵住就好，不必放出聲音。結尾的 [rd] 先捲舌，再讓舌尖頂住牙齦，不要只唸到「波」就停。
blackboard.tip_en: No vowel may go between the [b] and [l] at the start; students often say 'buh-lack'. While the lips close for [b], the tongue tip should already be on the gum ridge, so the release goes straight into [l]. Open the mouth wide for [æ]. The [k] is followed directly by [b]: just block the air with the back of the tongue, without releasing a sound. For the final [rd], curl the tongue first, then put the tip on the gum ridge — don't stop at 'bo'.

examples.en: The teacher wrote the date on the blackboard.
examples.zh: 老師把日期寫在黑板上。

examples.en: Can I help clean the blackboard?
examples.zh: 我可以幫忙擦黑板嗎？

blanket.tip_zh: 第一音節 [blæŋ] 的 n 其實是 [ŋ]，因為後面接著 [k]：舌根往上頂住軟顎，跟 pink、thank 的鼻音一樣，不要用舌尖發 [n]。開頭的 [bl] 中間別加母音。第二音節 [kət] 很輕，結尾的 [t] 舌尖頂住牙齦就收，不要唸出「特」。重音在第一音節。
blanket.tip_en: The n in the first syllable [blæŋ] is really [ŋ], because [k] follows: raise the back of the tongue against the soft palate, the same nasal sound as in 'pink' and 'thank', instead of making [n] with the tongue tip. Don't put a vowel between [b] and [l] at the start. The second syllable [kət] is very light; close the final [t] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge, without saying 'tuh'. The stress is on the first syllable.

examples.en: It's cold tonight, so I need a warm blanket.
examples.zh: 今晚很冷，所以我需要一條暖和的毯子。

examples.en: My little sister sleeps with her pink blanket.
examples.zh: 我妹妹都蓋著她的粉紅色毯子睡覺。

blanket.spelling_zh: n 在 k 前面唸 [ŋ]，不是 [n]。
blanket.spelling_en: The n before k is said [ŋ], not [n].

brother.tip_zh: 第二音節的 [ð] 學生常唸成 [d] 或 [z]，聽起來像 bruh-der。[ð] 要把舌尖輕放在上下牙齒中間，喉嚨同時震動，用手摸喉嚨應該感覺得到。接著舌頭往後捲發 [ɚ]，結尾一定要有捲舌音。第一音節 [brʌ] 的 o 唸短而放鬆的 [ʌ]，嘴巴不要張成 [ɑ]，[br] 中間也不能多加母音。
brother.tip_en: Students often say the [ð] in the second syllable as [d] or [z], so it sounds like 'bruh-der'. For [ð], rest the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower teeth while the throat vibrates — you should feel it if you touch your throat. Then pull the tongue back and curl it for [ɚ]; the ending must have the r sound. The o in the first syllable [brʌ] is a short, relaxed [ʌ] — don't open the mouth to [ɑ] — and no extra vowel goes between [b] and [r].

examples.en: My brother is two years older than me.
examples.zh: 我哥哥比我大兩歲。

examples.en: Do you have a brother or a sister?
examples.zh: 你有兄弟或姊妹嗎？

brother.spelling_zh: o 唸短的 [ʌ]，跟 mother、other 一樣，不唸 [o]。
brother.spelling_en: The o is a short [ʌ], as in 'mother' and 'other', not [o].

businessman.tip_zh: 最大的陷阱是照拼字唸成 bus-i-ness-man，多出一個音節。business 只有兩個音節 [bɪz] 和 [nəs]：u 唸 [ɪ]，s 唸有聲的 [z]，中間的 i 不發音。整個字是三個音節，重音在第一音節 [bɪz]；最後的 [mæn] 嘴巴張大，舌尖頂住牙齦把 [n] 收好。
businessman.tip_en: The biggest trap is reading the spelling as bus-i-ness-man, which adds an extra syllable. 'Business' has only two syllables, [bɪz] and [nəs]: the u is said [ɪ], the s is a voiced [z], and the i in the middle is silent. The whole word has three syllables, with the stress on the first, [bɪz]; for the last part [mæn], open the mouth wide and finish the [n] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge.

examples.en: My uncle is a businessman in Taipei.
examples.zh: 我叔叔是台北的一位商人。

examples.en: The businessman is carrying a black bag.
examples.zh: 那位商人提著一個黑色的包包。

businessman.variant_zh: 字尾 man 也常輕讀成 [mən]：[ˈbɪznəsmən]。
businessman.variant_en: The ending man is also often reduced to [mən]: [ˈbɪznəsmən].
businessman.spelling_zh: busi- 的 u 唸 [ɪ]，i 不發音，不要唸成 bus。
businessman.spelling_en: In busi-, the u is said [ɪ] and the i is silent — don't say 'bus'.

butterfly.tip_zh: 學生常照中文習慣唸成「巴特福來」：[ʌ] 張太大變成 [ɑ]、[t] 唸得太重、[ɚ] 沒有捲舌。美式唸法裡 [ʌ] 短而放鬆；中間的 [t] 夾在兩個母音之間，舌尖在牙齦輕彈一下，像很快的 d；接著捲舌唸 [ɚ]。最後 [flaɪ] 的 [f] 和 [l] 中間不加母音。重音在第一音節。
butterfly.tip_en: Students often say it the Mandarin way, like 'ba-te-fu-lai': the [ʌ] opens too wide into [ɑ], the [t] is too heavy, and the [ɚ] isn't curled. In the American pronunciation, [ʌ] is short and relaxed; the middle [t] sits between two vowels, so the tongue tip just flicks the gum ridge once, like a quick d; then curl the tongue for [ɚ]. In the last part [flaɪ], no vowel goes between [f] and [l]. The stress is on the first syllable.

examples.en: A butterfly landed on my hand!
examples.zh: 一隻蝴蝶停在我的手上！

examples.en: We saw a yellow butterfly in the garden.
examples.zh: 我們在花園裡看到一隻黃色的蝴蝶。

cake.tip_zh: [e] 在美式英語裡是會滑動的長音，從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ]，跟 make、name 的 a 一樣；學生常唸成短而平的 [ɛ]，變成 [kɛk]。字尾的 [k] 中文沒有，學生常多唸一個「克」，或乾脆不發。唸完母音後，舌根往上頂住軟顎把氣堵住，輕輕放開就好，不要再加母音。
cake.tip_en: In American English, [e] is a long gliding sound that moves from [e] toward [ɪ], like the a in 'make' and 'name'; students often say a short, flat [ɛ], making it [kɛk]. Mandarin has no final [k], so students often add an extra 'kuh' or leave it out. After the vowel, raise the back of the tongue against the soft palate to block the air and release it gently — don't add a vowel.

examples.en: Mom made a chocolate cake for my birthday.
examples.zh: 媽媽為我的生日做了一個巧克力蛋糕。

examples.en: Can I have another piece of cake, please?
examples.zh: 請問我可以再吃一塊蛋糕嗎？

camera.tip_zh: 學生常受「卡麥拉」影響，把三個音節唸得一樣重，而且都用 [ɑ]。英文重音在第一音節 [kæ]，嘴巴張大、嘴角往兩旁拉；後面的 [mərə] 要很快帶過：[mə] 輕輕一點，接著捲舌唸 [rə]，不是響亮的「拉」。
camera.tip_en: Students are often influenced by the Taiwanese slang 'ka-mai-la', saying all three syllables equally strongly and all with [ɑ]. In English the stress is on the first syllable [kæ] — open the mouth wide and pull the lip corners sideways; the following [mərə] goes by quickly: [mə] is just a light touch, then curl the tongue for [rə], not a loud 'la'.

examples.en: Dad took our picture with his new camera.
examples.zh: 爸爸用他的新相機幫我們拍照。

examples.en: Smile at the camera, everyone!
examples.zh: 大家看鏡頭，笑一個！

camera.variant_zh: 美國人也常唸成兩個音節 [ˈkæmrə]。
camera.variant_en: Americans also often say it in two syllables: [ˈkæmrə].

candle.tip_zh: 結尾的 [dḷ] 是重點：學生常唸成「肯豆」，把 [l] 變成像「歐」的母音，或在 [l] 前面多加一個母音。正確做法是舌尖發完 [d] 後留在牙齦上不動，只讓舌頭兩側放下來讓氣流出去，這就是 [ḷ]。前面的 [kæn] 是重音，[æ] 嘴巴張大，[n] 也要用舌尖頂住。
candle.tip_en: The ending [dḷ] is the key: students often say 'ken-do', turning [l] into an 'o'-like vowel, or add a vowel before the [l]. The right way: after [d], leave the tongue tip on the gum ridge without moving it, and only drop the sides of the tongue to let the air out — that is [ḷ]. The first part [kæn] is stressed; open the mouth wide for [æ], and make [n] with the tongue tip pressed up too.

examples.en: Make a wish and blow out the candle!
examples.zh: 許個願，然後吹熄蠟燭！

examples.en: Grandma put a candle on the table.
examples.zh: 奶奶在桌上放了一根蠟燭。

castle.tip_zh: castle 的 t 不發音，學生看到拼字常唸成 [kæstḷ]。正確是 [s] 直接接 [ḷ]：發完 [s] 後舌尖往上頂住牙齦，讓氣從舌頭兩側出去，中間不要加母音，也不要唸成「索」。重音在第一音節，[æ] 嘴巴張大、嘴角往兩旁拉，不要只唸成中文的「卡」。
castle.tip_en: The t in castle is silent; seeing the spelling, students often say [kæstḷ]. The right way is [s] going straight into [ḷ]: after [s], raise the tongue tip to the gum ridge and let the air out at the sides of the tongue, without adding a vowel in between and without making it 'so'. The stress is on the first syllable; open the mouth wide for [æ] and pull the lip corners sideways — not just Mandarin 'ka'.

examples.en: The princess lives in a big castle.
examples.zh: 公主住在一座大城堡裡。

examples.en: We built a sand castle at the beach.
examples.zh: 我們在海邊堆了一座沙堡。

castle.spelling_zh: t 不發音，跟 listen 的 t 一樣。
castle.spelling_en: The t is silent, like the t in 'listen'.

cat.tip_zh: [æ] 是 cat 的核心：下巴要比唸 bed 的 [ɛ] 更往下掉，嘴角往兩旁拉。學生常唸成 [ɛ]，聽起來像 ket，或用中文「卡」的母音，兩種都不夠準，也容易和 cut 混在一起。字尾的 [t] 舌尖頂住牙齦就停，不必把氣放出來，更不要多唸一個「特」。
cat.tip_en: [æ] is the heart of cat: drop the jaw lower than for the [ɛ] in 'bed', and pull the lip corners sideways. Students often say [ɛ], so it sounds like 'ket', or use the vowel of Mandarin 'ka'; neither is accurate, and both are easy to mix up with 'cut'. Stop the final [t] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge — no need to release the air, and never add an extra 'tuh'.

examples.en: Our cat sleeps on the sofa all day.
examples.zh: 我們家的貓整天都在沙發上睡覺。

examples.en: The little cat is playing with a ball.
examples.zh: 那隻小貓在玩球。

celebrate.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [sɛ]，學生常把重音放到第二音節，唸成 ce-LE-brate。正確節奏是「重、輕、中」：[sɛ] 響亮，[lə] 輕輕帶過，最後的 [bret] 是次重音，[e] 要唸完整並滑向 [ɪ]；[br] 中間不加母音，字尾 [t] 收住，不唸「特」。開頭的 c 唸 [s]。
celebrate.tip_en: The stress is on the first syllable [sɛ]; students often move it to the second, saying ce-LE-brate. The right rhythm is strong–weak–medium: [sɛ] is loud, [lə] is passed over lightly, and the last part [bret] has secondary stress — say its [e] fully, gliding toward [ɪ]; put no vowel between [b] and [r], and close the final [t] without saying 'tuh'. The c at the start is said [s].

examples.en: We celebrate Chinese New Year with our family.
examples.zh: 我們和家人一起慶祝農曆新年。

examples.en: Let's celebrate Dad's birthday with a big cake!
examples.zh: 我們用一個大蛋糕來慶祝爸爸的生日吧！

centimeter.tip_zh: 這個字有四個音節，重音在第一音節 [sɛn]，第三音節 [mi] 是次重音。學生常把每個音節都唸得一樣重，還把 [tə] 唸成響亮的「踢」。[tə] 要又短又輕；結尾 [tɚ] 的 [t] 夾在母音中間，美國人常輕彈成像 d 的音，最後一定要捲舌，不要唸到「特」就結束。
centimeter.tip_en: This word has four syllables, with the main stress on the first, [sɛn], and secondary stress on the third, [mi]. Students often say every syllable equally hard and turn [tə] into a loud 'tee'. Keep [tə] short and light. In the ending [tɚ], the [t] sits between vowels, so Americans often flick it into a d-like sound, and the word must end with a curled tongue — don't stop at 'te'.

examples.en: The ant is only one centimeter long.
examples.zh: 那隻螞蟻只有一公分長。

examples.en: Each square on this paper is one centimeter wide.
examples.zh: 這張紙上的每個格子都是一公分寬。

centimeter.spelling_zh: 美式拼法是 -meter，英式是 -metre；美式字尾唸捲舌的 [ɚ]。
centimeter.spelling_en: American spelling is -meter, British is -metre; in American English the ending is the curled [ɚ].

chair.tip_zh: 開頭的 [tʃ] 嘴唇要往前噘、稍微圓起來，舌頭前端頂住牙齦後方再放開；學生常用中文「切」的發音，嘴角往兩旁拉，聽起來太扁。後面的 [ɛr] 要先張開嘴發 [ɛ]，再把舌頭往後捲成 [r]，不要只唸到「切」就結束，也不要唸成 cheer 的 [ɪr]。
chair.tip_en: For the opening [tʃ], push the lips forward and round them slightly, press the front of the tongue just behind the gum ridge, then release; students often use Mandarin 'qie', with the lip corners pulled sideways, which sounds too flat. For the following [ɛr], first open the mouth for [ɛ], then curl the tongue back into [r] — don't stop at 'qie', and don't say the [ɪr] of 'cheer'.

examples.en: Please sit on the chair and wait.
examples.zh: 請坐在椅子上等一下。

examples.en: There is a small chair next to my desk.
examples.zh: 我的書桌旁邊有一張小椅子。

chocolate.tip_zh: 學生常照「巧克力」或拼字唸成三個音節，結尾還唸成 late 的 [let]。美式最常見的唸法只有兩個音節 [tʃɔ] 和 [klət]：中間的 o 不發音，[k] 直接接 [l]，結尾的 -late 只是輕輕的 [lət]。重音在第一音節，[tʃ] 嘴唇稍微往前噘。
chocolate.tip_en: Students often say three syllables, following Mandarin 'qiao-ke-li' or the spelling, and say the ending like the [let] of 'late'. The most common American pronunciation has only two syllables, [tʃɔ] and [klət]: the middle o is silent, [k] goes straight into [l], and the ending -late is just a light [lət]. The stress is on the first syllable; push the lips slightly forward for [tʃ].

examples.en: I drink hot chocolate on cold days.
examples.zh: 天冷的時候，我會喝熱可可。

examples.en: Can I have a piece of chocolate after lunch?
examples.zh: 午餐後我可以吃一塊巧克力嗎？

chocolate.variant_zh: 也有人唸三個音節 [ˈtʃɔkələt]，但中間的 [ə] 很輕。
chocolate.variant_en: Some people say three syllables, [ˈtʃɔkələt], but the middle [ə] is very light.
chocolate.spelling_zh: 結尾 -late 唸 [lət]，不唸 late 的 [let]。
chocolate.spelling_en: The ending -late is [lət], not the [let] of 'late'.

christmas.tip_zh: 拼字裡的 h 和 t 都不發音：ch 唸 [k]，Christ 這部分只唸 [krɪs]，不是 [kraɪst]。學生常唸成「克里斯瑪斯」，在 [k] 和 [r] 中間、[s] 和 [m] 中間多加母音。[kr] 要一口氣連著唸，[ɪ] 短而放鬆，[s] 直接接 [m]；重音在第一音節，最後的 [məs] 輕輕帶過。
christmas.tip_en: The h and the t in the spelling are both silent: ch is said [k], and the Christ part is just [krɪs], not [kraɪst]. Students often say 'ke-li-si-ma-si', adding vowels between [k] and [r] and between [s] and [m]. Say [kr] in one go, keep [ɪ] short and relaxed, and go straight from [s] to [m]; stress the first syllable and pass lightly over the last part [məs].

examples.en: We put up a Christmas tree in our living room.
examples.zh: 我們在客廳擺了一棵聖誕樹。

examples.en: Merry Christmas to you and your family!
examples.zh: 祝你和你的家人聖誕快樂！

christmas.spelling_zh: ch 唸 [k]，h 和 t 都不發音。
christmas.spelling_en: ch is said [k]; the h and the t are both silent.

circle.tip_zh: circle 兩個音節都沒有一般的 a、e、i 母音：第一音節 [sɝ] 要把舌頭往後捲、嘴唇微圓，不能唸成平平的 [sə]。第二音節 [kḷ] 中間沒有母音，[k] 之後舌尖直接頂住上排牙齒後方的牙齦發暗 L。台灣學生常把字尾唸成 [o]，聽起來像「瑟扣」。收尾時舌尖停在上牙齦，不要張嘴把聲音放開。
circle.tip_en: Neither syllable of circle has a plain a, e or i vowel: for the first syllable [sɝ], curl the tongue back and round the lips slightly — don't say a flat [sə]. The second syllable [kḷ] has no vowel in the middle: right after [k], the tongue tip presses the gum ridge behind the upper teeth for a dark L. Taiwanese learners often end the word with [o], so it sounds like 'se-ko'. At the end, keep the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge; don't open the mouth to let the sound go.

examples.en: Please sit in a circle on the floor.
examples.zh: 請在地板上圍成一個圓圈坐下。

examples.en: Draw a big circle around the right answer.
examples.zh: 在正確答案外面畫一個大圓圈。

circle.spelling_zh: 第一個 c 唸 [s]，第二個 c 唸 [k]。
circle.spelling_en: The first c sounds [s]; the second c sounds [k].

clothes.tip_zh: clothes 只有一個音節。結尾的 [ðz] 是兩個有聲子音連在一起：舌尖先輕放在上下門牙之間、喉嚨振動發 [ð]，再往後縮一點發 [z]。台灣學生常把結尾唸成無聲的 [s]，聽起來像「克漏斯」，或在中間多加母音唸成兩個音節。要一口氣唸完、喉嚨持續振動；如果 [ð] 來不及發，美國人日常也常唸 [kloz]，但結尾一定是有聲的 [z]，不是 [s]。
clothes.tip_en: Clothes has only one syllable. The ending [ðz] is two voiced consonants together: first rest the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower front teeth and voice [ð], then pull back slightly for [z]. Taiwanese learners often end it with a voiceless [s], so it sounds like 'ke-lou-s', or add a vowel in the middle and make it two syllables. Say it in one breath with the throat buzzing the whole time; if [ð] is too quick to manage, Americans also often just say [kloz] — but the ending is always a voiced [z], never [s].

examples.en: Put your clothes in the closet, please.
examples.zh: 請把你的衣服放進衣櫃裡。

examples.en: My mom bought me new clothes for school.
examples.zh: 媽媽幫我買了上學穿的新衣服。

clothes.variant_zh: 日常口語也常唸 [kloz]，th 幾乎不發音。
clothes.variant_en: In everyday speech often [kloz], with the th almost dropped.

comfortable.tip_zh: comfortable 的重音在第一音節 [ˈkʌm]，o 唸 [ʌ]，跟 come 一樣。台灣學生常照拼字唸成「康佛特伯」：把 for 唸成 [fɔr]、把重音放在 for 上，還把字尾 table 唸成桌子 table 的 [tebḷ]。其實後面三個音節都很輕：[fɚ] 輕輕捲舌，[tə] 是短短的 [ə]，最後 [bḷ] 收在暗 L。先唸熟 come，再把後面三個音節快速帶過。
comfortable.tip_en: The stress in comfortable is on the first syllable [ˈkʌm]; the o is [ʌ], as in come. Taiwanese learners often read it by spelling, like 'kang-fo-te-bo': they say for as [fɔr], put the stress on for, and say the ending table like the word table [tebḷ]. In fact the last three syllables are all light: [fɚ] with a light curl of the tongue, [tə] with a short [ə], and [bḷ] ending in a dark L. Get come right first, then run quickly through the last three syllables.

examples.en: This sofa is very comfortable.
examples.zh: 這張沙發很舒服。

examples.en: Wear comfortable shoes for the school trip.
examples.zh: 校外教學要穿舒適的鞋子。

comfortable.variant_zh: 美國人口語常唸成三音節 [ˈkʌmftɚbḷ]。
comfortable.variant_en: Americans often say it in three syllables: [ˈkʌmftɚbḷ].
comfortable.spelling_zh: 字尾 -table 不唸成單字 table 的 [tebḷ]。
comfortable.spelling_en: The ending -table is not said like the word table [tebḷ].

computer.tip_zh: computer 的重音在第二音節 [ˈpju]，第一音節 [kəm] 要又短又輕。台灣學生常把重音放在 com，而且把 com 唸成飽滿的 [kɑm]；也常把 pu 唸成 [pu]，漏掉中間的 [j]。正確的 [pju] 就是 p 後面接英文字母 U 的唸法。最後的 [tɚ] 要捲舌；美式口語中 t 夾在兩個母音之間，常變成輕快的彈舌音，聽起來像很快的 [d]。
computer.tip_en: The stress in computer is on the second syllable [ˈpju]; the first syllable [kəm] is short and light. Taiwanese learners often stress com and say it as a full [kɑm]; they also often say pu as [pu], leaving out the [j]. The correct [pju] is p followed by the name of the letter U. The final [tɚ] needs a curled tongue; in American speech the t between two vowels often becomes a quick tap that sounds like a fast [d].

examples.en: We use the computer in English class.
examples.zh: 我們在英文課上使用電腦。

examples.en: My grandpa is learning to use a computer.
examples.zh: 我爺爺正在學習用電腦。

convenient.tip_zh: convenient 的重音在第二音節 [ˈvin]，[v] 要用上排門牙輕碰下唇、喉嚨振動，不能唸成 [w] 或 [b]。台灣學生常照拼字切成四個音節，把字尾 ent 唸成飽滿的 [ɛnt]。其實 ni 只是滑過去的 [nj]，字尾 [jənt] 很輕；最後 [nt] 舌尖頂住上牙齦，t 輕輕收住，不要多加母音。第一音節 [kən] 也要輕，不要唸成 [kɑn]。
convenient.tip_en: The stress in convenient is on the second syllable [ˈvin]; for [v], touch the upper front teeth to the lower lip and voice it — don't say [w] or [b]. Taiwanese learners often split it by spelling into four syllables and say the ending ent as a full [ɛnt]. In fact ni is just a gliding [nj], and the ending [jənt] is light; for the final [nt], press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge and stop the t softly, without adding a vowel. The first syllable [kən] is light too — don't say [kɑn].

examples.en: The new MRT station is very convenient.
examples.zh: 新的捷運站很方便。

examples.en: Is Saturday morning convenient for you?
examples.zh: 星期六早上你方便嗎？

correct.tip_zh: correct 的重音在第二音節 [ˈrɛkt]，第一音節 [kə] 要輕而短。台灣學生常照拼字把 cor 唸成很重的 [kɔr]，重音放在前面，聽起來像 core 再接一段。字尾 [kt] 兩個子音連在一起，常被多加母音，或乾脆丟掉 t。練法：[k] 只用舌根擋住、不放氣，馬上接 [t]。另外 correct 和 collect 只差在 r 和 l，第二音節開頭一定要捲舌，否則會被聽成 collect。
correct.tip_en: The stress in correct is on the second syllable [ˈrɛkt]; the first syllable [kə] is light and short. Taiwanese learners often read cor by spelling as a heavy [kɔr] and stress the front, so it sounds like core plus something. The ending [kt] is two consonants together, and learners often add a vowel or drop the t. Practice: block [k] with the back of the tongue without releasing air, then go straight into [t]. Also, correct and collect differ only in r versus l, so the second syllable must start with the curled tongue, or it will be heard as collect.

examples.en: Your answer is correct. Good job!
examples.zh: 你的答案是對的，做得好！

examples.en: Please check if the spelling is correct.
examples.zh: 請檢查拼字是否正確。

correct.kk_flag: Given [kɚˈɛkt] comes from CMU ER0+EH1; Taiwan KK dictionaries write [kəˈrɛkt], with r starting the stressed syllable. Sound is close, but [kɚ·ɛkt] suggests a break before the stressed vowel. Consider [kəˈrɛkt] / sylls kə·rɛkt.

cover.tip_zh: cover 的 o 唸 [ʌ]，跟 love、come 的母音一樣，不是 [o]。台灣學生常看拼字唸成 [ˈkovɚ]，或把中間的 [v] 唸成 [b]、[w]。[v] 要讓上排門牙輕碰下唇、喉嚨振動，氣從縫隙擠出來；接著 [ɚ] 舌頭往後捲。cover 和 color [ˈkʌlɚ] 前後完全一樣，只靠中間的 [v] 分辨，所以一定要咬唇發清楚。可以先唸 love，再換成 [kʌv]，最後加上捲舌的 [ɚ]。
cover.tip_en: The o in cover is [ʌ], the same vowel as in love and come, not [o]. Taiwanese learners often read it by spelling as [ˈkovɚ], or turn the middle [v] into [b] or [w]. For [v], touch the upper front teeth to the lower lip and voice it, pushing the air through the gap; then curl the tongue back for [ɚ]. Cover and color [ˈkʌlɚ] are identical except for the middle [v] versus [l], so the lip-and-teeth [v] must be clear. Say love first, switch to [kʌv], then add the curled [ɚ].

examples.en: Please cover your mouth when you cough.
examples.zh: 咳嗽的時候請摀住嘴巴。

examples.en: I love the cover of this book.
examples.zh: 我很喜歡這本書的封面。

dangerous.tip_zh: dangerous 的第一音節 [ˈden] 母音是 [e]，跟 danger、name 一樣；台灣學生常看到 a 就唸成 [æ] 或 [ɑ]，聽起來像「蛋」。重音放在第一音節，後面 [dʒə] 和 [rəs] 都要輕。[dʒ] 嘴唇稍微往前嘟，比中文的「ㄐ」更圓；接著舌頭往後捲發 [r]，最後 [rəs] 又短又輕，s 只吐氣，不要在後面多加母音。
dangerous.tip_en: The first syllable of dangerous, [ˈden], has the vowel [e], as in danger and name; Taiwanese learners often see the a and say [æ] or [ɑ], so it sounds like 'dan'. Stress the first syllable and keep [dʒə] and [rəs] light. For [dʒ], push the lips slightly forward — rounder than Mandarin 'j'; then curl the tongue back for [r]. The final [rəs] is short and light: the s is just a breath, with no extra vowel after it.

examples.en: Running on the stairs is dangerous.
examples.zh: 在樓梯上奔跑很危險。

examples.en: It is dangerous to play near the road.
examples.zh: 在馬路旁邊玩很危險。

dangerous.spelling_zh: 開頭的 a 唸 [e]，不是 [æ]。
dangerous.spelling_en: The a at the start sounds [e], not [æ].
dangerous.kk_flag: Notation only: Taiwan KK dictionaries write [ˈdendʒərəs]; the given [ɚə] (CMU ER0 AH0) sounds the same.

daughter.tip_zh: daughter 的 augh 只唸一個母音 [ɔ]，gh 完全不發音；台灣學生常想把 gh 唸出來，或把 au 拆成兩個音。重音在第一音節 [ˈdɔ]，嘴巴張大、嘴唇微圓；第二音節 [tɚ] 要捲舌，不要唸成平平的「特」。daughter 跟 water 押韻，可以先唸 water，再把 w 換成 d。美式口語裡中間的 t 常變成輕快的彈舌音，像很快的 [d]。
daughter.tip_en: In daughter, augh is a single vowel [ɔ] and the gh is completely silent; Taiwanese learners often try to pronounce the gh or split au into two sounds. The stress is on the first syllable [ˈdɔ], with the mouth open and lips slightly rounded; the second syllable [tɚ] needs a curled tongue, not a flat 'te'. Daughter rhymes with water, so say water first and then swap w for d. In American speech the middle t often becomes a quick tap, like a fast [d].

examples.en: Mr. Lin's daughter is in my class.
examples.zh: 林先生的女兒跟我同班。

examples.en: She is the youngest daughter in her family.
examples.zh: 她是家裡最小的女兒。

daughter.spelling_en: The gh is silent; augh is just [ɔ].

day.tip_zh: day 的母音 [e] 在美式英語裡會從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ]，就像英文字母 A 的唸法。台灣學生常唸得太短太平，只剩 [dɛ]，聽起來像沒唸完。發音時嘴巴先半開，再往上收、嘴角往兩邊拉，把聲音稍微拉長，讓滑音完整出現。開頭的 [d] 舌尖輕點上牙齦就放開。day 跟 may、hey、birthday 押韻，可以連在一起練習。
day.tip_en: The vowel [e] in day glides from [e] toward [ɪ] in American English, just like the name of the letter A. Taiwanese learners often say it too short and flat, leaving only [dɛ], which sounds unfinished. Start with the mouth half open, then close it upward and pull the lip corners sideways, stretching the sound a little so the glide comes through. For the opening [d], tap the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge and release. Day rhymes with may, hey and birthday, so practice them together.

examples.en: We had a fun day at the beach.
examples.zh: 我們在海邊玩了開心的一天。

examples.en: I brush my teeth twice a day.
examples.zh: 我一天刷兩次牙。

december.tip_zh: December 的重音在第二音節 [ˈsɛm]，第一音節 [dɪ] 要短而輕。台灣學生常把重音放在第一個音節，唸成飽滿的 [di]，或把 cem 唸成 [sim]。[sɛm] 嘴巴要張開些，母音跟 men 一樣；[m] 雙唇閉起後直接接 [b]，嘴唇不要先打開加母音；最後 [bɚ] 舌頭往後捲。December 和 September、November、remember 結尾相同，可以四個字一起練節奏。
december.tip_en: The stress in December is on the second syllable [ˈsɛm]; the first syllable [dɪ] is short and light. Taiwanese learners often stress the first syllable and say a full [di], or say cem as [sim]. Open the mouth a bit more for [sɛm], the same vowel as in men; after closing the lips for [m], go straight into [b] without opening them to add a vowel; then curl the tongue back for the final [bɚ]. December ends the same way as September, November and remember, so practice the rhythm of all four together.

examples.en: My birthday is in December.
examples.zh: 我的生日在十二月。

examples.en: We have a Christmas party every December.
examples.zh: 我們每年十二月都會辦聖誕派對。

delicious.tip_zh: delicious 只有三個音節，重音在中間的 [ˈlɪ]。台灣學生常把 cious 拆開，唸成「西歐斯」多出一個音節，或把 ci 唸成 [s]。其實 ci 在這裡唸 [ʃ]，跟 she 的開頭一樣，嘴唇往前嘟，後面只接一個輕輕的 [əs]。[lɪ] 的母音是短的 [ɪ]，不要拉長成 [li]；第一音節 [dɪ] 也要輕。整個字唸成三拍：輕、重、輕。
delicious.tip_en: Delicious has only three syllables, with the stress on the middle one, [ˈlɪ]. Taiwanese learners often split cious apart into 'si-o-s', adding an extra syllable, or say ci as [s]. Here ci is [ʃ], like the start of she, with the lips pushed forward, followed only by a light [əs]. The vowel in [lɪ] is the short [ɪ], not a stretched [li]; the first syllable [dɪ] is light too. Say the word in three beats: light, strong, light.

examples.en: Grandma's dumplings are so delicious!
examples.zh: 奶奶包的水餃好好吃！

examples.en: This mango shaved ice is delicious.
examples.zh: 這碗芒果冰很好吃。

delicious.spelling_zh: ci 唸 [ʃ]，cious 只算一個音節 [ʃəs]。
delicious.spelling_en: ci sounds [ʃ]; cious is a single syllable [ʃəs].

dictionary.tip_zh: dictionary 有四個音節，重音在第一音節 [ˈdɪk]，第三音節 [nɛ] 帶次重音，中間的 [ʃə] 最輕最短。台灣學生常把重音移到後面，或把字尾 ary 唸成 [ɑrɪ]。美式唸法的字尾 [nɛrɪ]，母音和 very、strawberry 的結尾一樣，是嘴巴張開的 [ɛ]。另外 [dɪk] 的 [k] 要確實收住再接 [ʃ]，不要省掉，也不要在 [k] 後面多加母音。
dictionary.tip_en: Dictionary has four syllables: the main stress is on the first syllable [ˈdɪk], the third syllable [nɛ] has secondary stress, and the middle [ʃə] is the lightest and shortest. Taiwanese learners often move the stress toward the end, or say the ending ary as [ɑrɪ]. In the American pronunciation the ending [nɛrɪ] has the same open-mouth [ɛ] as the endings of very and strawberry. Also, finish the [k] in [dɪk] before going into [ʃ] — don't drop it, and don't add a vowel after it.

examples.en: Look up the new word in your dictionary.
examples.zh: 用你的字典查這個新單字。

examples.en: My teacher gave me an English dictionary.
examples.zh: 老師送我一本英文字典。

different.tip_zh: different 的重音在第一音節 [ˈdɪ]，後面都要輕。台灣學生常把重音放在中間，唸成 [dɪˈfɛrənt]，或把 [dɪ] 拉成長長的 [di]。中間的 fer 不是 [fɛr]，而是很輕的 [fə]，再捲舌接 [rənt]；美國人說快時常把它縮成兩個音節 [ˈdɪfrənt]。字尾 [ənt] 的 n 和 t 連在一起，舌尖頂住上牙齦收住，不要在後面多唸一個「特」。
different.tip_en: The stress in different is on the first syllable [ˈdɪ], and everything after it is light. Taiwanese learners often stress the middle, saying [dɪˈfɛrənt], or stretch [dɪ] into a long [di]. The middle fer is not [fɛr] but a light [fə], followed by a curled [rənt]; when Americans speak quickly they often shrink the word to two syllables, [ˈdɪfrənt]. In the ending [ənt], n and t go together: press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge and stop there, without adding an extra 'te' after it.

examples.en: My sister and I like different colors.
examples.zh: 我和妹妹喜歡不同的顏色。

examples.en: This game is different from that one.
examples.zh: 這個遊戲跟那個不一樣。

different.variant_en: In speech often shortened to two syllables: [ˈdɪfrənt].
different.kk_flag: Notation only: Taiwan KK dictionaries write [ˈdɪfərənt]; the given [ɚə] (CMU ER0 AH0) sounds the same.

difficult.tip_zh: difficult 的重音在第一音節 [ˈdɪ]，第二音節 [fə] 又輕又短。台灣學生常把三個音節唸得一樣重，像「低飛卡特」，或把重音移到中間。最難的是字尾 [kḷt]：l 是暗 L，舌尖頂住上牙齦、舌根同時往後抬，接著舌尖不離開就直接收 [t]，t 後面不要多加母音。可以先慢慢唸 [kḷ]，確定舌尖有碰到上牙齦，再補上 [t]。
difficult.tip_en: The stress in difficult is on the first syllable [ˈdɪ]; the second syllable [fə] is light and short. Taiwanese learners often give all three syllables equal weight, like 'di-fei-ka-te', or move the stress to the middle. The hardest part is the ending [kḷt]: the l is a dark L — press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge while lifting the back of the tongue — then, without moving the tongue tip away, finish with [t], adding no vowel after it. Say [kḷ] slowly first, making sure the tongue tip touches the gum ridge, then add the [t].

examples.en: This math problem is difficult for me.
examples.zh: 這題數學對我來說很難。

examples.en: Riding a bike is not difficult.
examples.zh: 騎腳踏車並不難。

doctor.tip_zh: doctor 的重音在第一音節 [ˈdɑk]，o 唸嘴巴張大的 [ɑ]，跟 hot、stop 的母音一樣。台灣學生常照拼字把 tor 唸成飽滿的 [tɔr]，結果兩個音節一樣重。其實第二音節很輕，只是捲舌的 [tɚ]，跟 teacher、water 的結尾相同。中間的 [kt] 也要注意：[k] 用舌根擋住後不要放出母音，直接接 [t]，不要唸成「達克特」三拍。
doctor.tip_en: The stress in doctor is on the first syllable [ˈdɑk]; the o is an open-mouth [ɑ], the same vowel as in hot and stop. Taiwanese learners often read tor by spelling as a full [tɔr], so both syllables come out equally strong. In fact the second syllable is light — just a curled [tɚ], the same ending as teacher and water. Watch the middle [kt] too: after blocking [k] with the back of the tongue, don't release a vowel; go straight into [t] instead of saying three beats like 'da-ke-te'.

examples.en: I went to see the doctor yesterday.
examples.zh: 我昨天去看醫生。

examples.en: My aunt is a doctor at a hospital.
examples.zh: 我阿姨是醫院的醫生。

driver.tip_zh: driver 開頭的 [dr] 是兩個子音連在一起，台灣學生常在中間多加母音，唸成「德賴佛」。發 [d] 時嘴唇就先微圓、舌頭準備往後捲，[d] 一放開就滑進 [r]，中間不停。重音在 [ˈdraɪ]，[aɪ] 要從 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]。第二音節 [vɚ] 的 [v] 要用上排門牙輕碰下唇、喉嚨振動，不是 [f] 或 [w]；最後捲舌收 [ɚ]。
driver.tip_en: The opening [dr] in driver is two consonants together, and Taiwanese learners often put a vowel between them, saying something like 'de-lai-fo'. While making [d], already round the lips slightly and get the tongue ready to curl back, so that as soon as [d] releases it slides into [r] without a pause. The stress is on [ˈdraɪ], where [aɪ] glides from [a] to [ɪ]. In the second syllable [vɚ], the [v] is made by touching the upper front teeth to the lower lip with voice — not [f] or [w]; finish by curling the tongue for [ɚ].

examples.en: The bus driver says good morning to us.
examples.zh: 公車司機跟我們說早安。

examples.en: My dad is a careful driver.
examples.zh: 我爸爸是個很小心的駕駛。

ear.tip_zh: ear 只有一個音節 [ɪr]，直接從母音 [ɪ] 開始，再把舌頭往後捲成 [r]。台灣學生常在前面多加一個 [j] 的滑音，結果唸成 year [jɪr]，意思變成「年」；也有人拆成兩拍，唸成「一兒」。練法：從放鬆的短 [ɪ] 直接起音，前面不要有滑音，再平順地捲舌。ear 和 hear、here 押韻，可以先唸 hear，再把 [h] 拿掉。
ear.tip_en: Ear is one syllable, [ɪr]: it starts straight on the vowel [ɪ], then the tongue curls back into [r]. Taiwanese learners often add a [j] glide in front, which turns it into year [jɪr], meaning 'year'; others split it into two beats, like 'yi-er'. Practice: start directly on a relaxed, short [ɪ] with no glide before it, then curl the tongue smoothly. Ear rhymes with hear and here, so say hear first and then drop the [h].

examples.en: The doctor looked inside my ear.
examples.zh: 醫生看了看我的耳朵裡面。

examples.en: My cat's ear is soft and pink.
examples.zh: 我家貓咪的耳朵軟軟的、粉粉的。

earth.tip_zh: earth 雖然拼字裡有 ear，但不唸 ear 的 [ɪr]，而是捲舌的 [ɝ]，跟 bird、girl 的母音一樣。台灣學生常把結尾的 [θ] 唸成 [s] 或 [f]，聽起來像「餓斯」。正確做法：先把舌頭往後捲發 [ɝ]，再把舌尖往前伸到上下門牙之間，輕輕吹氣發 [θ]，喉嚨不振動。兩個動作方向相反，可以分三步慢慢練：[ɝ]、舌尖前伸、吹出 [θ]。
earth.tip_en: Although earth is spelled with ear, it isn't the [ɪr] of ear but the curled [ɝ], the same vowel as in bird and girl. Taiwanese learners often turn the final [θ] into [s] or [f], so it sounds like 'er-s'. Do it this way: first curl the tongue back for [ɝ], then push the tongue tip forward between the upper and lower front teeth and blow gently for [θ], with no voice. The two moves go in opposite directions, so practice slowly in three steps: [ɝ], tongue tip forward, blow out [θ].

examples.en: We all live on the planet Earth.
examples.zh: 我們都住在地球這顆行星上。

examples.en: Let's keep the earth clean and green.
examples.zh: 讓我們一起讓地球保持乾淨、綠意滿滿。

earth.spelling_zh: 拼字有 ear，但唸 [ɝ]，不是 ear 的 [ɪr]。
earth.spelling_en: Spelled with ear, but said [ɝ], not the [ɪr] of ear.

earthquake.tip_zh: earthquake 由 earth 和 quake 組成，重音在前面的 [ˈɝθ]，quake 帶次重音。難在 [θ] 後面馬上接 [kw]：台灣學生常為了趕快接到 quake，就把 [θ] 省掉或唸成 [s]，變成 [ˈɝsˌkwek]。練法：舌尖伸到門牙之間吹完 [θ]，再把舌頭往後縮發 [k]，同時嘴唇嘟圓準備 [w]。quake 的 qu 唸 [kw]，母音是 [e]，跟 cake、make 押韻。
earthquake.tip_en: Earthquake is made of earth and quake; the main stress is on the front part [ˈɝθ], and quake has secondary stress. The hard part is that [kw] comes right after [θ]: Taiwanese learners, rushing to reach quake, often drop the [θ] or turn it into [s], giving [ˈɝsˌkwek]. Practice: put the tongue tip between the front teeth and finish blowing [θ], then pull the tongue back for [k] while rounding the lips for [w]. The qu in quake is [kw], and its vowel is [e], so it rhymes with cake and make.

examples.en: We learned what to do in an earthquake.
examples.zh: 我們學了地震時該怎麼做。

examples.en: Our school has an earthquake drill today.
examples.zh: 我們學校今天有地震演練。

eight.tip_zh: eight 的 eigh 只唸一個音 [e]。美式英語的 [e] 要從 [e] 滑到 [ɪ]，像英文字母 A；台灣學生常唸成短短的 [ɛ]，又在字尾 t 後面加母音，變成「欸特」兩拍。正確是一拍：嘴角往兩邊拉、把 [e] 滑完，舌尖頂住上牙齦停住發 [t]，氣可以不放出來。eight 和 date、great 押韻，可以一起練，也要和 it [ɪt]、at [æt] 分清楚。
eight.tip_en: In eight, eigh is a single sound, [e]. The American [e] glides from [e] to [ɪ], like the letter A; Taiwanese learners often say a short [ɛ] and add a vowel after the final t, making two beats like 'ei-te'. It should be one beat: pull the lip corners sideways, complete the [e] glide, and stop with the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [t] — the air doesn't have to be released. Eight rhymes with date and great, so practice them together, and keep it distinct from it [ɪt] and at [æt].

examples.en: I get up at eight every morning.
examples.zh: 我每天早上八點起床。

examples.en: There are eight students in our group.
examples.zh: 我們這組有八個學生。

eight.spelling_en: The gh is silent; eigh sounds [e].

eighteen.tip_zh: 單獨說 eighteen 時，重音在第二音節 [ˈtin]，母音是拉長的 [i]，最後一定要收 [n]。台灣學生常把重音放在前面、[n] 又收得不清楚，結果聽起來像 eighty [ˈetɪ]（八十）。分辨方法：eighteen 把 teen 唸長、唸重，舌尖頂住上牙齦把 [n] 收完整；eighty 則是重音在前、ty 很短。第一音節 [e] 也要滑完整，不要唸成短短的 [ɛ]。
eighteen.tip_en: Said on its own, eighteen has the stress on the second syllable [ˈtin], with a long [i] and a final [n] that must be pronounced. Taiwanese learners often put the stress at the front and leave the [n] unclear, so it sounds like eighty [ˈetɪ] (80). To tell them apart: in eighteen, make teen long and strong and finish the [n] fully with the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge; eighty has the stress at the front and a very short ty. The first syllable [e] also needs its full glide — not a short [ɛ].

examples.en: My cousin is eighteen years old.
examples.zh: 我表哥十八歲。

examples.en: There are eighteen books on the shelf.
examples.zh: 書架上有十八本書。

eighteen.variant_zh: 數數或後面接名詞時，重音常移到前面 [ˈeˌtin]。
eighteen.variant_en: When counting or before a noun, stress often moves forward: [ˈeˌtin].
eighteen.spelling_zh: gh 不發音，eigh 唸 [e]；t 只唸一次。
eighteen.spelling_en: The gh is silent and eigh sounds [e]; the t is said only once.

either.tip_zh: either 的 th 唸有聲的 [ð]：舌尖輕放在上下門牙之間，喉嚨振動，讓聲音從舌頭和牙齒的縫隙出來。台灣學生常把它唸成 [d] 或 [z]，聽起來像「衣得」。第一音節 [ˈi] 是重音，母音要拉長；第二音節 [ðɚ] 要捲舌，不是平平的 [ə]。美國人也常唸 [ˈaɪðɚ]，兩種都對，但中間 [ð] 的做法一樣，舌尖都要碰到牙齒。
either.tip_en: The th in either is the voiced [ð]: rest the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower front teeth and voice it, letting the sound come out through the gap between tongue and teeth. Taiwanese learners often say [d] or [z] instead, so it sounds like 'yi-de'. The first syllable [ˈi] is stressed, with a long vowel; the second syllable [ðɚ] needs a curled tongue, not a flat [ə]. Americans also often say [ˈaɪðɚ]; both are correct, but the middle [ð] is made the same way, with the tongue tip touching the teeth.

examples.en: I don't like carrots either.
examples.zh: 我也不喜歡紅蘿蔔。

examples.en: My brother can't swim, and I can't either.
examples.zh: 我哥哥不會游泳，我也不會。

elephant.tip_zh: elephant 的重音在第一音節 [ˈɛ]，嘴巴張開，母音和 egg 的開頭一樣。台灣學生常把第二音節唸成清楚的 [li] 或 [lɛ]，甚至把重音移到 le 上。其實 [lə] 和 [fənt] 都只用輕輕的 [ə]，整個字是「重、輕、輕」三拍。ph 唸 [f]，上排門牙輕碰下唇吹氣；最後的 [nt] 舌尖頂住上牙齦，n 和 t 一起收住，不要在 t 後面多加母音。
elephant.tip_en: The stress in elephant is on the first syllable [ˈɛ], with the mouth open — the same vowel as the start of egg. Taiwanese learners often say the second syllable as a clear [li] or [lɛ], or even move the stress onto le. In fact [lə] and [fənt] both use only a light [ə], so the word goes strong-light-light. The ph is [f]: touch the upper front teeth to the lower lip and blow; for the final [nt], press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge and stop n and t together, without adding a vowel after the t.

examples.en: The baby elephant is playing in the water.
examples.zh: 小象正在水裡玩。

examples.en: An elephant has a long nose and big ears.
examples.zh: 大象有長長的鼻子和大大的耳朵。

eleven.tip_zh: eleven 的重音在第二音節 [ˈlɛ]，第一音節 [ɪ] 又短又輕。台灣學生常把開頭唸成長長的 [i] 並加重，或把 [v] 唸成 [w]、[b]，變成「衣累溫」。[v] 要讓上排門牙輕碰下唇、喉嚨振動；最後的 [vən] 收在 [n]，舌尖頂住上牙齦，不要變成 [ŋ]。eleven 和 seven 的結尾一樣，可以先唸 seven，再把開頭換成 [ɪˈl]。
eleven.tip_en: The stress in eleven is on the second syllable [ˈlɛ]; the first syllable [ɪ] is short and light. Taiwanese learners often make the start a long, stressed [i], or turn [v] into [w] or [b], so it sounds like 'yi-lei-wen'. For [v], touch the upper front teeth to the lower lip and voice it; the final [vən] ends in [n] with the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge — don't let it become [ŋ]. Eleven ends the same way as seven, so say seven first, then change the start to [ɪˈl].

examples.en: There are eleven players on a soccer team.
examples.zh: 一支足球隊有十一名球員。

examples.en: My brother is eleven years old.
examples.zh: 我哥哥十一歲。

engineer.tip_zh: engineer 的主重音在最後一個音節 [nɪr]，不是開頭的 [ɛn]；學生常照中文習慣把第一拍唸最重，聽起來像「EN-ji-near」。第一音節 [ɛn] 只是次重音，中間的 [dʒə] 要輕又短。結尾 [nɪr] 的 [ɪ] 短而放鬆，接著舌尖往後捲成 r、不碰上顎，和 year、near 押韻。
engineer.tip_en: The main stress of engineer is on the last syllable [nɪr], not on the first syllable [ɛn]; students often follow their Chinese habit and say the first beat loudest, so it sounds like 'EN-ji-near'. The first syllable [ɛn] only has secondary stress, and the middle [dʒə] should be light and short. In the final [nɪr], the [ɪ] is short and relaxed, then the tongue tip curls back for r without touching the roof of the mouth; it rhymes with year and near.

examples.en: My aunt is an engineer who builds bridges.
examples.zh: 我阿姨是一位建造橋樑的工程師。

examples.en: Do you want to be an engineer someday?
examples.zh: 你以後想當工程師嗎？

engineer.kk_flag: General American puts the primary stress on the LAST syllable: [ˌɛndʒəˈnɪr]. The given KK marks two primary stresses, and stressed_syllable=1 points at the wrong syllable (should be 3).

english.tip_zh: English 只有兩個音節 [ɪŋ] 和 [glɪʃ]。常見錯誤是在 [g] 和 [l] 中間多塞一個母音，唸成三拍的「英格利序」；[g] 只是舌根輕碰一下，馬上接舌尖的 [l]。字尾 [ʃ] 嘴唇往前嘟、只送氣不出聲，後面不要再多加母音。第一個 [ɪ] 短而放鬆，不要拉成長長的 [i]。
english.tip_en: English has only two syllables, [ɪŋ] and [glɪʃ]. A common mistake is squeezing a vowel between [g] and [l], making three beats like 'ying-ge-li-shu'; [g] is only a quick touch of the back of the tongue, followed right away by [l] with the tongue tip. For the final [ʃ], push the lips forward and let out air only, no voice, and don't add a vowel after it. The first [ɪ] is short and relaxed; don't stretch it into a long [i].

examples.en: We have English class every Monday morning.
examples.zh: 我們每個星期一早上有英文課。

examples.en: My little brother can sing songs in English.
examples.zh: 我弟弟會用英文唱歌。

english.variant_zh: 也常聽到不發 [g] 的唸法 [ˈɪŋlɪʃ]。

envelope.tip_zh: envelope 重音在第一音節 [ˈɛn]，不要把結尾的 lope 唸得最重。[n] 之後馬上接 [v]：舌尖先頂住上牙齦發 [n]，再把下唇輕碰上排牙齒，發出有聲的 [v]，不要換成 [w] 或 [b]。中間的 e 只是輕輕的 [ə]，不是 [ɛ]。字尾 [p] 雙唇閉上就停，後面不要多加母音。
envelope.tip_en: Envelope is stressed on the first syllable [ˈɛn]; don't make the final lope the loudest part. [v] comes right after [n]: first press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n], then touch the lower lip lightly to the upper teeth for a voiced [v], not [w] or [b]. The middle e is only a light [ə], not [ɛ]. For the final [p], close the lips and stop; don't add a vowel after it.

examples.en: Please put the letter in the envelope.
examples.zh: 請把信放進信封裡。

examples.en: I wrote Grandma's address on the envelope.
examples.zh: 我在信封上寫了奶奶的地址。

eraser.tip_zh: eraser 重音在第二音節 [ˈre]，不在開頭；開頭的 e 唸短而輕的 [ɪ]，不要唸成長長的 [i]。[re] 的 [e] 嘴角往兩邊拉，尾巴帶一點滑向 [ɪ] 的音，就像 erase 的後半。字尾 [sɚ] 先發清楚的 [s]，再把舌尖往後捲成 [ɚ]，不要只發一個沒有捲舌的輕聲就結束。
eraser.tip_en: Eraser is stressed on the second syllable [ˈre], not at the start; the opening e is a short, light [ɪ], not a long [i]. For the [e] in [re], spread the corners of the mouth and let it glide slightly toward [ɪ] at the end, just like the second half of erase. For the final [sɚ], say a clear [s] first, then curl the tongue tip back into [ɚ]; don't end with a light sound that has no r-curl.

examples.en: Can I borrow your eraser, please?
examples.zh: 我可以借你的橡皮擦嗎？

examples.en: My new eraser smells like strawberries.
examples.zh: 我的新橡皮擦聞起來像草莓。

even.tip_zh: even 的 [v] 最容易出問題：學生常把它唸成 [b] 或 [w]，聽起來像「ibin」或「iwin」。發 [v] 時下唇輕碰上排牙齒，喉嚨同時震動。第一個 [i] 是長音，嘴角往兩邊拉；第二音節很輕。字尾 [n] 舌尖要頂住上牙齦收尾，不要滑到舌根變成 [ŋ]，否則聽起來像「eving」。
even.tip_en: The [v] in even is the usual problem: students often turn it into [b] or [w], so it sounds like 'ibin' or 'iwin'. For [v], touch the lower lip lightly to the upper teeth and voice it at the same time. The first [i] is long, with the mouth corners spread; the second syllable is light. Finish the final [n] with the tongue tip pressed on the upper gum ridge; don't slide back to [ŋ], or it sounds like 'eving'.

examples.en: My dad can even cook Japanese food.
examples.zh: 我爸爸甚至會做日本料理。

examples.en: Even my baby sister likes this song.
examples.zh: 連我的小妹妹都喜歡這首歌。

even.kk_flag: Minor: General American and Taiwan KK dictionaries usually give [ˈivən] with a reduced [ə] in the second syllable; [ˈivɪn] is CMU's IH0 and acceptable, but [ˈivən] is the usual reference form.

evening.tip_zh: evening 只有兩個音節 [iv] 和 [nɪŋ]。學生常照拼字唸成三拍的 e-ve-ning，在 [v] 和 [n] 中間多出一個母音。正確做法是下唇碰上齒發完 [v] 後不放鬆，直接把舌尖頂上牙齦接 [n]。字尾 [ŋ] 用舌根抵住軟顎，讓聲音從鼻子出來，和 morning 的結尾一樣。
evening.tip_en: Evening has only two syllables, [iv] and [nɪŋ]. Students often follow the spelling and say three beats, e-ve-ning, adding a vowel between [v] and [n]. Instead, after the lower lip touches the upper teeth for [v], don't relax; move the tongue tip straight to the upper gum ridge for [n]. For the final [ŋ], press the back of the tongue against the soft palate and let the sound come out through the nose, the same ending as morning.

examples.en: We take a walk in the evening.
examples.zh: 我們傍晚會去散步。

examples.en: Good evening, Mr. Lin! How are you?
examples.zh: 林先生，晚安！您好嗎？

evening.spelling_zh: 中間的 e 不發音，整個字只有兩拍。
evening.spelling_en: The middle e is silent; the word has only two beats.

ever.tip_zh: ever 開頭是 [ɛ]，跟 egg 的開頭一樣，嘴巴半開、嘴唇放鬆；不要把嘴唇圓起來唸成 over 的 [o]，兩個字意思完全不同。中間的 [v] 是下唇碰上排牙齒的有聲音，不能換成 [b]。字尾 [ɚ] 舌尖往後捲、不碰上顎，和 never 的結尾相同，整個字只有兩拍。
ever.tip_en: Ever starts with [ɛ], the same as the start of egg: mouth half open, lips relaxed. Don't round the lips into the [o] of over; the two words mean completely different things. The middle [v] is a voiced sound made with the lower lip on the upper teeth and can't be swapped for [b]. For the final [ɚ], curl the tongue tip back without touching the roof of the mouth, the same ending as never; the whole word has just two beats.

examples.en: Have you ever seen a rainbow?
examples.zh: 你曾經看過彩虹嗎？

examples.en: This is the best pizza ever!
examples.zh: 這是史上最好吃的披薩！

every.tip_zh: every 拼字有三個母音字母，學生常一個一個唸成 e-ve-ry，中間唸成清楚的 [ɛ]。其實中間的 e 幾乎不發音，[v] 之後直接捲舌接 [rɪ]，只有 ev-ry 兩拍，跟 everyone 的開頭一樣。重音永遠在第一音節 [ɛ]，[v] 要用下唇碰上排牙齒並發出聲音。
every.tip_en: Every has three vowel letters, and students often say them one by one, e-ve-ry, with a clear [ɛ] in the middle. In fact the middle e is almost silent: after [v] the tongue curls straight into [rɪ], giving just two beats, ev-ry, the same as the start of everyone. The stress is always on the first syllable [ɛ], and [v] is made with the lower lip on the upper teeth, with voice.

examples.en: I brush my teeth every morning.
examples.zh: 我每天早上刷牙。

examples.en: Every student has a new book.
examples.zh: 每個學生都有一本新書。

every.variant_zh: 慢慢唸時也有人唸成三個音節 [ˈɛvərɪ]。
every.variant_en: In slow, careful speech some people say three syllables: [ˈɛvərɪ].
every.kk_flag: Acceptable as a careful three-syllable form, but everyday General American is two syllables [ˈɛvrɪ] (the CMU variant, and the form most dictionaries give); consider making [ˈɛvrɪ] the headline KK.

everyone.tip_zh: everyone 結尾的 one 唸 [wʌn]，跟 won 同音；學生常唸成 [wɑn]，或把嘴唇圓起來唸成 [won]。[ʌ] 嘴巴微開、舌頭放平放鬆，跟 fun、run 的母音一樣。前面的 every 只唸兩拍 [ɛvrɪ]，[v] 和 [r] 緊緊相連，中間不加母音。整個字三拍，重音在 [ɛv]，最後的 [n] 用舌尖頂住上牙齦。
everyone.tip_en: The one at the end of everyone is said [wʌn], the same as won; students often say [wɑn], or round the lips into [won]. For [ʌ], open the mouth slightly and keep the tongue flat and relaxed, the same vowel as fun and run. The every part is only two beats, [ɛvrɪ], with [v] and [r] tightly joined and no vowel between them. The whole word has three beats, stressed on [ɛv], and the final [n] is made with the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge.

examples.en: Everyone in my class likes music.
examples.zh: 我們班每個人都喜歡音樂。

examples.en: Good morning, everyone! Let's start our lesson.
examples.zh: 大家早安！我們開始上課吧。

everyone.spelling_zh: one 的部分開頭有 [w] 音，但拼字裡沒有 w。
everyone.spelling_en: The one part starts with a [w] sound, but has no w.

everything.tip_zh: everything 的難點在第三音節 [θɪŋ]：學生常把 [θ] 唸成 [s]，變成「every-sing」，聽起來像在說唱歌。從前面的 [rɪ] 接過來時，把舌尖往前伸，輕輕放在上下牙齒之間吹氣，喉嚨不要震動。字尾 [ŋ] 舌根抵住軟顎，跟單獨唸 thing 時一樣。前面的 every 只有兩拍 [ɛvrɪ]，重音在最前面。
everything.tip_en: The hard part of everything is the third syllable [θɪŋ]: students often turn [θ] into [s], making 'every-sing', which sounds like singing. Coming from the [rɪ] before it, push the tongue tip forward and rest it lightly between the upper and lower teeth, then blow air without voicing. For the final [ŋ], press the back of the tongue against the soft palate, just as when saying thing on its own. The every part has only two beats, [ɛvrɪ], with the stress at the very front.

examples.en: Mom packed everything for our trip.
examples.zh: 媽媽把旅行要帶的東西都打包好了。

examples.en: Everything in this store is so cute!
examples.zh: 這家店裡的每樣東西都好可愛！

example.tip_zh: example 的 x 在這裡唸有聲的 [gz]，不是 [ks]；學生常照 ex 的拼法唸成 [ɛks]，開頭又重又硬。其實開頭 [ɪg] 輕而短，重音落在第二音節 [zæm]，[æ] 要把下巴往下拉、嘴角往兩邊開。結尾 [pḷ] 雙唇閉一下就把舌尖抬到上牙齦，發出暗 L，不要多加一個母音變成另一拍。
example.tip_en: In example, the x is the voiced [gz], not [ks]; students often follow the ex spelling and say [ɛks], making the start loud and hard. In fact the opening [ɪg] is light and short, and the stress falls on the second syllable [zæm]; for [æ], drop the jaw and spread the mouth corners. For the final [pḷ], close the lips briefly, then lift the tongue tip to the upper gum ridge for a dark L; don't add a vowel that makes an extra beat.

examples.en: Can you give me an example?
examples.zh: 你可以舉個例子嗎？

examples.en: Our teacher wrote an example on the board.
examples.zh: 老師在黑板上寫了一個例子。

excellent.tip_zh: excellent 重音在第一音節 [ɛk]，學生常受 excel 影響，把重音移到第二音節，唸成「ex-CEL-lent」。後面兩拍 [sə] 和 [lənt] 都要輕，母音弱化成 [ə]。結尾 [nt] 是子音串：舌尖頂住上牙齦發 [n]，舌頭不動直接放出 [t]，不要多加母音，也不要把 [t] 吞掉只剩 [n]。
excellent.tip_en: Excellent is stressed on the first syllable [ɛk]; students are often influenced by excel and move the stress to the second syllable, saying 'ex-CEL-lent'. The last two beats, [sə] and [lənt], are both light, with the vowels reduced to [ə]. The final [nt] is a consonant cluster: press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n], then release [t] without moving the tongue; don't add a vowel, and don't swallow the [t] so that only [n] is left.

examples.en: Excellent work! You got every answer right.
examples.zh: 做得太好了！你每一題都答對了。

examples.en: The food at this restaurant is excellent.
examples.zh: 這家餐廳的食物非常好吃。

excellent.spelling_zh: xc 合起來只唸 [ks]，c 不再多發一個音。
excellent.spelling_en: xc together make just [ks]; the c adds no sound.

excited.tip_zh: excited 重音在第二音節 [saɪ]，[aɪ] 要從張大的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]，唸得飽滿。最常見的問題是把結尾 [təd] 吞掉，聽起來像 excite，或和 exciting 分不清楚。[t] 後面的 -ed 要多唸一拍 [əd]，舌尖碰上牙齦兩次。開頭 [ɪk] 輕而短，不要唸成又重又長的 [ɛk]。
excited.tip_en: Excited is stressed on the second syllable [saɪ]; glide [aɪ] fully from a wide-open [a] to [ɪ]. The most common problem is swallowing the ending [təd], so it sounds like excite or gets mixed up with exciting. After [t], the -ed adds a whole extra beat, [əd], with the tongue tip touching the upper gum ridge twice. The opening [ɪk] is light and short; don't make it a heavy, long [ɛk].

examples.en: I am so excited about the school trip!
examples.zh: 我對校外教學超級興奮！

examples.en: The kids were excited to see the snow.
examples.zh: 孩子們看到雪都很興奮。

exciting.tip_zh: exciting 和 excited 只差在結尾：這裡是 [tɪŋ]，[ɪ] 短而放鬆，最後的 [ŋ] 用舌根往上抵住軟顎，讓聲音從鼻子出來。學生常把 [ŋ] 收成舌尖的 [n]，或把 [ɪ] 拉長成 [i]。重音放在中間的 [saɪ]，[s] 要清楚吹氣；前面的 [ɪk] 輕輕帶過，整個字三拍。
exciting.tip_en: Exciting differs from excited only in the ending: here it is [tɪŋ], with a short, relaxed [ɪ], and the final [ŋ] made by pressing the back of the tongue up against the soft palate so the sound comes out through the nose. Students often end with a tongue-tip [n] instead of [ŋ], or stretch [ɪ] into [i]. Put the stress on the middle [saɪ] with a clear, hissing [s]; pass lightly over the opening [ɪk]. The whole word has three beats.

examples.en: The soccer game was really exciting!
examples.zh: 那場足球賽真的很刺激！

examples.en: We read an exciting story about a dragon.
examples.zh: 我們讀了一個關於龍的精彩故事。

exercise.tip_zh: exercise 結尾的 se 唸有聲的 [z]，學生常唸成無聲的 [s]，聽起來像「exer-sice」。發 [z] 時舌頭位置和 [s] 一樣，但喉嚨要震動，像蜜蜂的嗡嗡聲。中間的 [sɚ] 要捲舌，不要唸成平平的 [sɛ]。重音在第一音節 [ɛk]，最後的 [saɪz] 是次重音，[aɪ] 要滑完整再接 [z]。
exercise.tip_en: The se at the end of exercise is a voiced [z]; students often say a voiceless [s], so it sounds like 'exer-sice'. For [z], the tongue is in the same place as for [s], but the throat vibrates, like a bee buzzing. The middle [sɚ] needs the r-curl; don't flatten it into [sɛ]. The stress is on the first syllable [ɛk], and the last syllable [saɪz] has secondary stress; glide [aɪ] all the way before adding [z].

examples.en: We exercise in the park every morning.
examples.zh: 我們每天早上在公園運動。

examples.en: Exercise is good for your body.
examples.zh: 運動對身體很好。

exercise.spelling_zh: 字尾 -ise 的 s 唸 [z]，e 不發音。
exercise.spelling_en: In the final -ise, the s is [z] and the e is silent.

expensive.tip_zh: expensive 重音在第二音節 [spɛn]。[s] 後面的 [p] 不送氣，聽起來比較接近 [b]，不必用力噴氣。結尾 [sɪv] 是最容易漏掉的地方：學生常把 [v] 唸成 [f]，或乾脆不發，只剩「expensi」。發 [v] 時下唇貼住上排牙齒，同時讓喉嚨震動，收尾後不要再加母音。
expensive.tip_en: Expensive is stressed on the second syllable [spɛn]. The [p] after [s] is unaspirated, so it sounds closer to [b]; there is no need to push out a puff of air. The ending [sɪv] is the part most often lost: students often say [v] as [f], or drop it so only 'expensi' is left. For [v], rest the lower lip against the upper teeth and voice it at the same time, and don't add a vowel after it.

examples.en: This toy is too expensive for me.
examples.zh: 這個玩具對我來說太貴了。

examples.en: Wow, your new bike looks expensive!
examples.zh: 哇，你的新腳踏車看起來好貴！

experience.tip_zh: experience 有四拍，重音在第二音節 [spɪ]。學生常把它唸成 ex-pe-ri-ence，第二音節用了 [ɛ]，或把重音放到第三音節。[spɪ] 的 [ɪ] 後面緊接捲舌的 [r]，舌尖往後捲、不碰上顎。最後的 [əns] 很輕：母音弱化成 [ə]，[n] 頂住上牙齦後直接吹出 [s]，不要再加母音多出一拍。
experience.tip_en: Experience has four beats, stressed on the second syllable [spɪ]. Students often say ex-pe-ri-ence with an [ɛ] in the second syllable, or put the stress on the third syllable. The [ɪ] in [spɪ] is followed closely by an r-curled [r]: curl the tongue tip back without touching the roof of the mouth. The final [əns] is light: the vowel reduces to [ə], and after [n] on the upper gum ridge you blow straight out into [s]; don't add a vowel that makes an extra beat.

examples.en: Camping was a fun experience for our family.
examples.zh: 露營對我們家來說是一次很好玩的經驗。

examples.en: Do you have any experience with pets?
examples.zh: 你有養寵物的經驗嗎？

eye.tip_zh: eye 只唸一個雙母音 [aɪ]，和 I 同音。學生常像中文第四聲那樣一下子往下掉，[ɪ] 還沒滑到就收掉了。發音時下巴先張大發 [a]，再慢慢合上滑到 [ɪ]，聲音平穩或微微下降。說複數 eyes 時結尾是有聲的 [z]，喉嚨要震動，不要唸成 [s]。可以用 my、bye 練習同一個母音。
eye.tip_en: Eye is a single diphthong [aɪ], the same sound as I. Students often drop it sharply like a Mandarin fourth tone and cut it off before reaching [ɪ]. Open the jaw wide for [a] first, then close it gradually as you glide to [ɪ], keeping the pitch level or falling only slightly. In the plural eyes, the ending is a voiced [z] with throat vibration, not [s]. Practice the same vowel with my and bye.

examples.en: I have something in my eye.
examples.zh: 我的眼睛裡有東西。

examples.en: The cat has one blue eye and one green eye.
examples.zh: 那隻貓有一隻藍眼睛和一隻綠眼睛。

eye.spelling_zh: 拼字有三個字母，但整個字只唸 [aɪ]，跟 I 同音。
eye.spelling_en: Three letters, but the word is just [aɪ], like I.

factory.tip_zh: factory 的 -tory 不要照 story 唸成 [tɔrɪ]；這裡是很輕的 [tərɪ]，[tə] 輕輕帶過、再捲舌接 [rɪ]，口語中幾乎只剩 [trɪ]。第一音節 [fæk] 才是重點，[æ] 要把下巴往下拉、嘴角往兩邊開，不要縮成 [ɛ]。[k] 和 [t] 之間不要插入母音，舌根頂一下就直接換成舌尖。
factory.tip_en: Don't say the -tory of factory like story, [tɔrɪ]; here it is a very light [tərɪ]: pass over [tə] quickly, then curl the tongue for [rɪ], and in speech it is almost just [trɪ]. The first syllable [fæk] is the important one: for [æ], drop the jaw and spread the mouth corners; don't shrink it to [ɛ]. Don't insert a vowel between [k] and [t]: the back of the tongue touches once, then switch straight to the tongue tip.

examples.en: My uncle works at a toy factory.
examples.zh: 我叔叔在玩具工廠上班。

examples.en: We visited a chocolate factory on our trip.
examples.zh: 我們旅行時參觀了一間巧克力工廠。

factory.variant_en: In fast speech often two syllables: [ˈfæktrɪ].

family.tip_zh: family 的第一音節 [fæ] 嘴巴要張大、下巴往下拉；學生常唸成比較扁的 [ɛ]，聽起來像「femily」。中間的 [mə] 非常輕，美國人說快時幾乎跳過，變成兩拍 [ˈfæmlɪ]；不要把三個音節唸得一樣重。最後的 [lɪ] 舌尖輕碰上牙齦，[ɪ] 短而放鬆。
family.tip_en: For the first syllable [fæ] of family, open the mouth wide and drop the jaw; students often say a flatter [ɛ], so it sounds like 'femily'. The middle [mə] is very light, and Americans speaking fast almost skip it, making two beats, [ˈfæmlɪ]; don't give all three syllables equal weight. For the final [lɪ], touch the tongue tip lightly to the upper gum ridge and keep [ɪ] short and relaxed.

examples.en: There are five people in my family.
examples.zh: 我家有五個人。

examples.en: My family eats dinner together every night.
examples.zh: 我們家每天晚上一起吃晚餐。

family.variant_en: In everyday speech often two syllables: [ˈfæmlɪ].

father.tip_zh: father 中間的 th 是有聲的 [ð]，學生常唸成 [d] 或 [z]，聽起來像「fader」或「fazer」。發 [ð] 時舌尖輕輕夾在上下牙齒之間，喉嚨同時震動。前面的 [ɑ] 嘴巴張大、舌頭放低，從這個開口的位置把舌尖往前送到牙齒之間，再往後捲成字尾的 [ɚ]。
father.tip_en: The th in the middle of father is the voiced [ð]; students often say [d] or [z], so it sounds like 'fader' or 'fazer'. For [ð], hold the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower teeth and voice it at the same time. The [ɑ] before it has the mouth wide open and the tongue low; from that open position, bring the tongue tip forward between the teeth, then curl it back for the final [ɚ].

examples.en: My father reads stories to me at night.
examples.zh: 我爸爸晚上會唸故事給我聽。

examples.en: My father and I play basketball on Sundays.
examples.zh: 我和爸爸星期天會一起打籃球。

favorite.tip_zh: favorite 結尾的 -ite 不唸 [aɪt]，跟 kite、bite 不一樣，這裡是短短的 [ɪt]。學生常照拼字把結尾唸成像 write 的音。重音在第一音節 [fe]，[e] 嘴角往兩邊拉。中間的 [və] 先用下唇碰上齒發 [v]，輕輕帶過再捲舌接 [rɪt]，說快時常合在一起。字尾 [t] 舌尖點一下就停，不要加母音。
favorite.tip_en: The -ite at the end of favorite is not [aɪt] as in kite and bite; here it is a short [ɪt]. Students often follow the spelling and make the ending sound like write. The stress is on the first syllable [fe], with the mouth corners spread for [e]. For the middle [və], touch the lower lip to the upper teeth for [v], pass over it lightly, then curl the tongue for [rɪt]; in fast speech they often blend together. For the final [t], tap the tongue tip once and stop; don't add a vowel.

examples.en: Blue is my favorite color.
examples.zh: 藍色是我最喜歡的顏色。

examples.en: What is your favorite animal?
examples.zh: 你最喜歡的動物是什麼？

favorite.spelling_zh: 結尾 -ite 唸 [ɪt]，不是 kite 的 [aɪt]。
favorite.spelling_en: The final -ite is [ɪt], not the [aɪt] of kite.

february.tip_zh: February 重音在第一音節 [fɛb]。學生常被拼字裡的兩個 r 困住，硬要把第一個 r 捲出來，結果舌頭打結。常見的美式唸法第一個 r 不發音，b 後面接輕輕的 [jə]，再接 [wɛrɪ]，這一段有次重音。結尾的 [ɛrɪ] 跟 very 的 [ɛrɪ] 一樣，January 的結尾也是這個音，可以一起練。
