february.tip_en: February is stressed on the first syllable [fɛb]. Students often get stuck on the two r's in the spelling and force out the first r, which ties the tongue in a knot. In the common American pronunciation the first r is silent: after b comes a light [jə], then [wɛrɪ], which has secondary stress. The ending [ɛrɪ] is the same as the [ɛrɪ] of very, and January ends with the same sound, so practice them together.

examples.en: My birthday is in February.
examples.zh: 我的生日在二月。

examples.en: February is the shortest month of the year.
examples.zh: 二月是一年中最短的月份。

february.variant_zh: 也可以把第一個 r 唸出來：[ˈfɛbruˌɛrɪ]。
february.variant_en: Also correct with the first r: [ˈfɛbruˌɛrɪ].
february.spelling_zh: 常見的美式唸法中，第一個 r 不發音。
february.spelling_en: In the common American pronunciation, the first r is silent.

festival.tip_zh: festival 重音在第一音節 [fɛs]，後面兩拍都很輕。學生常在 [s] 和 [t] 中間加母音，唸成「fe-si-ti-val」，或把重音放到中間。[st] 要連在一起：先發 [s]，舌尖直接頂上牙齦放出 [t]。結尾 [vḷ] 下唇碰上齒發 [v]，接著把舌尖抬到上牙齦發暗 L，不要收成 [vo]。
festival.tip_en: Festival is stressed on the first syllable [fɛs], and the two beats after it are light. Students often add a vowel between [s] and [t], saying 'fe-si-ti-val', or put the stress in the middle. [st] must stay together: say [s], then press the tongue tip straight onto the upper gum ridge to release [t]. For the final [vḷ], touch the lower lip to the upper teeth for [v], then lift the tongue tip to the upper gum ridge for a dark L; don't end it as [vo].

examples.en: The Dragon Boat Festival is in early summer.
examples.zh: 端午節在初夏。

examples.en: Our school has a music festival every spring.
examples.zh: 我們學校每年春天都有音樂節。

fever.tip_zh: fever 的兩個子音 [f] 和 [v] 嘴型完全一樣，都是下唇輕碰上排牙齒，差別只在 [v] 要讓喉嚨震動。學生常把 [v] 也唸成無聲的 [f]，或換成 [w]。練習時把手放在喉嚨上：發 [f] 不會震，發 [v] 會震。開頭的 [i] 是長音、嘴角往兩邊拉，結尾的 [ɚ] 舌尖往後捲。
fever.tip_en: The two consonants in fever, [f] and [v], use exactly the same mouth shape: the lower lip lightly touching the upper teeth. The only difference is that [v] makes the throat vibrate. Students often say [v] as a voiceless [f] too, or swap it for [w]. To practice, put a hand on your throat: [f] doesn't buzz, [v] does. The [i] at the start is long, with the mouth corners spread, and for the final [ɚ] the tongue tip curls back.

examples.en: I stayed home because I had a fever.
examples.zh: 我因為發燒待在家裡。

examples.en: Drink lots of water when you have a fever.
examples.zh: 發燒的時候要多喝水。

fill.tip_zh: fill 的 [ɪ] 短而放鬆，常被拉長成 [i]，聽起來就變成 feel（感覺）。嘴角不要往兩旁拉，下巴稍微放低，母音快速帶過。字尾 [l] 也常被吞掉，只剩下母音；收尾時舌尖要確實貼住上排牙齒後面的牙齦，停一下再結束，可以跟 hill、will 一起練。
fill.tip_en: The [ɪ] in fill is short and relaxed, but it often gets stretched into [i], which makes it sound like feel. Don't pull the corners of your mouth back; drop the jaw slightly and say the vowel quickly. The final [l] is also often swallowed, leaving only the vowel; to finish, press the tongue tip firmly on the gum ridge behind the upper teeth and hold it a moment. You can practice it together with hill and will.

examples.en: Please fill your water bottle before class.
examples.zh: 請在上課前把你的水壺裝滿。

examples.en: Can you fill the cup with milk?
examples.zh: 你可以把杯子裝滿牛奶嗎？

finally.tip_zh: finally 的重音在第一音節 [faɪ]，中間的 [nə] 要又輕又短。常見錯誤是照 final 的拼字把中間的 a 唸成響亮的 [æ]，或三個音節一樣重。先把 [faɪ] 唸得長而有力，從 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]，接著 [nə] 一帶而過，最後 [lɪ] 舌尖碰一下上牙齦就放開，輕輕收尾。
finally.tip_en: The stress in finally is on the first syllable [faɪ]; the middle [nə] must be light and short. A common mistake is following the spelling of final and saying the middle a as a loud [æ], or giving all three syllables equal weight. Make [faɪ] long and strong, gliding from [a] to [ɪ], then pass quickly over [nə], and finish lightly with [lɪ]: the tongue tip touches the gum ridge once and lets go.

examples.en: We finally got home after a long drive.
examples.zh: 開了很久的車，我們終於到家了。

examples.en: Finally, it's time for lunch!
examples.zh: 終於到午餐時間了！

finally.spelling_zh: 兩個 l 只唸一個 [l]
finally.spelling_en: The double l is said as a single [l].

finger.tip_zh: finger 第一音節結尾是後鼻音 [ŋ]，舌根抬起碰軟顎，不是舌尖的 [n]。接著舌根放開就是 [g]，所以 [ŋ] 和 [g] 兩個都要有；學生常照 singer 的方式把 [g] 省掉。字尾 [ɚ] 要把舌頭往後捲，不要唸成平平的「格」。
finger.tip_en: The first syllable of finger ends in the back nasal [ŋ]: the back of the tongue rises to touch the soft palate — it is not a tongue-tip [n]. Releasing the back of the tongue then gives [g], so both [ŋ] and [g] must be heard; students often drop the [g] the way singer does. For the final [ɚ], curl the tongue back — don't say a flat 「格」 (ge).

examples.en: Point your finger at the right picture.
examples.zh: 用手指指出正確的圖片。

examples.en: She has a pretty ring on her finger.
examples.zh: 她的手指上戴著一枚漂亮的戒指。

finger.spelling_zh: ng 在這裡唸 [ŋg]，g 要發出來（singer 的 g 則不發）
finger.spelling_en: Here ng is [ŋg] — the g is pronounced (unlike in singer).

fisherman.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [fɪ]。中間的 [ʃɚ] 常被唸成 [s]，或用中文的「西」代替；英文 [ʃ] 要把嘴唇嘟起往前推，舌面靠近上顎但不碰到，送出氣流，然後馬上捲舌接 [ɚ]。最後的 [mæn] 是次重音，比第一音節輕，不要三個音節一樣重。
fisherman.tip_en: The stress is on the first syllable [fɪ]. The middle [ʃɚ] is often said with [s], or replaced by the Mandarin 「西」 (xi) sound; English [ʃ] needs the lips rounded and pushed forward, with the tongue close to the roof of the mouth but not touching it, pushing air out — then curl the tongue straight into [ɚ]. The final [mæn] has secondary stress and is lighter than the first syllable; don't give all three syllables equal weight.

examples.en: The fisherman caught a big fish this morning.
examples.zh: 那位漁夫今天早上抓到一條大魚。

examples.en: My uncle is a fisherman in Keelung.
examples.zh: 我叔叔是基隆的漁夫。

fisherman.variant_en: The last syllable is often reduced to [mən]: [ˈfɪʃɚmən].

food.tip_zh: food 的 [u] 是長音，嘴唇要圓、往前嘟緊，比 good、foot 的 [ʊ] 更緊更長。字尾 [d] 常被省略，聽起來只剩 foo，或多加一個母音變成兩個音節。舌尖頂住上牙齦，喉嚨保持震動，輕輕放開就結束；如果把 [d] 換成 [l]，就成了 fool（傻瓜）。
food.tip_en: The [u] in food is long: round the lips and push them forward tightly — tighter and longer than the [ʊ] in good or foot. The final [d] is often dropped, leaving just "foo", or an extra vowel is added, making two syllables. Press the tongue tip on the gum ridge, keep the voice on, and release lightly to finish; if [d] turns into [l], it becomes fool.

examples.en: What's your favorite food?
examples.zh: 你最喜歡的食物是什麼？

examples.en: Let's buy some food for the picnic.
examples.zh: 我們去買一些野餐要吃的食物吧。

foreign.tip_zh: foreign 的第二音節是很輕的 [rən]，不是 rain 的 [en]；常見錯誤是看到 eign 就唸成「雷恩」，或把 g 也唸出來。重音在第一音節 [fɔ]，嘴唇微圓發 [ɔ]，再捲舌接到 [r]，後面的 [ən] 輕而短，舌尖頂住上牙齦收在 [n]。
foreign.tip_en: The second syllable of foreign is a very light [rən], not the [en] of rain; a common mistake is to see eign and say it like 「雷恩」 (lei-en, like rain), or to pronounce the g as well. Stress the first syllable [fɔ]: round the lips slightly for [ɔ], then curl the tongue into [r]; the [ən] after it is light and short, ending with the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n].

examples.en: Do you speak any foreign languages?
examples.zh: 你會說任何外語嗎？

examples.en: We met a foreign student at the museum.
examples.zh: 我們在博物館遇到一位外國學生。

foreign.variant_zh: 也常唸成 [ˈfɑrən]，第一個母音嘴巴較開
foreign.variant_en: Also often [ˈfɑrən], with a more open first vowel.
foreign.spelling_zh: eign 的 g 不發音，結尾只唸 [ən]
foreign.spelling_en: The g in eign is silent; the ending is just [ən].

foreigner.tip_zh: foreigner 有兩個捲舌音：第二音節開頭的 [r] 和字尾的 [ɚ]。學生常把 eign 唸成 rain 的 [en]，重音也跟著跑到第二音節。重音只放在第一音節 [fɔ]，中間 [rə] 又輕又快；最後 [nɚ] 舌尖先碰上牙齦發 [n]，再把舌頭往後捲，不要唸成平平的「那」。
foreigner.tip_en: foreigner has two r-sounds: the [r] that opens the second syllable and the final [ɚ]. Students often say eign as the [en] of rain, and the stress moves to the second syllable along with it. Put the stress only on the first syllable [fɔ] and keep the middle [rə] light and quick; for the last [nɚ], touch the tongue tip to the gum ridge for [n], then curl the tongue back — don't say a flat 「那」 (na).

examples.en: A friendly foreigner asked us for directions.
examples.zh: 一位友善的外國人向我們問路。

examples.en: The foreigner at the night market loved the bubble tea.
examples.zh: 夜市裡的那位外國人很喜歡珍珠奶茶。

foreigner.variant_zh: 說快時中間的 [ə] 常省略：[ˈfɔrnɚ] 或 [ˈfɑrnɚ]
foreigner.variant_en: In fast speech the middle [ə] often drops: [ˈfɔrnɚ] or [ˈfɑrnɚ].
foreigner.spelling_zh: 跟 foreign 一樣，g 不發音
foreigner.spelling_en: As in foreign, the g is silent.

full.tip_zh: full 的 [ʊ] 短而放鬆，嘴唇只微微圓起；如果嘟緊拉長成 [u]，就變成 fool（傻瓜）。也別把嘴角拉開唸成 [ɪ]，那會變成 fill。字尾暗 L 常被吞掉只剩「福」，收尾時舌尖要碰到上牙齦，同時舌根稍微往後抬，聲音才會厚實。
full.tip_en: The [ʊ] in full is short and relaxed, with the lips only slightly rounded; if you tighten and stretch it into [u], it becomes fool. Don't spread the lips into [ɪ] either — that turns it into fill. The final dark L is often swallowed, leaving just 「福」 (fu); at the end, touch the tongue tip to the gum ridge while raising the back of the tongue slightly, so the sound comes out thick and full.

examples.en: My backpack is full of books.
examples.zh: 我的背包裝滿了書。

examples.en: I'm full, thank you!
examples.zh: 我吃飽了，謝謝！

girl.tip_zh: girl 只有一個音節，但 [ɝ] 和 [l] 緊緊連在一起。常見錯誤是捲舌後把 l 吞掉，或在 [ɝ] 和 [l] 之間多加一個母音，變成兩個音節。先把舌頭往後捲，發 her、bird 裡的 [ɝ]，保持捲舌，再把舌尖往上抬碰上牙齦收在 [l]，中間不停頓。
girl.tip_en: girl has only one syllable, but [ɝ] and [l] are packed tightly together. Common mistakes are dropping the l after the curled vowel, or adding an extra vowel between [ɝ] and [l], which makes two syllables. First curl the tongue back for the [ɝ] in her and bird, hold the curl, then lift the tongue tip to the gum ridge to finish on [l], with no pause in between.

examples.en: The girl next to me likes drawing.
examples.zh: 坐我旁邊的女孩喜歡畫畫。

examples.en: That girl is my best friend.
examples.zh: 那個女孩是我最好的朋友。

give.tip_zh: give 的 [ɪ] 要短，不要拉成 [i]。字尾 [v] 是有聲音：上排牙齒輕碰下唇，喉嚨要震動。常見錯誤是唸成無聲的 [f]，聽起來像 gif，或在後面多加母音變成「給夫」。把手放在喉嚨上，確認 [v] 有震動，然後直接停住，不加尾音。
give.tip_en: The [ɪ] in give is short — don't stretch it into [i]. The final [v] is voiced: the upper teeth lightly touch the lower lip and the throat vibrates. A common mistake is saying a voiceless [f], so it sounds like gif, or adding a vowel at the end, like 「給夫」 (gei-fu). Put your hand on your throat to check that [v] vibrates, then stop right there with no extra sound.

examples.en: Can you give me a pencil, please?
examples.zh: 可以給我一支鉛筆嗎？

examples.en: I want to give my mom a card.
examples.zh: 我想送媽媽一張卡片。

give.spelling_zh: 字尾 e 不發音，i 唸短的 [ɪ]，不是 five 的 [aɪ]
give.spelling_en: The final e is silent, and i is a short [ɪ], not the [aɪ] of five.

glasses.tip_zh: 開頭 [gl] 是兩個子音連在一起，不要在 g 和 l 之間加母音唸成「格拉」。[æ] 要把嘴巴張大、嘴角往兩旁拉，像 cat 的母音，不是中文的「啊」。字尾 [əz] 的 [z] 是有聲音，喉嚨要震動，學生常唸成無聲的 [s]；想像蜜蜂嗡嗡叫，讓聲音持續震動。
glasses.tip_en: The opening [gl] is two consonants together — don't put a vowel between g and l, as in 「格拉」 (ge-la). For [æ], open the mouth wide and pull the corners back, like the vowel in cat, not Mandarin 「啊」 (a). The [z] in the final [əz] is voiced and the throat must vibrate; students often say a voiceless [s] — imagine a buzzing bee and keep the sound vibrating.

examples.en: My dad wears glasses when he reads.
examples.zh: 我爸爸看書時會戴眼鏡。

examples.en: I can't find my glasses anywhere!
examples.zh: 我到處都找不到我的眼鏡！

grandfather.tip_zh: grandfather 的重點在第三音節開頭的 [ð]：[fɑ] 後面不是 [d] 或 [z]，要把舌尖輕輕放在上下排牙齒之間，喉嚨震動往外送氣。開頭 [gr] 之間不要加母音，[æ] 嘴巴張大。重音在 grand，father 部分稍輕，最後的 [ɚ] 捲舌收尾。
grandfather.tip_en: The key to grandfather is the [ð] that starts the third syllable: what follows [fɑ] is not [d] or [z] — rest the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower teeth and push air out with the throat vibrating. Don't put a vowel between [g] and [r] at the start, and open the mouth wide for [æ]. The stress is on grand; the father part is a little lighter, ending with a curled [ɚ].

examples.en: My grandfather likes to go fishing on Sundays.
examples.zh: 我爺爺星期天喜歡去釣魚。

examples.en: Grandfather told us a funny story.
examples.zh: 爺爺跟我們講了一個好笑的故事。

grandfather.variant_zh: 口語中 d 常省略：[ˈgrænˌfɑðɚ]
grandfather.variant_en: In everyday speech the d is often dropped: [ˈgrænˌfɑðɚ].

grandmother.tip_zh: mother 部分的 o 唸 [ʌ]，像 cup 的母音，嘴巴輕鬆半開，不要照拼字唸成 [o]。接著的 [ð] 舌尖放在牙齒之間並帶震動，不能換成 [z] 或 [d]。前面 grand 的 [nd] 碰到 [m] 時，d 幾乎不爆開，舌尖一碰到牙齦就閉上嘴唇發 [m]。
grandmother.tip_en: The o in the mother part is [ʌ], like the vowel in cup — mouth relaxed and half open; don't follow the spelling and say [o]. The [ð] after it has the tongue tip between the teeth, with voicing; it can't become [z] or [d]. Where the [nd] of grand meets [m], the d is barely released: the tongue tip just touches the gum ridge and the lips close for [m].

examples.en: My grandmother makes dumplings every New Year.
examples.zh: 我奶奶每年過年都會包水餃。

examples.en: We visit my grandmother every weekend.
examples.zh: 我們每個週末都去看奶奶。

grandmother.spelling_zh: mother 的 o 唸 [ʌ]，不唸 [o]
grandmother.spelling_en: The o in mother is [ʌ], not [o].

guitar.tip_zh: guitar 的重音在第二音節 [tɑr]，學生常受中文「吉他」影響，把重音放在第一音節。第一音節 [gɪ] 要短而輕；第二音節拉長、音調提高，[t] 用力送氣，[ɑ] 嘴巴張大，最後舌頭往後捲收在 [r]，不要停在「他」就結束。
guitar.tip_en: The stress in guitar is on the second syllable [tɑr]; influenced by the Mandarin 「吉他」 (jita), students often stress the first syllable. Keep the first syllable [gɪ] short and light; make the second syllable longer and higher, with a strongly aspirated [t] and a wide-open [ɑ], and finish by curling the tongue back into [r] — don't stop at 「他」 (ta).

examples.en: My brother is learning to play the guitar.
examples.zh: 我哥哥正在學彈吉他。

examples.en: She played the guitar at the school concert.
examples.zh: 她在學校音樂會上彈吉他。

guitar.spelling_zh: gu 的 u 不發音，只唸 [g]
guitar.spelling_en: The u in gu is silent; it's just [g].

hair.tip_zh: hair 的母音是 [ɛ]，嘴巴半開，像 bed 的母音，再把舌頭往後捲到 [r]。常見錯誤是嘴巴太扁，唸得像 here、hear 的 [ɪr]，意思就變了。開頭 [h] 只是輕輕吐氣，不要像中文「喝」那樣在舌根摩擦。可以用同韻的 chair、bear 一起練。
hair.tip_en: The vowel in hair is [ɛ]: mouth half open, like the vowel in bed, then curl the tongue back into [r]. A common mistake is keeping the mouth too flat, so it sounds like the [ɪr] of here or hear, which changes the meaning. The opening [h] is just a light breath — don't make friction at the back of the tongue like Mandarin 「喝」 (he). Practice with the rhyming words chair and bear.

examples.en: My sister has long black hair.
examples.zh: 我姊姊有一頭黑色長髮。

examples.en: Don't forget to brush your hair.
examples.zh: 別忘了梳頭髮。

half.tip_zh: half 的 l 不發音，學生常照拼字唸出 [l]。母音是 [æ]，下巴往下、嘴巴張大，跟 laugh 同韻。字尾 [f] 是無聲音，上排牙齒輕碰下唇吹氣就好，喉嚨不震動，否則會變成 have；也不要多加母音唸成「哈夫」。
half.tip_en: The l in half is silent, but students often follow the spelling and say [l]. The vowel is [æ]: drop the jaw and open the mouth wide; it rhymes with laugh. The final [f] is voiceless: the upper teeth lightly touch the lower lip and you just blow air, with no throat vibration — otherwise it becomes have. Don't add a vowel either, as in 「哈夫」 (ha-fu).

examples.en: I ate half of the pizza.
examples.zh: 我吃了半個披薩。

examples.en: Let's meet at half past three.
examples.zh: 我們三點半見吧。

half.spelling_zh: alf 的 l 不發音，只唸 [æf]
half.spelling_en: The l in -alf is silent; say only [æf].

halloween.tip_zh: Halloween 的重音在最後一個音節 [win]，不在開頭。常見錯誤是受 hello 影響唸成「哈囉溫」，三個音一樣重或重音在前。開頭 [hæ] 嘴巴張大，中間 [lə] 很輕很短，最後 [win] 拉長、音調提高，[i] 是長音，收尾時舌尖頂住上牙齦發 [n]。
halloween.tip_en: The stress in Halloween is on the last syllable [win], not at the start. A common mistake, influenced by hello, is saying 「哈囉溫」 (ha-luo-wen) with all three syllables equal or the stress up front. Open the mouth wide for [hæ], keep the middle [lə] very light and short, and make [win] long and higher in pitch; the [i] is long, and you finish with the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n].

examples.en: We wear costumes on Halloween.
examples.zh: 我們在萬聖節穿上變裝服。

examples.en: What are you going to be for Halloween?
examples.zh: 萬聖節你要裝扮成什麼？

hamburger.tip_zh: hamburger 重音在第一音節 [hæm]，[æ] 嘴巴張大。學生常被中文「漢堡」帶著把 [m] 唸成舌尖的 [n]；其實發 [m] 時雙唇閉上，直接接 [b] 最順。後面兩個音節 [bɚ]、[gɚ] 都是輕的捲舌音，子音一出來舌頭就要捲，不要唸成「堡」或「格」。
hamburger.tip_en: The stress in hamburger is on the first syllable [hæm], with a wide-open [æ]. Led by the Mandarin 「漢堡」 (hanbao), students often turn [m] into a tongue-tip [n]; in fact, the lips close for [m], which leads most smoothly into [b]. The next two syllables, [bɚ] and [gɚ], are both light r-colored sounds — curl the tongue as soon as each consonant comes out, and don't say 「堡」 (bao) or 「格」 (ge).

examples.en: I'd like a hamburger and a glass of juice.
examples.zh: 我想要一個漢堡和一杯果汁。

examples.en: This hamburger is too big for me!
examples.zh: 這個漢堡對我來說太大了！

happen.tip_zh: happen 的第一音節 [hæ] 要重、嘴巴張大；第二音節 [pən] 很輕，[p] 送氣後 [ə] 幾乎一帶而過。常見錯誤是兩個音節一樣重，把 en 唸得很清楚。結尾 [n] 要用舌尖頂住上牙齦，不要變成後鼻音 [ŋ]。拼字有兩個 p，但只唸一個 [p]。
happen.tip_en: The first syllable of happen, [hæ], is strong with the mouth wide open; the second syllable [pən] is very light — after the aspirated [p], the [ə] passes almost instantly. A common mistake is giving both syllables equal weight and saying en very clearly. The final [n] uses the tongue tip on the gum ridge — don't let it become the back nasal [ŋ]. The spelling has two p's, but you say only one [p].

examples.en: What will happen next in the story?
examples.zh: 故事接下來會發生什麼事？

examples.en: Good things happen when we work together.
examples.zh: 我們一起努力時，好事就會發生。

happy.tip_zh: happy 的 [æ] 是關鍵：學生常唸成「黑皮」，嘴巴開得不夠，母音變成 [ɛ]。下巴要往下放、嘴角往兩旁拉，像要說 cat。重音在第一音節，第二音節 [pɪ] 短而輕，[p] 送出一點氣。可以先慢慢唸 [hæ]，確認嘴巴張開，再快速接上 [pɪ]。
happy.tip_en: The key in happy is [æ]: students often say 「黑皮」 (hei-pi), with the mouth not open enough, so the vowel becomes [ɛ]. Drop the jaw and pull the corners of the mouth back, as if saying cat. The stress is on the first syllable; the second syllable [pɪ] is short and light, with a little puff of air on [p]. Say [hæ] slowly first to check that the mouth is open, then add [pɪ] quickly.

examples.en: I'm so happy to see you!
examples.zh: 看到你我好開心！

examples.en: We sang Happy Birthday to Grandma.
examples.zh: 我們唱生日快樂歌給奶奶聽。

hat.tip_zh: hat 的 [æ] 舌頭在前、嘴角往兩旁拉開：嘴巴太扁會聽成 [ɛ]；舌頭往後縮又會變成 hot（熱的）的 [ɑ]。字尾 [t] 輕輕停住就好，舌尖頂住上牙齦，美式口語常常不爆出氣，但絕不能多加母音變成兩個音節。可以跟同韻的 cat、bat 一起練。
hat.tip_en: For the [æ] in hat, keep the tongue forward and spread the corners of the mouth: too flat a mouth and it's heard as [ɛ]; pull the tongue back and it becomes the [ɑ] of hot. Just stop gently on the final [t] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge — in casual American speech it often isn't released with a puff of air — but never add a vowel and make it two syllables. Practice with the rhyming words cat and bat.

examples.en: Wear a hat when it's sunny.
examples.zh: 天氣晴朗時要戴帽子。

examples.en: I like your red hat!
examples.zh: 我喜歡你的紅色帽子！

have.tip_zh: have 的字尾 [v] 有聲：上排牙齒輕碰下唇，喉嚨震動。學生常唸成無聲的 [f]，聽起來像 half，或乾脆把尾音省掉。比較 half [hæf] 和 have [hæv]：母音相同，差別在最後喉嚨有沒有震動，而且 have 的 [æ] 會稍微拉長一點。
have.tip_en: The final [v] in have is voiced: the upper teeth lightly touch the lower lip and the throat vibrates. Students often say a voiceless [f], so it sounds like half, or simply drop the ending. Compare half [hæf] and have [hæv]: the vowel is the same; the difference is whether the throat vibrates at the end, and the [æ] in have is held a little longer.

examples.en: I have two brothers and one sister.
examples.zh: 我有兩個哥哥和一個妹妹。

examples.en: Do you have a pencil?
examples.zh: 你有鉛筆嗎？

have.spelling_zh: 字尾 e 不發音，a 唸 [æ]，不像 save 唸 [e]
have.spelling_en: The final e is silent, and a is [æ], not [e] as in save.

hill.tip_zh: hill 跟 heel（腳跟）只差在母音：hill 的 [ɪ] 短而鬆，舌頭稍低；heel 的 [i] 長而緊、嘴角拉開。母音後面接暗 L 時，會有一點往 [l] 滑過去的感覺，但最後舌尖一定要碰到上牙齦，不能只剩「嘿喔」。可以拿同韻的 will、still 一起練。
hill.tip_en: hill and heel differ only in the vowel: the [ɪ] in hill is short and loose, with the tongue a bit lower; the [i] in heel is long and tense, with the lips spread. Before the dark L, the vowel glides a little toward [l], but at the end the tongue tip must touch the gum ridge — don't leave only 「嘿喔」 (hei-o). Practice with the rhyming words will and still.

examples.en: We walked up the hill to see the sunset.
examples.zh: 我們走上山丘看夕陽。

examples.en: Our school is on a small hill.
examples.zh: 我們學校在一座小山丘上。

history.tip_zh: history 重音在第一音節 [hɪs]，後面都要輕。學生常三個音節一樣重，或把 to 唸成清楚的 [o]。中間的 [tə] 只是很輕的音，美國人說快時常幾乎消失，變成 [ˈhɪstrɪ]。[s] 後面的 [t] 不送氣，兩個子音之間也不要加母音。
history.tip_en: The stress in history is on the first syllable [hɪs]; everything after it is light. Students often give all three syllables equal weight, or say to with a clear [o]. The middle [tə] is just a very light sound, and in fast American speech it often almost disappears, giving [ˈhɪstrɪ]. The [t] after [s] is not aspirated, and no vowel goes between those two consonants either.

examples.en: History is my favorite subject.
examples.zh: 歷史是我最喜歡的科目。

examples.en: We learned about Taiwan's history today.
examples.zh: 我們今天學了台灣的歷史。

history.variant_en: In everyday speech it often shrinks to two syllables: [ˈhɪstrɪ].
history.kk_flag: Taiwan KK dictionaries write [ˈhɪstərɪ] (or [ˈhɪstrɪ]); [ˈhɪstɚɪ] looks like a CMU conversion artifact (ER0 + IY0) and forces the odd syllable split hɪs·tɚ·ɪ. Suggest [ˈhɪstərɪ] → hɪs·tə·rɪ.

holiday.tip_zh: holiday 的 o 唸 [ɑ]，嘴巴張大，像 hot 的母音，不是 [o]。重音在第一音節，中間 [lə] 輕輕帶過；最後 [de] 有次重音，要唸出跟 day 一樣從 [e] 往上滑的感覺，不要唸成短促平板的「得」。三個音節的輕重是：重、輕、中。
holiday.tip_en: The o in holiday is [ɑ]: open the mouth wide, as for the vowel in hot — not [o]. The stress is on the first syllable and the middle [lə] passes lightly; the final [de] has secondary stress and should have the same upward glide from [e] as day — don't make it a short, flat 「得」 (de). The three syllables go: strong, light, medium.

examples.en: What do you want to do this holiday?
examples.zh: 這次放假你想做什麼？

examples.en: Christmas is my favorite holiday.
examples.zh: 聖誕節是我最喜歡的節日。

holiday.spelling_zh: o 唸 [ɑ]，不像 holy 唸 [o]
holiday.spelling_en: The o is [ɑ], not the [o] of holy.

honest.tip_zh: honest 開頭的 h 不發音，第一個音就是嘴巴張大的 [ɑ]，所以要說 an honest boy，不是 a honest boy。常見錯誤是照拼字發出 [h]，或把字尾 [st] 唸成「斯特」，多加一個母音。第二音節的 [ə] 輕輕帶過，[s] 之後舌尖頂住上齒齦發 [t]，收在那裡就好。
honest.tip_en: The h at the start of honest is silent; the first sound is the open-mouthed [ɑ], so we say an honest boy, not a honest boy. A common mistake is pronouncing the [h] because of the spelling, or turning the final [st] into something like 'si-te' with an extra vowel. Pass lightly over the [ə] in the second syllable; after [s], press the tongue tip to the gum ridge for [t] and simply stop there.

examples.en: Tom is an honest boy.
examples.zh: 湯姆是個誠實的男孩。

examples.en: Please give me an honest answer.
examples.zh: 請給我一個誠實的回答。

honest.spelling_zh: 開頭的 h 不發音，和 hour 一樣。
honest.spelling_en: The h at the start is silent, just like in hour.

hospital.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [ˈhɑs]，母音是嘴巴張大的 [ɑ]，學生常看到字母 o 就唸成圓唇的 [o]。字尾 -tal 也不要唸成 [tæl] 或加上清楚的母音；[tḷ] 是舌尖頂住上齒齦發完 [t] 後不放開，直接讓舌根往後抬，發出暗 L。中間的 [pɪ] 短而輕。
hospital.tip_en: The stress is on the first syllable [ˈhɑs], and its vowel is the open-mouthed [ɑ]; learners often see the letter o and say a rounded [o]. Don't say the ending -tal as [tæl] or with a clear vowel either: for [tḷ], press the tongue tip to the gum ridge for [t], keep it there, and raise the back of the tongue to make a dark L. The middle [pɪ] is short and light.

examples.en: My mom works at the hospital as a nurse.
examples.zh: 我媽媽在醫院當護士。

examples.en: The hospital is across from our school.
examples.zh: 醫院就在我們學校對面。

hospital.kk_flag: The secondary stress mark on the 2nd syllable (ˌspɪ) is a CMU artifact; standard GA/KK is [ˈhɑspɪtḷ] with no secondary stress.

hot.tip_zh: hot 的母音是 [ɑ]：下巴往下、嘴巴張大，舌頭放低，像看醫生時說「啊」。學生常照字母 o 唸成圓唇的 [o]，聽起來不像 hot。也要跟 hat 的 [æ] 分開：[æ] 嘴角往兩邊拉，[ɑ] 嘴巴上下拉開、嘴角不往旁邊拉。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上齒齦就停，不要加母音。
hot.tip_en: The vowel in hot is [ɑ]: drop the jaw, open the mouth wide and keep the tongue low, like saying 'ah' for the doctor. Learners often follow the letter o and use a rounded [o], which doesn't sound like hot. Also keep it apart from the [æ] in hat: for [æ] the corners of the mouth spread sideways; for [ɑ] the mouth opens up and down without spreading. For the final [t], touch the tongue tip to the gum ridge and stop; don't add a vowel.

examples.en: It is very hot today.
examples.zh: 今天非常熱。

examples.en: Be careful, the soup is hot!
examples.zh: 小心，湯很燙！

hotel.tip_zh: hotel 的重音在第二音節 [ˈtɛl]，學生常把重音放在第一音節，唸成 HO-tel。第一音節 [ho] 短而輕，第二音節拉長、音調升高。後半其實就是 tell：先說 tell，再在前面輕輕加上 [ho]。字尾的 l 是暗 L，舌尖頂上齒齦、舌根抬起，不要省略或唸成「喔」。
hotel.tip_en: The stress in hotel is on the second syllable [ˈtɛl]; learners often stress the first syllable and say HO-tel. The first syllable [ho] is short and light; the second is longer and higher in pitch. The second half is really just tell: say tell first, then add a light [ho] in front. The final l is a dark L: tongue tip on the gum ridge, back of the tongue raised; don't drop it or turn it into an 'o' sound.

examples.en: We stayed at a hotel near the beach.
examples.zh: 我們住在海灘附近的一家旅館。

examples.en: Our hotel room has a big window.
examples.zh: 我們的飯店房間有一扇大窗戶。

hour.tip_zh: hour 的 h 不發音，唸起來跟 our 一樣，所以要說 an hour。學生常照拼字在開頭加上 [h]，或只唸出 [aʊ] 就停，漏掉最後的 [r]。做法：嘴巴先張大發 [a]，再收圓滑到 [ʊ]，最後舌尖往後捲、不碰到任何地方，讓聲音帶出捲舌的 [r]。
hour.tip_en: The h in hour is silent; it sounds the same as our, so we say an hour. Learners often add an [h] because of the spelling, or stop at [aʊ] and leave out the final [r]. How to do it: open the mouth wide for [a], round it as you glide to [ʊ], and finally curl the tongue tip back without touching anything to add the r-colored [r].

examples.en: I read for an hour every night.
examples.zh: 我每天晚上閱讀一個小時。

examples.en: The bus comes once an hour.
examples.zh: 公車每小時來一班。

hour.spelling_zh: h 不發音，hour 與 our 同音。
hour.spelling_en: The h is silent; hour sounds the same as our.

however.tip_zh: however 的重音在第二音節 [ˈɛ]，不是 how。學生常把 how 和 ever 拆開、中間停頓，或把 how 唸得最重。要連成一口氣：[haʊ] 的尾音自然滑進 [ɛ]。[v] 要上齒輕咬下唇並震動，不要唸成 [w] 或 [b]；結尾 [vɚ] 捲舌。練習時先說 ever，再在前面輕輕加上 how。
however.tip_en: The stress in however is on the second syllable [ˈɛ], not on how. Learners often split how and ever with a pause, or say how the loudest. Say it in one breath: the end of [haʊ] glides naturally into [ɛ]. For [v], lightly bite the lower lip with the upper teeth and let it buzz; don't turn it into [w] or [b]; the ending [vɚ] is r-colored. To practice, say ever first, then add a light how in front.

examples.en: I like apples. However, I don't like apple juice.
examples.zh: 我喜歡蘋果，不過我不喜歡蘋果汁。

examples.en: It was raining. However, we still played outside.
examples.zh: 當時在下雨，然而我們還是在外面玩。

i.tip_zh: I 是雙母音 [aɪ]：從嘴巴張大的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]，嘴角最後微微往兩邊拉。學生常把它唸成中文「愛」的第四聲，又短又重、音調往下掉，句子聽起來像在生氣。在句子裡 I 通常輕而平，重音放在後面的動詞：說 I like it 時，把 like 唸重，I 輕輕帶過，但滑音仍要做完整。
i.tip_en: I is the diphthong [aɪ]: glide from an open-mouthed [a] to [ɪ], with the corners of the mouth spreading slightly at the end. Learners often say it like the Mandarin 'ài' with a fourth tone—short, heavy and falling—which makes the sentence sound angry. In a sentence, I is usually light and level, and the stress goes on the verb after it: in I like it, stress like and pass lightly over I, but still finish the glide.

examples.en: I have a little brother.
examples.zh: 我有一個弟弟。

examples.en: I like to draw pictures after school.
examples.zh: 我喜歡放學後畫畫。

idea.tip_zh: idea 有三個音節 [aɪ]·[di]·[ə]，重音在第二音節 [ˈdi]。學生常把重音放在開頭的 [aɪ]，或漏掉最後的 [ə]，只唸兩個音節，聽起來像 I-dee。[di] 要拉長、音調拉高；結尾的 [ə] 嘴巴放鬆微張，輕輕發出來就好，不要捲舌加 [r]。
idea.tip_en: idea has three syllables, [aɪ]·[di]·[ə], with the stress on the second, [ˈdi]. Learners often stress the opening [aɪ], or drop the final [ə] and say only two syllables, which sounds like I-dee. Make [di] long and high in pitch; for the final [ə], relax the mouth, open it slightly and say it softly—don't curl the tongue and add an [r].

examples.en: That is a great idea!
examples.zh: 那是個很棒的主意！

examples.en: Who has an idea for the class party?
examples.zh: 誰對班級派對有想法？

important.tip_zh: important 的重音在第二音節 [ˈpɔr]，[ɪm] 短而輕，[pɔr] 要捲舌。學生常把字尾 -tant 唸成「疼特」，多加一個完整的母音。[tṇt] 的做法：舌尖頂住上齒齦發 [t] 後不要放開，讓氣直接從鼻子出來變成 [ṇ]，最後再輕輕放出 [t]。整個字只有 [pɔr] 是重的。
important.tip_en: The stress in important is on the second syllable [ˈpɔr]; [ɪm] is short and light, and [pɔr] needs the curled r. Learners often say the ending -tant like 'teng-te', adding a full vowel. For [tṇt]: press the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [t] and don't let go; let the air go straight out through the nose to make [ṇ], and finally release a light [t]. Only [pɔr] is strong in the whole word.

examples.en: Breakfast is an important meal.
examples.zh: 早餐是很重要的一餐。

examples.en: It is important to wash your hands.
examples.zh: 洗手是很重要的。

interested.tip_zh: interested 的重音在第一音節 [ˈɪn]。學生最常把重音移到中間的 rest，唸成 in-ter-REST-ed。美式口語常唸成三個音節，ter 的母音省掉，[t] 直接連 [r]，就像 tree 開頭的 [tr]。字尾 -ed 唸 [ɪd]，因為前面是 [t]，要多一個小音節，不能只加 [d]，也別和 interesting 搞混。
interested.tip_en: The stress in interested is on the first syllable [ˈɪn]. The most common mistake is moving it to rest in the middle: in-ter-REST-ed. In everyday American speech it is often three syllables: the vowel of ter drops out and [t] joins straight onto [r], like the [tr] at the start of tree. The ending -ed is [ɪd] because it follows [t], so it adds a small syllable—don't just add [d]—and don't mix it up with interesting.

examples.en: I am interested in dinosaurs.
examples.zh: 我對恐龍很有興趣。

examples.en: Are you interested in joining the art club?
examples.zh: 你有興趣參加美術社嗎？

interested.variant_zh: 也常聽到四個音節的 [ˈɪntɚɪstɪd]，兩種都正確。
interested.variant_en: A four-syllable [ˈɪntɚɪstɪd] is also common; both are correct.

interesting.tip_zh: interesting 只有開頭的 [ˈɪn] 是重的，後面全部輕輕帶過，不要把 rest 唸得最響。字尾 [ɪŋ] 是舌根往上頂住軟顎的鼻音，嘴巴保持微開，學生常把它唸成舌尖的 [n]，或在最後多發一個 [g]。可以想 sing 的結尾。分清 interesting 的 [ɪŋ] 和 interested 的 [ɪd]，意思才不會說錯。
interesting.tip_en: Only the opening [ˈɪn] in interesting is strong; everything after it is light—don't make rest the loudest part. The final [ɪŋ] is a nasal made by raising the back of the tongue against the soft palate with the mouth slightly open; learners often turn it into a tongue-tip [n] or add an extra [g] at the end. Think of the end of sing. Keep the [ɪŋ] of interesting apart from the [ɪd] of interested, so the meaning comes out right.

examples.en: This book is really interesting.
examples.zh: 這本書真的很有趣。

examples.en: We watched an interesting video about whales.
examples.zh: 我們看了一部關於鯨魚的有趣影片。

interesting.variant_zh: 也常聽到四個音節的 [ˈɪntɚɪstɪŋ]，兩種都對。
interesting.variant_en: A four-syllable [ˈɪntɚɪstɪŋ] is also common; both are fine.

internet.tip_zh: Internet 的重音在第一音節 [ˈɪn]，最後的 [nɛt] 只是次重音，不要唸得比開頭還重。中間的 [tɚ] 要捲舌：舌尖往後捲、不碰上顎，學生常唸成平平的「特」。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上齒齦就停，不要加母音變成「內特」。net 跟 get、pet 押韻，可以先練這幾個字。
internet.tip_en: The stress in Internet is on the first syllable [ˈɪn]; the final [nɛt] has only secondary stress, so don't make it stronger than the start. The middle [tɚ] needs the curled r: curl the tongue tip back without touching the roof of the mouth; learners often say a flat 'te'. For the final [t], put the tongue tip on the gum ridge and stop—don't add a vowel to make it 'nei-te'. net rhymes with get and pet, so practice those first.

examples.en: We use the Internet to do homework.
examples.zh: 我們用網路寫功課。

examples.en: My grandpa learned to use the Internet.
examples.zh: 我爺爺學會了用網路。

interview.tip_zh: view 的開頭是 [vj]：上齒輕咬下唇發出震動的 [v]，再滑進 [ju]。學生常把 [v] 唸成 [w]，或漏掉 [j]，只剩 [vu]。[vju] 跟 few 的 [fju] 嘴型一樣，只是喉嚨要震動。重音在第一音節 [ˈɪn]，中間 [tɚ] 捲舌，view 是次重音，不要唸成 in-ter-VIEW。
interview.tip_en: view starts with [vj]: lightly bite the lower lip with the upper teeth for a buzzing [v], then glide into [ju]. Learners often turn [v] into [w], or drop the [j] and say only [vu]. [vju] uses the same mouth shape as the [fju] in few—just add voice in the throat. The stress is on the first syllable [ˈɪn], the middle [tɚ] is r-colored, and view takes only secondary stress—don't say in-ter-VIEW.

examples.en: My sister has a job interview today.
examples.zh: 我姊姊今天有工作面試。

examples.en: Our class will interview the school principal.
examples.zh: 我們班要訪問校長。

island.tip_zh: island 的 s 不發音，唸 [ˈaɪlənd]。學生常照拼字唸成 [ˈaɪslənd]，多出一個 [s]。前半其實就是 I [aɪ]，後面接一個很輕的 [lənd]，[ə] 短到幾乎聽不見。字尾 [nd] 兩個子音都要有：舌尖頂上齒齦發 [n]，再輕輕放出 [d]，不要加母音變成「的」。
island.tip_en: The s in island is silent: say [ˈaɪlənd]. Learners often follow the spelling and say [ˈaɪslənd] with an extra [s]. The first half is just I [aɪ], followed by a very light [lənd] whose [ə] is so short it is almost silent. Both consonants of the final [nd] are needed: tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n], then a light release for [d]—don't add a vowel like 'de'.

examples.en: Taiwan is a beautiful island.
examples.zh: 台灣是一座美麗的島嶼。

examples.en: We took a boat to a small island.
examples.zh: 我們搭船去一座小島。

island.spelling_zh: s 不發音，is- 唸起來跟 I 一樣。
island.spelling_en: The s is silent; is- sounds just like I.

january.tip_zh: January 的重音在第一音節 [ˈdʒæn]，[æ] 要下巴往下、嘴角往兩邊拉，學生常唸成比較窄的 [ɛ]。[dʒ] 嘴唇微微往前嘟，舌尖放在上齒齦後面。後半 -uary 是 [ju] 加上 [ˌɛrɪ]，[ɛrɪ] 跟 very 的後半一樣，帶次重音，不要把主要重音移到最後。
january.tip_en: The stress in January is on the first syllable [ˈdʒæn]; for [æ], drop the jaw and spread the corners of the mouth—learners often use the narrower [ɛ]. For [dʒ], push the lips slightly forward with the tongue tip just behind the gum ridge. The second half -uary is [ju] plus [ˌɛrɪ]; [ɛrɪ] is the same as the end of very and carries secondary stress—don't move the main stress to the end.

examples.en: My birthday is in January.
examples.zh: 我的生日在一月。

examples.en: It is very cold in January.
examples.zh: 一月非常冷。

kilogram.tip_zh: kilogram 的重音在第一音節 [ˈkɪ]，母音是短而放鬆的 [ɪ]，不是長的 [i]。第二音節的 o 弱化成 [ə]，學生常照拼字唸成清楚的 [o]，聽起來每個音節一樣重。最後的 gram 帶次重音，[æ] 嘴巴張大、嘴角往兩邊拉，結尾 [m] 雙唇要閉上。gram 跟 ham 押韻。
kilogram.tip_en: The stress in kilogram is on the first syllable [ˈkɪ], with a short, relaxed [ɪ], not a long [i]. The o in the second syllable weakens to [ə]; learners often follow the spelling and say a clear [o], so every syllable sounds equally strong. The final gram has secondary stress: open the mouth wide for [æ] with the corners spread, and close the lips for the final [m]. gram rhymes with ham.

examples.en: I bought a kilogram of apples.
examples.zh: 我買了一公斤蘋果。

examples.en: The bag of rice weighs one kilogram.
examples.zh: 這袋米重一公斤。

knife.tip_zh: knife 的 k 不發音，開頭直接是 [n]，學生常照拼字在前面多加一個 [k]。中間 [aɪ] 從張大嘴滑到 [ɪ]。最重要的是字尾 [f]：上齒輕碰下唇吹氣，不要省略，也不要加母音變成「夫」。字尾發不清楚，就容易和只差最後一個音的 nice、night、nine 混淆。knife 跟 wife、life 押韻。
knife.tip_en: The k in knife is silent; it starts straight with [n]—learners often add a [k] in front because of the spelling. The middle [aɪ] glides from an open mouth to [ɪ]. The most important part is the final [f]: touch the upper teeth to the lower lip and blow—don't drop it, and don't add a vowel to make it 'fu'. If the ending is unclear, it is easily confused with nice, night and nine, which differ only in the last sound. knife rhymes with wife and life.

examples.en: Dad cuts the cake with a knife.
examples.zh: 爸爸用刀子切蛋糕。

examples.en: Please use a knife and fork.
examples.zh: 請用刀叉。

knife.spelling_zh: 開頭的 k 不發音，和 know、knee 一樣。
knife.spelling_en: The k at the start is silent, as in know and knee.

know.tip_zh: know 的 k 不發音，唸起來和 no 完全一樣，都是 [no]。拼字的 -ow 在這裡唸 [o]，像 go，不是 now 的 [aʊ]，學生常因為拼字像 now 而唸錯。[o] 是圓唇音，嘴巴從圓形再收得更小一點，聲音拉長，不要唸得又短又扁。
know.tip_en: The k in know is silent; it sounds exactly like no—both are [no]. The -ow here is [o], as in go, not the [aʊ] of now; learners often get it wrong because the spelling looks like now. [o] is a rounded vowel: start with round lips and close them a little more, holding the sound—don't make it short and flat.

examples.en: I know the answer!
examples.zh: 我知道答案！

examples.en: Do you know my teacher?
examples.zh: 你認識我的老師嗎？

know.spelling_zh: k 不發音，know 和 no 同音。
know.spelling_en: The k is silent; know and no sound the same.

language.tip_zh: language 第一音節 [læŋ] 的 n 其實是 [ŋ]：舌根抬起碰軟顎，像 long 的結尾，接著馬上發 [g]。學生常省略 [g]，唸成 lan-wage，或把 [æ] 唸得太窄。後半 -guage 不是 age 的 [e]，而是很輕的 [ə]，最後的 [dʒ] 嘴唇往前嘟，送出氣就停，不要加母音。重音在第一音節。
language.tip_en: In the first syllable of language, [læŋ], the n is really [ŋ]: raise the back of the tongue to the soft palate, as at the end of long, and go straight into [g]. Learners often drop the [g] and say lan-wage, or make the [æ] too narrow. The second half -guage doesn't have the [e] of age but a very light [ə]; for the final [dʒ], push the lips forward, release and stop—don't add a vowel. The stress is on the first syllable.

examples.en: English is a fun language to learn.
examples.zh: 英文是一種學起來很有趣的語言。

examples.en: What language do people speak in Japan?
examples.zh: 日本人說什麼語言？

language.spelling_zh: -guage 的 u 唸 [w]，a 弱化成 [ə]。
language.spelling_en: In -guage, the u sounds like [w] and the a weakens to [ə].

laugh.tip_zh: laugh 的拼字很容易騙人：au 唸 [æ]，gh 唸 [f]，整個字是 [læf]，跟 half 押韻。學生常把 au 唸成 [ɔ] 或 [ɑ]，或者看到 gh 就不發音，把字尾的 [f] 漏掉。做法：[l] 舌尖頂上齒齦，接著嘴巴張大、嘴角往兩邊拉發 [æ]，最後上齒輕碰下唇吹出 [f]。
laugh.tip_en: The spelling of laugh is easy to be fooled by: au is [æ], gh is [f], and the whole word is [læf], rhyming with half. Learners often say au as [ɔ] or [ɑ], or treat gh as silent and leave out the final [f]. How to do it: tongue tip on the gum ridge for [l], then open the mouth wide with the corners spread for [æ], and finally touch the upper teeth to the lower lip and blow out [f].

examples.en: My little brother likes to laugh.
examples.zh: 我弟弟很愛笑。

examples.en: Funny movies always make me laugh.
examples.zh: 搞笑電影總是讓我哈哈大笑。

laugh.spelling_zh: au 唸 [æ]，gh 唸 [f]，跟 half 押韻。
laugh.spelling_en: au sounds like [æ] and gh like [f]; it rhymes with half.

level.tip_zh: level 前後拼字一樣，但兩個 l 不一樣：開頭是亮 L，舌尖頂上齒齦、舌頭往前；字尾 [ḷ] 是暗 L，舌根往後抬，而且前面沒有母音。學生常把 [ɛ] 拉長成 [e]，或把 [v] 唸成 [b]，結尾再加一個「喔」。做法：上齒咬下唇發 [v]，舌尖馬上頂上齒齦接暗 L。
level.tip_en: level is spelled the same both ways, but its two l's are different: the first is a clear L, tongue tip on the gum ridge with the tongue forward; the final [ḷ] is a dark L with the back of the tongue raised, and there's no vowel before it. Learners often stretch [ɛ] into [e], turn [v] into [b], and add an 'o' at the end. How to do it: bite the lower lip for [v], then put the tongue tip straight on the gum ridge for the dark L.

examples.en: I finished the last level of the game!
examples.zh: 我破了遊戲的最後一關！

examples.en: What level is your English class?
examples.zh: 你的英文課是什麼程度？

library.tip_zh: library 有兩個 [r]：[br] 和後面的 [r]。學生常在 [b] 和 [r] 中間多加一個母音，變成四個音節，或乾脆漏掉第一個 [r]，唸成 [ˈlaɪbɛri]。做法：雙唇閉上準備 [b] 時，舌頭就先捲好，嘴唇一放開就是 [br]，像 brown 的開頭。開頭 [l] 舌尖碰上齒齦，[r] 舌尖不碰任何地方。重音在 [ˈlaɪ]。
library.tip_en: library has two [r] sounds: in [br] and the one after it. Learners often slip a vowel between [b] and [r], making four syllables, or drop the first [r] altogether and say [ˈlaɪbɛri]. How to do it: while the lips are closed for [b], have the tongue already curled, so opening the lips gives [br] at once, like the start of brown. For the opening [l] the tongue tip touches the gum ridge; for [r] it touches nothing. The stress is on [ˈlaɪ].

examples.en: I borrow books from the library.
examples.zh: 我從圖書館借書。

examples.en: Let's meet at the school library after lunch.
examples.zh: 我們午餐後在學校圖書館見面吧。

library.kk_flag: Secondary stress is misplaced: GA is [ˈlaɪˌbrɛrɪ] (secondary on brɛ, final syllable unstressed); the given KK puts ˌ before ri. The final [i] is also inconsistent with January's -ɛrɪ in this batch.

lion.tip_zh: lion 有兩個音節 [ˈlaɪ]·[ən]，學生常把它縮成一個音節，聽起來像 line。第一音節 [laɪ] 重而完整，從張大嘴滑到 [ɪ]；第二音節 [ən] 輕而短，兩拍要分清楚。字尾是舌尖頂住上齒齦的 [n]，不是舌根的 [ŋ]，結束時舌尖要碰到上面。
lion.tip_en: lion has two syllables, [ˈlaɪ]·[ən]; learners often squeeze it into one, which sounds like line. The first syllable [laɪ] is strong and complete, gliding from an open mouth to [ɪ]; the second, [ən], is light and short—the two beats must be clearly separate. The final sound is a tongue-tip [n] on the gum ridge, not the back-of-tongue [ŋ]; the tongue tip must touch up there at the end.

examples.en: The lion is sleeping under a tree.
examples.zh: 獅子在樹下睡覺。

examples.en: We saw a lion at the zoo.
examples.zh: 我們在動物園看到一隻獅子。

listen.tip_zh: listen 的 t 不發音，唸 [ˈlɪsən]，學生常照拼字唸成 [ˈlɪstən]。第一音節是短而放鬆的 [ɪ]，不要拉長成 [i]，也不要張嘴到 [ɛ]，不然會變成 lesson。[s] 之後直接接很輕的 [ən]，字尾 [n] 舌尖頂上齒齦收住。重音在第一音節。
listen.tip_en: The t in listen is silent: say [ˈlɪsən]; learners often follow the spelling and say [ˈlɪstən]. The first syllable has a short, relaxed [ɪ]—don't stretch it into [i] or open up to [ɛ], or it becomes lesson. After [s], go straight into a very light [ən], and finish the [n] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge. The stress is on the first syllable.

examples.en: Please listen to your teacher.
examples.zh: 請聽老師說話。

examples.en: I like to listen to music at night.
examples.zh: 我喜歡晚上聽音樂。

listen.spelling_zh: 中間的 t 不發音，和 Christmas 的 t 一樣。
listen.spelling_en: The t in the middle is silent, as in Christmas.

mailman.tip_zh: mailman 的重音在 mail。最容易出錯的是 mail 結尾的 [l]：因為後面緊接 [m]，學生常把它吞掉，唸成 [ˈmemæn]。做法：發完 [e] 之後，舌尖往上頂上齒齦、舌根抬起，停一下再閉上雙唇發 [m]。第二音節 [mæn] 帶次重音，嘴巴張大、嘴角往兩邊拉。先分開說 mail、man，再慢慢連起來。
mailman.tip_en: The stress in mailman is on mail. The easiest place to go wrong is the [l] at the end of mail: because [m] follows right after, learners often swallow it and say [ˈmemæn]. How to do it: after [e], push the tongue tip up to the gum ridge and raise the back of the tongue, pause briefly, then close the lips for [m]. The second syllable [mæn] has secondary stress: open the mouth wide with the corners spread. Say mail and man separately first, then join them slowly.

examples.en: The mailman brings letters every morning.
examples.zh: 郵差每天早上送信來。

examples.en: Our mailman always waves to us.
examples.zh: 我們的郵差總是向我們揮手。

man.tip_zh: man 的母音是 [æ]，台灣學生常把嘴巴張得不夠大，唸得像 men（複數「男人們」）的 [ɛ]，單數和複數就分不清了。發 [æ] 時下巴往下拉、嘴角同時往兩邊拉開，嘴巴要比說「欸」時張得更大。字尾 [n] 要把舌尖頂住上排牙齒後方的齒齦停一下，不要收成 [ŋ]。
man.tip_en: The vowel in man is [æ]. Taiwanese students often don't open the mouth wide enough, so it sounds like the [ɛ] of men (the plural, 'men'), and singular and plural blur together. For [æ], drop the jaw and pull the corners of the mouth wide at the same time, opening wider than for 'eh'. For the final [n], press the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper front teeth and hold it briefly; don't let it turn into [ŋ].

examples.en: The man next door walks his dog every morning.
examples.zh: 隔壁那位先生每天早上都會遛狗。

examples.en: Ask the man at the front desk for help.
examples.zh: 去請櫃台的那位先生幫忙。

math.tip_zh: math 結尾是無聲的 [θ]，台灣學生常唸成 [s]，聽起來像 mass，或乾脆把尾音吞掉。發 [θ] 時舌尖輕輕伸到上下門牙之間，讓氣流從舌頭和牙齒的縫隙送出，聲帶不震動；送完氣就停，不要再加一個母音唸成「麥斯」。前面的 [æ] 嘴巴也要張大，不要唸成 [ɛ]。
math.tip_en: math ends in voiceless [θ]. Taiwanese students often say [s], so it sounds like mass, or they drop the final sound. For [θ], put the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower front teeth and push air through the gap between tongue and teeth, with no voice; stop once the air is out and don't add a vowel (like 'mai-si'). The [æ] before it also needs a wide-open mouth, not [ɛ].

examples.en: Math is my favorite subject at school.
examples.zh: 數學是我在學校最喜歡的科目。

examples.en: We have a math test on Friday.
examples.zh: 我們星期五有數學考試。

matter.tip_zh: matter 重音在第一音節 [mæ]，[æ] 要張大嘴。美式口語中，夾在兩個母音之間的 [t] 常變成輕快的閃音：舌尖在上齒齦輕彈一下，聽起來接近輕的 [d]。台灣學生常把 [t] 唸得又重又用力，再把字尾 [ɚ] 唸成「特」不捲舌。第二音節要輕而短，舌頭往後捲。
matter.tip_en: matter is stressed on the first syllable [mæ], with a wide-open [æ]. In everyday American speech, a [t] between two vowels often becomes a quick flap: the tongue tip taps the ridge behind the upper teeth once, sounding close to a light [d]. Taiwanese students often hit the [t] hard and then say the final [ɚ] like 'te' without curling the tongue. Keep the second syllable light and short, with the tongue curled back.

examples.en: What's the matter? You look tired.
examples.zh: 怎麼了？你看起來很累。

examples.en: No matter how busy she is, Mom reads to us at night.
examples.zh: 不管多忙，媽媽晚上都會唸書給我們聽。

medicine.tip_zh: medicine 重音在第一音節 [mɛ]，後面兩個音節都是輕的 [ə]。台灣學生常照拼字把每個字母都唸清楚，三拍一樣重，或把 di 唸成 [di]。正確節奏是重－輕－輕：第一拍用力，[də] 和 [sən] 快速帶過，嘴巴放鬆。字尾 [n] 舌尖要頂住上齒齦，不要變成 [ŋ]。
medicine.tip_en: medicine is stressed on the first syllable [mɛ]; the next two syllables both have the weak [ə]. Taiwanese students often pronounce every letter clearly from the spelling, giving three equal beats, or say di as [di]. The correct rhythm is strong–weak–weak: hit the first beat, then run [də] and [sən] quickly with a relaxed mouth. For the final [n], press the tongue tip to the ridge behind the upper teeth; don't let it become [ŋ].

examples.en: Please take your medicine after dinner.
examples.zh: 晚餐後請記得吃藥。

examples.en: The doctor gave me some medicine for my cold.
examples.zh: 醫生開了一些感冒藥給我。

medium.tip_zh: medium 重音在第一音節，me 唸長音 [i]，不是 medicine 裡的短音 [ɛ]；台灣學生看到 med 常順口唸成 [ɛ]。後面的 [dɪ] 和 [əm] 輕輕帶過。字尾是 [m]：中文沒有以 m 結尾的字，學生常收成 [n]，或多加一個「姆」的母音。正確做法是最後雙唇輕輕閉上就停，不要再出聲。
medium.tip_en: medium is stressed on the first syllable, and me is the long [i], not the short [ɛ] of medicine; seeing 'med', Taiwanese students often slip into [ɛ]. The following [dɪ] and [əm] are said lightly. The word ends in [m]: Mandarin has no syllables ending in m, so students often finish with [n] or add an extra 'mu' vowel. Instead, just close the lips gently at the end and stop, with no extra sound.

examples.en: Can I have a medium cup of milk tea?
examples.zh: 我可以點一杯中杯奶茶嗎？

examples.en: This T-shirt comes in small, medium, and large.
examples.zh: 這件 T 恤有小號、中號和大號。

modern.tip_zh: modern 的 o 唸 [ɑ]，嘴巴張大、下巴往下，不是 [o]。第二音節 [dɚn] 是捲舌的 [ɚ] 再接 [n]，台灣學生常照外來語唸成「摩登」，把 dern 唸成「登」不捲舌，有時還把重音移到第二音節。正確是第一音節用力；第二音節舌頭先往後捲出 [ɚ]，再把舌尖頂到上齒齦收 [n]，整拍輕而短。
modern.tip_en: The o in modern is [ɑ], with the mouth open wide and the jaw down, not [o]. The second syllable [dɚn] is the r-colored [ɚ] followed by [n]. Taiwanese students often say it like the loanword 'mo-deng', saying dern as 'deng' without curling the tongue, and sometimes move the stress to the second syllable. Stress the first syllable; in the second, curl the tongue back for [ɚ], then touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind the upper teeth for [n], keeping the beat light and short.

examples.en: Our new library is big and modern.
examples.zh: 我們的新圖書館又大又現代化。

examples.en: Taipei is a modern city with many tall buildings.
examples.zh: 台北是一座有很多高樓的現代化城市。

monkey.tip_zh: monkey 的 o 唸 [ʌ]，和 cup、sun 的母音一樣，台灣學生常照拼字唸成 [ɑ] 或 [o]。中間的 n 要唸 [ŋ]：因為後面接 [k]，舌根先抬起頂住上顎後方發 [ŋ]，接著在同一個位置直接放開成 [k]，不要用舌尖頂前面唸成 [n]。重音在第一音節，字尾 [kɪ] 輕而短。
monkey.tip_en: The o in monkey is [ʌ], the same vowel as in cup and sun; Taiwanese students often read it from the spelling as [ɑ] or [o]. The n must be [ŋ]: because [k] follows, raise the back of the tongue against the back of the roof of the mouth for [ŋ], then release from the same spot into [k]; don't use the tongue tip at the front for [n]. Stress the first syllable; the final [kɪ] is light and short.

examples.en: The monkey is eating a banana in the tree.
examples.zh: 猴子在樹上吃香蕉。

examples.en: We saw a funny monkey at the zoo.
examples.zh: 我們在動物園看到一隻好笑的猴子。

moon.tip_zh: moon 的 oo 是長音 [u]，嘴唇要嘟圓往前推並維持住，台灣學生常唸得太短、嘴唇太鬆。字尾 [n] 更容易出錯：學生常把結尾收成 [ŋ]，變成 [muŋ]，或尾音不見只剩「木」。發完 [u] 後，舌尖要往上頂住上排牙齒後方的齒齦，讓聲音從鼻子出來，結尾和 noon、soon 一樣。
moon.tip_en: The oo in moon is the long [u]: round the lips, push them forward and hold them. Taiwanese students often make it too short with lips too relaxed. The final [n] is even easier to get wrong: students often end with [ŋ], making [muŋ], or drop the ending so only 'mu' is left. After the [u], lift the tongue tip to the ridge behind the upper front teeth and let the sound come out through the nose; the ending is the same as in noon and soon.

examples.en: The moon is very bright tonight.
examples.zh: 今晚的月亮好亮。

examples.en: At Mid-Autumn Festival, we eat mooncakes and look at the moon.
examples.zh: 中秋節時，我們會吃月餅、賞月。

mother.tip_zh: mother 中間是有聲的 [ð]，台灣學生常唸成 [d] 或 [z]，因為中文沒有這個音。發 [ð] 時舌尖輕放在上下門牙之間，喉嚨要震動，用手摸喉嚨應該感覺得到。第一個母音是 [ʌ]，嘴巴半開放鬆，不要照拼字唸成 [o] 或 [ɑ]。字尾 [ɚ] 舌頭往後捲、輕輕帶過，和 brother、other 的結尾一樣。
mother.tip_en: mother has the voiced [ð] in the middle; Taiwanese students often say [d] or [z] because Mandarin has no such sound. For [ð], rest the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower front teeth and let the throat vibrate; you should feel it if you touch your throat. The first vowel is [ʌ], with a half-open, relaxed mouth; don't read it from the spelling as [o] or [ɑ]. For the final [ɚ], curl the tongue back and say it lightly, the same ending as in brother and other.

examples.en: My mother makes the best fried rice.
examples.zh: 我媽媽做的炒飯最好吃。

examples.en: I made a card for my mother on Mother's Day.
examples.zh: 母親節時，我做了一張卡片給媽媽。

motorcycle.tip_zh: motorcycle 有四個音節，主重音在第一音節 [mo]，[saɪ] 是次重音，中間的 [tɚ] 輕而捲舌。最常見的錯在字尾：台灣學生常把 cle 唸成「扣」，在 [k] 後面多加一個母音。字尾其實是成音節的 [ḷ]：[k] 一放開，舌尖就頂住上齒齦、舌根往後抬，發出暗 L，中間不插入任何母音。
motorcycle.tip_en: motorcycle has four syllables; the main stress is on the first syllable [mo], [saɪ] has secondary stress, and the middle [tɚ] is light with a tongue curl. The most common mistake is at the end: Taiwanese students often say cle like 'kou', adding a vowel after [k]. The ending is actually a syllabic [ḷ]: as soon as [k] is released, the tongue tip presses the ridge behind the upper teeth and the back of the tongue lifts for a dark L, with no vowel inserted.

examples.en: My dad rides a motorcycle to work every day.
examples.zh: 我爸爸每天騎機車上班。

examples.en: Please wear a helmet on the motorcycle.
examples.zh: 坐機車時請戴安全帽。

mouth.tip_zh: mouth 結尾是無聲的 [θ]，台灣學生常唸成 [s]，結果變成 mouse（老鼠），意思完全不同。[aʊ] 要從張大嘴的 [a] 滑到圓唇的 [ʊ]，滑完之後舌尖馬上伸到上下門牙之間吹氣，聲帶不震動。可以先慢慢說 [maʊ]，再把舌頭伸出來送氣，對照練習 mouth 和 mouse 的差別。
mouth.tip_en: mouth ends in voiceless [θ]; Taiwanese students often say [s], turning it into mouse, which means something completely different. [aʊ] glides from an open-mouthed [a] to rounded [ʊ]; right after the glide, put the tongue tip between the upper and lower front teeth and blow air with no voice. Say [maʊ] slowly first, then stick the tongue out and push air, practicing mouth and mouse side by side.

examples.en: Open your mouth and say 'ah.'
examples.zh: 張開嘴巴，說「啊」。

examples.en: Don't talk with your mouth full.
examples.zh: 嘴巴裡有食物時不要說話。

museum.tip_zh: museum 重音在第二音節 [zi]，台灣學生常把重音放在第一音節 mu，整個字的節奏就跑掉了。正確是輕－重－輕：[mju] 輕短，[zi] 拉長用力，最後 [əm] 輕輕帶過。中間的 s 唸有聲的 [z]，不是 [s]，喉嚨要震動，像 zoo 的開頭。字尾 [m] 要把雙唇閉起來，不要收成 [n]。
museum.tip_en: museum is stressed on the second syllable [zi]; Taiwanese students often stress the first syllable mu, which throws off the rhythm of the whole word. The correct pattern is weak–strong–weak: [mju] short and light, [zi] long and strong, then [əm] said lightly. The s is the voiced [z], not [s]; the throat vibrates, like the start of zoo. For the final [m], close the lips; don't end with [n].

examples.en: Our class visited the science museum last week.
examples.zh: 我們班上週去參觀了科學博物館。

examples.en: The museum has a big dinosaur model.
examples.zh: 博物館裡有一個很大的恐龍模型。

music.tip_zh: music 的 s 唸有聲的 [z]，台灣學生常照拼字唸成 [s]，聽起來像「謬昔克」。發 [z] 時舌尖靠近上齒齦，像蜜蜂嗡嗡叫，喉嚨要震動。開頭是 [mju]，m 後面有 [j] 滑音，嘴唇從閉合直接滑到圓唇的 [u]，不要只唸成 [mu]。重音在第一音節，字尾 [k] 輕輕收住，不要多加母音。
music.tip_en: The s in music is the voiced [z]; Taiwanese students often read it as [s] from the spelling, sounding like 'miu-si-ke'. For [z], hold the tongue tip near the ridge behind the upper teeth and buzz like a bee, with the throat vibrating. It begins with [mju]: there is a [j] glide after m, so the lips go from closed straight into rounded [u]; don't say just [mu]. Stress the first syllable, and close the final [k] lightly without adding a vowel.

examples.en: We have music class on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 我們星期二有音樂課。

examples.en: My sister listens to music while she does homework.
examples.zh: 我妹妹一邊寫功課一邊聽音樂。

national.tip_zh: national 的 na 唸 [næ]，是嘴巴張大的 [æ]。台灣學生因為先學過 nation [ˈneʃən]，常把開頭也唸成 [ne]，這是最常見的錯：nation 變成 national 時，母音會改變。中間的 [ʃə] 輕輕帶過；字尾 [nəl] 的 l 是暗 L，舌尖頂住上齒齦、舌根抬起，不要唸成「喔」或省略。
national.tip_en: The na in national is [næ], with the wide-open [æ]. Because Taiwanese students learned nation [ˈneʃən] first, they often start this word with [ne] too; this is the most common mistake: the vowel changes when nation becomes national. The middle [ʃə] is said lightly; the l at the end of [nəl] is a dark L, with the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth and the back of the tongue raised; don't turn it into 'o' or drop it.

examples.en: We visited a national park during summer vacation.
examples.zh: 暑假時我們去了一座國家公園。

examples.en: Everyone stood up for the national anthem.
examples.zh: 奏國歌時，大家都站了起來。

national.variant_zh: 口語常縮成兩個音節 [ˈnæʃnəl]，兩種都對。
national.variant_en: In casual speech it is often two syllables, [ˈnæʃnəl]; both are correct.

neighbor.tip_zh: neighbor 的 eigh 只唸一個 [e]，和 eight 的開頭一樣，gh 完全不發音。台灣學生看到這麼多字母，常想把 g 唸出來，或把 ei 拆成兩個音。正確是 [ne] 接 [bɚ]：重音在第一音節，發 [e] 時嘴角往兩邊拉。第二音節雙唇先閉合發 [b]，接著舌頭往後捲出 [ɚ]，不要唸成「伯」就停住不捲舌。
neighbor.tip_en: The eigh in neighbor is just one sound, [e], the same as the start of eight; the gh is completely silent. Seeing so many letters, Taiwanese students often try to pronounce the g, or split ei into two sounds. Say [ne] then [bɚ]: stress the first syllable and pull the corners of the mouth wide for [e]. For the second syllable, close the lips for [b], then curl the tongue back for [ɚ]; don't stop at 'bo' without the curl.

examples.en: Our neighbor has a big orange cat.
examples.zh: 我們的鄰居有一隻大橘貓。

examples.en: We gave our neighbor some homemade cookies.
examples.zh: 我們送了一些自己做的餅乾給鄰居。

neighbor.spelling_en: eigh is just [e]; the gh is silent.

never.tip_zh: never 中間的 [v] 是上排門牙輕咬下唇再震動，台灣學生常唸成 [w] 或 [b]，聽起來像「內握」或「內伯」。發 [v] 時牙齒要真的碰到下唇，喉嚨同時震動，下唇會有麻麻的感覺。第一音節 [nɛ] 重而短，嘴巴微開。字尾 [ɚ] 輕輕捲舌，和 ever 的結尾一樣。
never.tip_en: The [v] in the middle of never is made by lightly biting the lower lip with the upper front teeth while voicing; Taiwanese students often say [w] or [b], sounding like 'nei-wo' or 'nei-bo'. For [v], the teeth must actually touch the lower lip while the throat vibrates; the lower lip will feel a slight buzz. The first syllable [nɛ] is stressed and short, with the mouth slightly open. The final [ɚ] is a light tongue curl, the same ending as in ever.

examples.en: My grandma never forgets my birthday.
examples.zh: 奶奶從來不會忘記我的生日。

examples.en: Never cross the street when the light is red.
examples.zh: 紅燈時絕對不要過馬路。

newspaper.tip_zh: newspaper 是 news 加 paper 組成的，重音在第一音節 [nuz]，paper 的部分變輕。台灣學生常把兩個字分開唸，在 news 後面多加一個母音，唸成「紐斯－配波」四拍。正確是 [nuz] 結尾的子音直接連到 [pe]，中間不停頓、不加母音。[pe] 的 [e] 嘴角往兩邊拉，最後 [pɚ] 輕輕捲舌。美式開頭是 [nu]，不加 [j]。
newspaper.tip_en: newspaper is news plus paper; the stress is on the first syllable [nuz], and the paper part becomes lighter. Taiwanese students often say the two words separately and add a vowel after news, making four beats like 'niu-si-pei-po'. Instead, link the final consonant of [nuz] straight into [pe], with no pause and no added vowel. The [e] in [pe] pulls the corners of the mouth wide, and the final [pɚ] has a light tongue curl. American English starts with [nu], without a [j].

examples.en: Grandpa reads the newspaper every morning.
examples.zh: 爺爺每天早上看報紙。

examples.en: We covered the table with an old newspaper.
examples.zh: 我們用舊報紙把桌子蓋起來。

nobody.tip_zh: nobody 是 no 加 body，重音在第一音節 [no]，台灣學生常把重音移到 bo 上，唸成 no-BO-dy，聽起來像兩個分開的字。正確是第一拍最重：[no] 要唸足，嘴唇圓起來並略帶滑音；接著 [bɑ] 嘴巴張開但放輕，最後 [dɪ] 短短帶過。可以想成 NO-body：先大聲說 no，再小聲接 body。
nobody.tip_en: nobody is no plus body, stressed on the first syllable [no]; Taiwanese students often move the stress onto bo, saying no-BO-dy, which sounds like two separate words. The first beat should be strongest: give [no] its full length, with rounded lips and a slight glide; then [bɑ] with an open but lighter mouth, and finally [dɪ] said briefly. Think of it as NO-body: say no loudly, then body softly.

examples.en: Nobody was late for class today.
examples.zh: 今天沒有人上課遲到。

examples.en: Nobody knows where the cat went.
examples.zh: 沒有人知道貓跑去哪裡了。

nobody.variant_zh: 口語常把中間弱化，唸成 [ˈnobədɪ]。
nobody.variant_en: In casual speech the middle is often reduced: [ˈnobədɪ].
nobody.kk_flag: Given KK [ˈnoˌbɑˌdi] puts a secondary-stress mark on the last syllable; in General American the final -dy is unstressed, so [ˈnoˌbɑdɪ] (or reduced [ˈnobədɪ]) is expected. Also, the batch's rhyme list (agree, be, bee, free, he, key) matches only the last syllable and does not really rhyme with nobody.

nothing.tip_zh: nothing 的 o 唸 [ʌ]，和 nut、bus 的母音一樣，台灣學生常照拼字唸成 [o]，變成「挪性」。中間的 th 是無聲的 [θ]，常被唸成 [s] 或 [f]：舌尖伸到上下門牙之間吹氣，接著舌頭快速收回發 [ɪ]。字尾 -ing 是 [ɪŋ]，舌根抬起頂住上顎後方，舌尖不要碰上齒齦收成 [n]。
nothing.tip_en: The o in nothing is [ʌ], the same vowel as in nut and bus; Taiwanese students often read it as [o] from the spelling, making it sound like 'nuo-sing'. The th in the middle is voiceless [θ] and is often said as [s] or [f]: put the tongue tip between the upper and lower front teeth and blow, then quickly pull the tongue back for [ɪ]. The -ing ending is [ɪŋ]: raise the back of the tongue against the back of the roof of the mouth, and don't let the tongue tip touch the ridge behind the teeth to make [n].

examples.en: There is nothing in the box.
examples.zh: 盒子裡什麼都沒有。

examples.en: I have nothing to do this afternoon.
examples.zh: 我今天下午沒事做。

november.tip_zh: November 重音在第二音節 [vɛm]，台灣學生常把重音放在開頭的 no，唸成 NO-vember。正確是輕－重－輕：[no] 輕輕帶過，[vɛm] 用力。[v] 要上齒輕咬下唇並震動，不要唸成 [w] 或 [b]。[vɛm] 結尾雙唇閉合發 [m]，直接接 [b]，嘴唇不用打開；最後 [bɚ] 捲舌，和 December、remember 的結尾一樣。
november.tip_en: November is stressed on the second syllable [vɛm]; Taiwanese students often stress the opening no, saying NO-vember. The pattern is weak–strong–weak: [no] said lightly, [vɛm] strong. For [v], lightly bite the lower lip with the upper teeth and voice it; don't say [w] or [b]. At the end of [vɛm], close the lips for [m] and go straight into [b] without opening them; the final [bɚ] has a tongue curl, the same ending as December and remember.

examples.en: My birthday is in November.
examples.zh: 我的生日在十一月。

examples.en: The weather gets cooler in November.
examples.zh: 十一月天氣會變涼。

nurse.tip_zh: nurse 只有一個母音 [ɝ]，是要捲舌的重音母音。台灣學生常照拼字把 u 和 r 分開唸，或舌頭不捲，唸成像「呢斯」。發 [ɝ] 時舌尖往後捲、不碰到上顎，嘴唇微圓，把這個音拉長，和 bird、her 的母音一樣。字尾 [s] 輕輕吹氣就停，後面不要再加母音。
nurse.tip_en: nurse has only one vowel, [ɝ], a stressed vowel with a tongue curl. Taiwanese students often split u and r into two sounds from the spelling, or skip the curl, making it sound like 'ne-si'. For [ɝ], curl the tongue tip back without touching the roof of the mouth, round the lips slightly, and hold the sound; it is the same vowel as in bird and her. For the final [s], just blow a little air and stop, with no vowel after it.

examples.en: The school nurse helped me when I felt sick.
examples.zh: 我不舒服的時候，學校的護理師幫助了我。

examples.en: My aunt is a nurse at the hospital.
examples.zh: 我阿姨在醫院當護士。

october.tip_zh: October 重音在第二音節 [to]，台灣學生常把重音放在開頭的 Oc。開頭 [ɑk] 嘴巴張大，[k] 只做出舌根的動作，不要多加母音唸成「阿克」，要直接接到 [t]。[to] 的 [o] 要唸足並略帶圓唇滑音，最後 [bɚ] 舌頭往後捲、輕輕帶過。整個字的節奏是輕－重－輕。
october.tip_en: October is stressed on the second syllable [to]; Taiwanese students often stress the opening Oc. The opening [ɑk] has a wide-open mouth; the [k] is just the movement of the back of the tongue, with no extra vowel like 'a-ke', linking straight into [t]. Give the [o] in [to] its full length with a slight rounded glide, and say the final [bɚ] lightly with the tongue curled back. The rhythm of the whole word is weak–strong–weak.

examples.en: We go camping every October.
examples.zh: 我們每年十月都會去露營。

examples.en: Halloween is at the end of October.
examples.zh: 萬聖節在十月底。

of.tip_zh: of 的 f 唸有聲的 [v]，不是 [f]，這是拼字最容易誤導的地方；台灣學生常唸成 [ɔf] 或「歐夫」，和 off 混在一起。正確是短短的 [ʌ] 接 [v]：上齒輕碰下唇，喉嚨震動。在句子裡 of 通常唸得很弱，像 a glass of water 會輕到接近 [əv]，所以不要每次都唸得很重。
of.tip_en: The f in of is the voiced [v], not [f]; this is where the spelling misleads most. Taiwanese students often say [ɔf] or 'ou-fu', mixing it up with off. The correct form is a short [ʌ] plus [v]: upper teeth lightly on the lower lip, with the throat vibrating. In sentences of is usually weak; in a glass of water it becomes close to [əv], so don't stress it every time.

examples.en: Can I have a glass of water?
examples.zh: 可以給我一杯水嗎？

examples.en: One of my friends lives near the park.
examples.zh: 我有一個朋友住在公園附近。

of.spelling_en: The f here is pronounced [v], not [f].

officer.tip_zh: officer 重音在第一音節 [ɔ]，嘴巴張開成圓的 [ɔ]，後面 [fə] 和 [sɚ] 都要輕。台灣學生常把 office 的部分唸成「歐飛斯」，再加上 er 變成四拍，或把重音放到 fi 上。正確是三個音節、重－輕－輕：[ɔ] 用力，[fə] 輕而短，最後 [sɚ] 舌頭往後捲，不要拆成「斯」和「兒」兩拍。
officer.tip_en: officer is stressed on the first syllable [ɔ], with the mouth open and rounded for [ɔ]; the following [fə] and [sɚ] are both weak. Taiwanese students often say the office part as 'ou-fei-si' and then add er, making four beats, or put the stress on fi. It is three syllables, strong–weak–weak: [ɔ] strong, [fə] light and short, and the final [sɚ] with the tongue curled back; don't split it into two beats like 'si' plus 'er'.

examples.en: The police officer helped us find our way.
examples.zh: 警察幫我們找到了路。

examples.en: A friendly officer stood at the school gate.
examples.zh: 一位親切的警察站在學校門口。

often.tip_zh: often 最常見的唸法是 [ˈɔfən]，t 不發音；台灣學生常照拼字把 t 用力唸出來，變成「歐夫疼」。重音在第一音節 [ɔ]，嘴巴張開成圓形。接著上齒碰下唇發 [f]，直接連到輕而短的 [ən]，中間不加母音。字尾 [n] 舌尖頂住上齒齦，不要收成 [ŋ]。
often.tip_en: The most common pronunciation of often is [ˈɔfən], with a silent t; Taiwanese students often pronounce the t hard from the spelling, making it sound like 'ou-fu-teng'. Stress the first syllable [ɔ] with an open, rounded mouth. Then touch the upper teeth to the lower lip for [f] and go straight into a light, short [ən], with no vowel in between. For the final [n], press the tongue tip to the ridge behind the upper teeth; don't end with [ŋ].

examples.en: I often ride my bike to school.
examples.zh: 我常常騎腳踏車上學。

examples.en: How often do you visit your grandparents?
examples.zh: 你多久去看一次爺爺奶奶？

often.variant_zh: 也有人會唸出 t：[ˈɔftṇ]，兩種都常聽到。
often.variant_en: Some people do pronounce the t: [ˈɔftṇ]; both are common.
often.spelling_zh: 最常見的唸法中，t 不發音。
often.spelling_en: In the most common pronunciation, the t is silent.

on.tip_zh: on 只有一個音節 [ɑn]，下巴要放低、嘴巴張大，像看醫生時說「啊」。常見錯誤是嘴唇嘟得太圓、太緊，聽起來像 own [on]；或把字尾唸成後鼻音 [ŋ]，變成「昂」。收尾時舌尖要頂住上排牙齒後面的牙齦，讓聲音從鼻子出來，才是清楚的 [n]。
on.tip_en: on has just one syllable, [ɑn]: drop the jaw and open the mouth wide, like saying "ah" at the doctor's. A common mistake is rounding the lips too much and too tightly, so it sounds like own [on]; another is ending with the back nasal [ŋ], turning it into "ang". To finish, press the tongue tip on the gum ridge behind the upper teeth and let the sound come out through the nose — that is a clean [n].

examples.en: Your pencil is on the floor.
examples.zh: 你的鉛筆在地板上。

examples.en: The cat is sleeping on my bed.
examples.zh: 貓咪正在我的床上睡覺。

on.variant_zh: 有些美國人唸 [ɔn]，嘴唇稍微圓一點，也是對的。
on.variant_en: Some Americans say [ɔn], with slightly rounder lips; that is also correct.

one.tip_zh: one 唸 [wʌn]，母音是短而放鬆的 [ʌ]，嘴巴半開，和 fun、run 押韻。常見錯誤是唸成「萬」，嘴巴張太大、聲調往下掉；或字尾變成後鼻音 [ŋ]，聽起來像「旺」。先把嘴唇嘟起來發 [w]，馬上放鬆成 [ʌ]，最後舌尖頂住上牙齦收 [n]。
one.tip_en: one is [wʌn]; the vowel is a short, relaxed [ʌ] with the mouth half open, and it rhymes with fun and run. A common mistake is saying it like Mandarin 萬 (wàn), with the mouth too wide and a falling tone; another is ending with the back nasal [ŋ], so it sounds like 旺 (wàng). Round the lips for [w], relax right away into [ʌ], then finish with the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n].

examples.en: I have one brother and two sisters.
examples.zh: 我有一個哥哥和兩個姊姊。

examples.en: Can I have one more cookie, please?
examples.zh: 我可以再吃一塊餅乾嗎？

one.spelling_zh: one 裡沒有 w 這個字母，開頭卻要發 [w] 的音。
one.spelling_en: one has no letter w, but it starts with a [w] sound.

or.tip_zh: or 唸 [ɔr]：先把嘴唇稍微圓起來發 [ɔ]，接著舌尖往後捲、不碰到上顎，帶出 [r]。常見錯誤是只唸「歐」就停住，少了捲舌，聽起來像 oh；也有人把 [ɔ] 唸成會滑動的 [o]。可以用押韻的 door、for、floor 一起練，每個字的結尾都要捲舌。
or.tip_en: or is [ɔr]: round the lips slightly for [ɔ], then curl the tongue tip back without touching the roof of the mouth to add [r]. A common mistake is stopping at "oh" with no curl, so it sounds like oh; some also turn [ɔ] into the gliding [o]. Practice with the rhymes door, for and floor — every one of them ends with the curl.

examples.en: Do you want milk or juice?
examples.zh: 你要牛奶還是果汁？

examples.en: Is your birthday in May or June?
examples.zh: 你的生日在五月還是六月？

or.variant_zh: 在句子中常弱讀成 [ɚ]，例如 tea or coffee。
or.variant_en: In sentences it is often reduced to [ɚ], as in "tea or coffee".

orange.tip_zh: orange 只有兩個音節，重音在第一音節 [ɔ]。常見錯誤是唸成「歐蘭吉」三個音節：第二音節開頭用了 [l]，母音唸得太飽滿，字尾 [dʒ] 後面又多加一個「ㄧ」。第二音節要用捲舌的 [r]，輕輕帶過成 [rəndʒ]；最後的 [dʒ] 嘴唇往前噘，跟 juice 開頭的音一樣，發完就停，不要再加母音。
orange.tip_en: orange has only two syllables, stressed on the first, [ɔ]. A common mistake is saying it as three syllables, like "o-lan-ji": the second syllable starts with [l], its vowel is too full, and an extra "ee" is added after the final [dʒ]. Start the second syllable with a curled [r] and keep it light, [rəndʒ]; for the final [dʒ], push the lips forward — the same sound that starts juice — and stop there, with no extra vowel.

examples.en: I eat an orange every morning.
examples.zh: 我每天早上吃一顆柳橙。

examples.en: Would you like some orange juice?
examples.zh: 你想喝點柳橙汁嗎？

orange.variant_zh: 美國東北部常唸 [ˈɑrəndʒ]，第一個母音嘴巴張得更大。
orange.variant_en: In the US Northeast it is often [ˈɑrəndʒ], with the mouth opening wider on the first vowel.

other.tip_zh: other 的重點在第二音節 [ðɚ]。常見錯誤是把 [ð] 唸成 [d] 或 [z]，變成「阿德」或「阿惹」。舌尖輕輕放在上下門牙之間，喉嚨同時要震動，再把舌頭往後捲成 [ɚ]。開頭的 o 唸短短的 [ʌ]，跟 mother、brother 的第一個母音一樣，不要唸成「歐」。
other.tip_en: The key is the second syllable, [ðɚ]. A common mistake is turning [ð] into [d] or [z], so it sounds like "a-der" or "a-zer". Rest the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower front teeth with the throat vibrating, then curl the tongue back for [ɚ]. The first o is a short [ʌ], the same as the first vowel in mother and brother — not "oh".

examples.en: Where is my other shoe?
examples.zh: 我的另一隻鞋子在哪裡？

examples.en: Some kids like cats, and other kids like dogs.
examples.zh: 有些小朋友喜歡貓，其他小朋友喜歡狗。

other.spelling_zh: 開頭的 o 在這裡唸 [ʌ]，不唸 [o]。
other.spelling_en: The first o here is said [ʌ], not [o].

over.tip_zh: over 常被唸成「歐佛」或「歐窩」：[v] 變成沒有聲音的 [f]，或嘴唇沒碰到牙齒，變成 [w]。發 [v] 時上排牙齒輕碰下嘴唇，喉嚨要震動，像蜜蜂的嗡嗡聲。結尾的 [ɚ] 舌頭往後捲，不要停在「佛」。開頭的 [o] 嘴唇先圓，再慢慢收小。
over.tip_en: over is often said like "o-fo" or "o-wo": [v] becomes the voiceless [f], or the lips miss the teeth and it becomes [w]. For [v], rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and let the throat vibrate, like a buzzing bee. For the final [ɚ], curl the tongue back instead of stopping at "fo". For the opening [o], start with round lips and let them close a little.

examples.en: The game is over. Let's go home.
examples.zh: 比賽結束了，我們回家吧。

examples.en: Summer vacation is almost over.
examples.zh: 暑假快要結束了。

papaya.tip_zh: papaya 有三個音節，重音在中間的 [paɪ]。常見錯誤是照中文習慣把第一音節唸得又重又滿，變成「趴趴呀」，或把 [aɪ] 唸成單純的「ㄚ」。第一音節 [pə] 要輕而短，中間的 [paɪ] 拉長、加大聲，跟 pie 同音，最後的 [ə] 輕輕帶過就好。
papaya.tip_en: papaya has three syllables, stressed on the middle one, [paɪ]. A common mistake is giving the first syllable full weight, as in "pa-pa-ya", or flattening [aɪ] into a plain "ah". Keep the first syllable [pə] short and light, make the middle [paɪ] long and loud — it sounds just like pie — and let the final [ə] fade softly.

examples.en: Grandma cut a papaya for dessert.
examples.zh: 奶奶切了一顆木瓜當甜點。

examples.en: Papaya milk is popular in Taiwan.
examples.zh: 木瓜牛奶在台灣很受歡迎。

perhaps.tip_zh: perhaps 的重音在第二音節 [hæps]，不在 per。常見錯誤是把第一音節唸重、[æ] 唸成扁扁的 [ɛ]，結尾 [ps] 又多加母音，變成「趴黑普斯」。第一音節輕輕唸 [pɚ]，舌頭微捲；[h] 要聽得到氣，下巴往下張大發 [æ]；最後雙唇閉合發 [p]，直接接 [s] 的嘶聲，中間不加母音。
perhaps.tip_en: perhaps is stressed on the second syllable, [hæps], not on per. Common mistakes are stressing the first syllable, flattening [æ] into [ɛ], and adding vowels to the final [ps], so it sounds like "pa-hei-pu-si". Say the first syllable lightly as [pɚ] with a slight tongue curl; make the [h] an audible breath and drop the jaw wide for [æ]; then close the lips for [p] and go straight into the hiss of [s], with no vowel in between.

examples.en: Perhaps it will rain this afternoon.
examples.zh: 下午或許會下雨。

examples.en: Perhaps we can play together tomorrow.
examples.zh: 也許我們明天可以一起玩。

person.tip_zh: person 的第一音節 [pɝ]，整個母音都要捲舌，跟 her、bird 的母音一樣。常見錯誤是唸成「趴森」或「佩森」，嘴巴張太開、舌頭沒有捲。發 [ɝ] 時舌尖往後捲起、不碰上顎，嘴唇微圓。第二音節 [sən] 很輕，最後舌尖頂住上牙齦收 [n]，不要唸成後鼻音的「桑」。
person.tip_en: The first syllable of person, [pɝ], is r-colored all the way through — the same vowel as in her and bird. A common mistake is saying "pa-sen" or "pei-sen", with the mouth too open and no tongue curl. For [ɝ], curl the tongue tip back without touching the roof of the mouth and round the lips slightly. The second syllable [sən] is very light; finish with the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n], not the back nasal of "sang".

examples.en: My teacher is a very kind person.
examples.zh: 我的老師是一個非常親切的人。

examples.en: Each person gets one piece of cake.
examples.zh: 每個人可以拿一塊蛋糕。

photo.tip_zh: photo 開頭的 ph 唸 [f]：上排牙齒輕碰下嘴唇吹氣，不是雙唇爆開的 [p]，否則會變成「剖頭」。兩個音節都是 [o]，美式發音裡嘴唇會從圓慢慢收小、往 [u] 滑過去，不要唸成短短平平的「ㄛ」。重音在第一音節 [fo]，第二音節 [to] 輕一點。
photo.tip_en: The ph at the start of photo is [f]: rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and blow — not a [p] that pops from both lips, or it sounds like "po-tou". Both syllables have [o]; in American English the lips start round and close slightly, gliding toward [u], so don't say a short, flat "aw". The stress is on the first syllable, [fo]; the second, [to], is lighter.

examples.en: Let's take a photo with Grandpa.
examples.zh: 我們跟爺爺拍張照吧。

examples.en: This is a photo of my family.
examples.zh: 這是我家人的照片。

photo.spelling_zh: ph 唸 [f]，跟 phone 一樣。
photo.spelling_en: ph is said [f], just like in phone.

piano.tip_zh: piano 有三個音節，重音在第二音節 [æ]。常見錯誤是唸成「批阿諾」，把 [æ] 唸成中文的「ㄚ」，或把重音放在第一音節。[æ] 要下巴往下張大、嘴角往兩旁拉，和 apple 開頭的音一樣，而且要唸得最長、最響。第一音節 [pɪ] 短而輕，最後的 [o] 嘴唇收圓。
piano.tip_en: piano has three syllables, stressed on the second, [æ]. A common mistake is saying "pi-a-no" with [æ] as Mandarin's plain "a", or putting the stress on the first syllable. For [æ], drop the jaw and pull the corners of the mouth wide, as at the start of apple, and make it the longest, loudest part. The first syllable [pɪ] is short and light; round the lips for the final [o].

examples.en: My sister plays the piano every night.
examples.zh: 我姊姊每天晚上彈鋼琴。

examples.en: We have a piano lesson on Friday.
examples.zh: 我們星期五有鋼琴課。

picture.tip_zh: picture 的第一音節是 [pɪk]，跟 pick 一樣，[k] 不能省略。常見錯誤是漏掉 [k] 直接接 [tʃ]，聽起來變成 pitcher（水壺）；或把 [ɪ] 拉成長長的 [i]。發完 [ɪ] 後舌根輕碰上顎、停一下發 [k]，再接嘴唇往前噘的 [tʃ]，最後舌頭捲起發 [ɚ]，不要停在平平的「球」。
picture.tip_en: The first syllable of picture is [pɪk], the same as pick, and the [k] can't be dropped. A common mistake is skipping the [k] and going straight into [tʃ], which turns it into pitcher (a jug); another is stretching [ɪ] into a long [i]. After [ɪ], briefly touch the back of the tongue to the roof of the mouth for [k], then push the lips forward for [tʃ], and finally curl the tongue for [ɚ] — don't end on a flat "chiu".

examples.en: Can you draw a picture of your dog?
examples.zh: 你可以畫一張你家狗狗的圖嗎？

examples.en: Mom put my picture on the wall.
examples.zh: 媽媽把我的畫掛在牆上。

pizza.tip_zh: pizza 中間的 zz 唸 [ts]，不是 [z]，也不是單純的 [s]。常見錯誤是照中文「披薩」來唸，兩個音節一樣重，第二音節還唸得很響。正確是第一音節 [pit] 拉長加重：舌尖先頂住上牙齦，再放開滑成 [s]，跟 cats 字尾的 [ts] 一樣；第二音節 [sə] 輕輕帶過。
pizza.tip_en: The zz in the middle of pizza is [ts] — not [z], and not a plain [s]. A common mistake is saying it like the Mandarin 披薩, with both syllables equally strong and the second one loud. Instead, make the first syllable [pit] long and stressed: press the tongue tip on the gum ridge, then release it into [s], just like the [ts] at the end of cats. The second syllable [sə] is quick and light.

examples.en: We had pizza for dinner on Saturday.
examples.zh: 我們星期六晚餐吃披薩。

examples.en: Can I have another slice of pizza?
examples.zh: 我可以再吃一片披薩嗎？

pleasure.tip_zh: pleasure 的難點是 [ʒ]，中文沒有這個音。常見錯誤是唸成沒有聲音的 [ʃ]，或照拼字唸出 sure，變成「普累秀」。發 [ʒ] 時嘴唇往前噘，舌頭位置和 [ʃ] 一樣，但喉嚨要震動，跟 television 裡 s 的音相同。開頭 [pl] 中間不要多加「ㄨ」，最後舌頭捲成 [ɚ]。
pleasure.tip_en: The hard part of pleasure is [ʒ], a sound Mandarin doesn't have. A common mistake is using the voiceless [ʃ], or reading the spelling sure aloud, so it sounds like "pu-lei-shiu". For [ʒ], push the lips forward with the tongue where it is for [ʃ], but let the throat vibrate — the same sound as the s in television. Don't add an "oo" between the [p] and [l] at the start, and finish by curling the tongue for [ɚ].

examples.en: It's a pleasure to meet you.
examples.zh: 很高興認識你。

examples.en: Reading books gives me great pleasure.
examples.zh: 讀書帶給我很大的樂趣。

pleasure.spelling_en: -sure here is said [ʒɚ], not like the word sure.

police.tip_zh: police 的重音在第二音節 [lis]，跟 piece 押韻。常見錯誤是把第一音節唸重、唸飽滿，再在字尾多加母音，變成「波利斯」三個一樣清楚的音節。第一音節 [pə] 要非常短，幾乎一帶而過；第二音節 [lis] 的 [i] 拉長，舌尖碰上牙齦發 [l]，結尾 [s] 是清脆的嘶聲，後面不要加母音。
police.tip_en: police is stressed on the second syllable, [lis], and rhymes with piece. A common mistake is making the first syllable strong and full and adding a vowel at the end, so it becomes "po-li-si", three equally clear syllables. Make the first syllable [pə] very short, almost swallowed; stretch the [i] in [lis], touch the tongue tip to the gum ridge for [l], and end with a crisp hiss for [s], with no vowel after it.

examples.en: The police officer helped us find the way.
examples.zh: 警察幫我們找到了路。

examples.en: Call the police if you need help.
examples.zh: 需要幫忙時就打電話給警察。

police.spelling_zh: i 唸長音 [i]，字尾 ce 唸 [s]。
police.spelling_en: The i is a long [i]; the final ce is said [s].

popcorn.tip_zh: popcorn 是兩個音節 [pɑp·kɔrn]，重音在前面。常見錯誤是在第一個 [p] 後面多加母音，變成「趴普康」，或第二音節漏掉捲舌、結尾唸成 [ŋ]。第一音節發完 [p] 時雙唇閉著就好，不用爆開，直接接 [k]；第二音節嘴唇圓起來、舌頭往後捲發 [ɔr]，最後舌尖頂上牙齦收 [n]，跟 born 的結尾一樣。
popcorn.tip_en: popcorn has two syllables, [pɑp·kɔrn], stressed on the first. Common mistakes are adding a vowel after the first [p], making it "pa-pu-kang", and, in the second syllable, dropping the r-curl or ending with [ŋ]. After the first [p], just keep the lips closed — no need to pop them open — and go straight into [k]; for the second syllable, round the lips and curl the tongue back for [ɔr], then finish with the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n], the same ending as born.

examples.en: Let's eat popcorn and watch a movie.
examples.zh: 我們來吃爆米花、看電影吧。

examples.en: The popcorn smells so good!
examples.zh: 爆米花聞起來好香！

popular.tip_zh: popular 有三個音節，重音在第一音節 [pɑ]，開頭的 o 是嘴巴張大的 [ɑ]，不是圓唇的 [o]。常見錯誤是漏掉第二音節裡的 [j]，唸成「趴撲勒」。第二音節 [pjə] 雙唇閉合後，舌面立刻往上抬，帶出像 you 開頭的 [j]，再很快放鬆。結尾 [lɚ] 舌尖先碰上牙齦，再往後捲，不要停在「勒」。
popular.tip_en: popular has three syllables, stressed on the first, [pɑ]; the first o is the open [ɑ], not a round [o]. A common mistake is leaving out the [j] in the second syllable, saying "pa-pu-le". For the second syllable [pjə], after closing the lips, raise the middle of the tongue right away to make the [j] that starts you, then relax quickly. For the ending [lɚ], touch the tongue tip to the gum ridge, then curl it back — don't stop at "le".

examples.en: This song is very popular at our school.
examples.zh: 這首歌在我們學校很受歡迎。

examples.en: Bubble tea is popular with students.
examples.zh: 珍珠奶茶很受學生歡迎。

possible.tip_zh: possible 結尾的 [bḷ] 沒有母音，是最容易出錯的地方。常見錯誤是唸成「趴色波」，把 [bḷ] 唸成「波」，或多加母音再發清楚的 l。發完 [b] 後，舌尖直接頂住上牙齦、舌根往後抬，發出暗沉的 l，跟 table 的結尾一樣。開頭的 o 唸嘴巴張大的 [ɑ]，中間的 [sə] 輕輕帶過。
possible.tip_en: The ending [bḷ] of possible has no vowel, and it's the easiest place to go wrong. A common mistake is saying "pa-se-bo", turning [bḷ] into "bo", or adding a vowel and then a clear l. After [b], put the tongue tip straight onto the gum ridge and raise the back of the tongue for a dark l, the same ending as table. The first o is an open [ɑ], and the middle [sə] is quick and light.

examples.en: Is it possible to finish this today?
examples.zh: 今天有可能做完這個嗎？

examples.en: Please come home as soon as possible.
examples.zh: 請盡快回家。

probably.tip_zh: probably 的重音在第一音節 [prɑ]。常見錯誤是 [p] 和 [r] 中間加母音唸成「普拉」，或照拼字把 o 唸成「羅」，後面每個音節又唸得一樣重。發 [pr] 時，雙唇打開前舌頭就先捲好，嘴唇一張開就是 [r]，接著下巴張大發 [ɑ]，像 hot 的母音。中間的 [bə] 很輕，最後的 [blɪ] 乾脆收尾。
probably.tip_en: probably is stressed on the first syllable, [prɑ]. Common mistakes are adding a vowel between [p] and [r], like "pu-la", reading the o from the spelling as "luo", and giving every syllable after it equal weight. For [pr], curl the tongue before the lips open, so [r] comes out the moment they part; then drop the jaw for [ɑ], the vowel in hot. The middle [bə] is very light, and the final [blɪ] ends cleanly.

examples.en: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.
examples.zh: 明天大概會是晴天。

examples.en: Dad is probably still at work.
examples.zh: 爸爸可能還在上班。

probably.variant_zh: 口語說快時常縮成兩個音節 [ˈprɑblɪ]。
probably.variant_en: In quick, casual speech it is often shortened to two syllables, [ˈprɑblɪ].

purple.tip_zh: purple 和 people 只差第一個母音：purple 是捲舌的 [ɝ]，people 是 [i]。常見錯誤是唸成「趴波」，嘴巴張太大又沒有捲舌，結尾 [pḷ] 還多加一個「ㄛ」。第一音節舌頭往後捲、嘴唇微圓，像 her 的母音；接著雙唇閉合發 [p]，舌尖直接頂住上牙齦發暗 l，中間不要有母音。
purple.tip_en: purple and people differ only in the first vowel: purple has the r-colored [ɝ], people has [i]. A common mistake is saying "pa-bo", with the mouth too open and no tongue curl, plus an extra "o" on the final [pḷ]. For the first syllable, curl the tongue back and round the lips slightly, like the vowel in her; then close the lips for [p] and put the tongue tip straight onto the gum ridge for a dark l, with no vowel in between.

examples.en: My favorite color is purple.
examples.zh: 我最喜歡的顏色是紫色。

examples.en: She is wearing a purple dress today.
examples.zh: 她今天穿了一件紫色的洋裝。

question.tip_zh: question 開頭的 qu 唸 [kw]：發完 [k] 嘴唇要馬上圓起來帶出 [w]，不能只唸 [k]。中間的 [stʃ] 是一串子音：先發 [s] 的嘶聲，舌尖再頂上牙齦，放開成 chair 開頭的 [tʃ]。常見錯誤是漏掉 [t] 或 [s]，或把第二音節唸成響亮的「瓊」。第二音節 [tʃən] 要輕，結尾是舌尖音 [n]。
question.tip_en: The qu at the start of question is [kw]: right after [k], round the lips to add [w] — don't say [k] alone. The middle [stʃ] is a consonant cluster: hiss [s], then press the tongue tip on the gum ridge and release it into the [tʃ] that starts chair. Common mistakes are dropping the [t] or the [s], or making the second syllable a loud "chiong". Keep the second syllable [tʃən] light, ending with the tongue-tip [n].

examples.en: Can I ask you a question?
examples.zh: 我可以問你一個問題嗎？

examples.en: Raise your hand if you have a question.
examples.zh: 有問題的話請舉手。

quiz.tip_zh: quiz 只有一個音節 [kwɪz]，母音是短而放鬆的 [ɪ]，像 sit 的母音。常見錯誤是把 [ɪ] 拉長成 [i]，或字尾的 [z] 變成沒有聲音的 [s]，甚至多加一個母音，聽起來像「葵茲」。發 [z] 時舌尖靠近上牙齦，喉嚨持續震動，像蜜蜂的嗡嗡聲；這個結尾也是 quiz 和 quick 的差別所在。
quiz.tip_en: quiz has one syllable, [kwɪz], and its vowel is a short, relaxed [ɪ], as in sit. Common mistakes are stretching [ɪ] into [i], turning the final [z] into a voiceless [s], or adding a vowel after it so it sounds like "kwei-zu". For [z], hold the tongue tip near the gum ridge and keep the throat buzzing like a bee — that ending is also what separates quiz from quick.

examples.en: We have a spelling quiz on Monday.
examples.zh: 我們星期一有拼字小考。

examples.en: I got every answer right on the math quiz.
examples.zh: 數學小考我全部答對了。

rabbit.tip_zh: rabbit 開頭的 [r] 常被唸成 [l]，變成「萊比特」。發 [r] 時嘴唇微圓，舌尖往後捲但不碰上顎；接著下巴往下張大發 [æ]，跟 apple 的開頭一樣。第二音節 [bət] 很輕，母音短而模糊，不要唸成清楚的「比」；結尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上牙齦就停，不要再加「ㄜ」。可以用押韻的 habit 一起練。
rabbit.tip_en: The [r] at the start of rabbit is often turned into [l], so it sounds like "lai-bi-te". For [r], round the lips slightly and curl the tongue tip back without touching the roof of the mouth; then drop the jaw for [æ], as at the start of apple. The second syllable [bət] is very light, with a short, unclear vowel — not a clear "bee". For the final [t], touch the tongue tip to the gum ridge and stop, without adding "uh". Practice with the rhyme habit.

examples.en: Our class has a white rabbit.
examples.zh: 我們班上有一隻白兔。

examples.en: The rabbit is eating a carrot.
examples.zh: 兔子正在吃紅蘿蔔。

radio.tip_zh: radio 的第一個字母 a 要唸 [e]，跟 day 的母音一樣，嘴型從 [e] 往 [ɪ] 滑。常見錯誤是照拼字唸成「拉迪歐」，用了嘴巴大開的 [ɑ]，或把開頭的 [r] 唸成 [l]。三個音節中重音在第一音節 [re]，中間的 [dɪ] 短而輕，最後的 [o] 嘴唇收圓。開頭的 [r] 嘴唇先微微噘起，舌頭捲起、不碰上顎。
radio.tip_en: The first letter, a, in radio is said [e], the vowel in day, gliding from [e] toward [ɪ]. A common mistake is reading it as "la-di-o" with a wide-open [ɑ], or turning the opening [r] into [l]. Of the three syllables, the first, [re], is stressed; the middle [dɪ] is short and light, and the lips round for the final [o]. For the opening [r], push the lips forward a little and curl the tongue without touching the roof of the mouth.

examples.en: Grandpa listens to the radio every morning.
examples.zh: 爺爺每天早上聽收音機。

examples.en: Can you turn on the radio, please?
examples.zh: 可以請你打開收音機嗎？

radio.spelling_zh: a 在這裡唸 [e]，像 day，不唸 [æ]。
radio.spelling_en: The a here is said [e], as in day, not [æ].

rain.tip_zh: rain 開頭的 [r] 和結尾的 [n] 都要注意。常見錯誤是開頭唸成 [l]，像「雷恩」，或結尾變成後鼻音 [ŋ]。開頭嘴唇微圓、舌尖往後捲不碰上顎；中間的 [e] 從 day 的母音往 [ɪ] 滑；最後舌尖頂住上牙齦收 [n]。rain 和 train、main 押韻；如果母音唸成 [ʌ]，就變成 run 了。
