rain.tip_en: Watch both the [r] at the start of rain and the [n] at the end. Common mistakes are starting with [l], like "lei-en", or ending with the back nasal [ŋ]. At the start, round the lips slightly and curl the tongue tip back without touching the roof of the mouth; the vowel [e] glides from the vowel in day toward [ɪ]; finish with the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n]. rain rhymes with train and main; if the vowel becomes [ʌ], it turns into run.

examples.en: Take an umbrella. It might rain later.
examples.zh: 帶把傘吧，等一下可能會下雨。

examples.en: The kids love to play in the rain.
examples.zh: 孩子們很喜歡在雨中玩。

refrigerator.tip_zh: refrigerator 共有五個音節，重音在第二音節 [frɪ]。學生常把開頭 re 唸成又長又重的 [ri]，或把中間的 [dʒə] 吞掉，只剩四拍。修正：開頭 [rə] 輕輕帶過，[frɪ] 用力，接著 [dʒə] 嘴唇微噘、輕輕帶過，最後的 [retɚ] 和 later 押韻。
refrigerator.tip_en: refrigerator has five syllables, with the stress on the second syllable [frɪ]. Learners often say the opening re as a long, heavy [ri], or swallow the middle [dʒə] so only four beats are left. Fix: let the opening [rə] pass lightly, push on [frɪ], then say [dʒə] with the lips slightly rounded and pass over it lightly; the final [retɚ] rhymes with later.

examples.en: Please put the milk back in the refrigerator.
examples.zh: 請把牛奶放回冰箱。

examples.en: Our refrigerator is full of fruit and vegetables.
examples.zh: 我們的冰箱裝滿了水果和蔬菜。

refrigerator.spelling_zh: 簡稱 fridge 有 d，但 refrigerator 本身沒有 d
refrigerator.spelling_en: The short form fridge has a d, but refrigerator itself does not.

relative.tip_zh: relative 重音在第一音節 [rɛ]，母音是短的 [ɛ]，不是 [i]；看到 re 開頭就唸成 [ri] 是典型的錯誤。中間 [lə] 要輕而短。結尾 [v] 要上齒輕碰下唇、聲帶振動，學生常唸成無聲的 [f]，或在後面多加一個母音。可以先練 give 的結尾 [ɪv]，再接上去。
relative.tip_en: relative is stressed on the first syllable [rɛ], and the vowel is a short [ɛ], not [i]; reading the re- at the start as [ri] is a typical mistake. The middle [lə] should be light and short. For the final [v], rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and keep the voice buzzing; learners often turn it into a voiceless [f] or add an extra vowel after it. Practice the [ɪv] ending of give first, then attach it.

examples.en: My favorite relative is my aunt in Taichung.
examples.zh: 我最喜歡的親戚是住在台中的阿姨。

examples.en: Is that boy your relative or your classmate?
examples.zh: 那個男生是你的親戚還是你的同學？

remember.tip_zh: remember 重音在第二音節 [mɛm]，不在開頭的 [rɪ]。[mɛm] 唸完時雙唇要確實閉住，再直接打開成 [b]，中間不要多塞一個母音。結尾 [bɚ] 要捲舌，不要唸成平平的 [bə]。其實 remember 就是輕的 [rɪ] 加上 member，先把 member 唸熟再加字首。
remember.tip_en: remember is stressed on the second syllable [mɛm], not on the opening [rɪ]. At the end of [mɛm] the lips must close fully, then open straight into [b], with no extra vowel squeezed in between. The ending [bɚ] needs a curled tongue; don't flatten it to [bə]. In fact remember is just a light [rɪ] plus member, so get member smooth first, then add the prefix.

examples.en: Do you remember my phone number?
examples.zh: 你記得我的電話號碼嗎？

examples.en: Remember to bring your homework tomorrow.
examples.zh: 記得明天要帶你的作業。

reporter.tip_zh: reporter 重音在第二音節 [pɔr]。[ɔ] 後面要接捲舌的 [r]，學生常把這個 [r] 省掉，唸成 [rɪˈpɔtɚ]；接著結尾 [tɚ] 還要再捲一次舌。練法：先慢慢唸 [pɔr]，舌尖往後捲住不放，再接 [tɚ]，最後在前面輕輕加上 [rɪ]。結尾可以跟 quarter 一起練。
reporter.tip_en: reporter is stressed on the second syllable [pɔr]. After [ɔ] there must be a curled [r]; learners often leave it out and say [rɪˈpɔtɚ], and then the ending [tɚ] needs the tongue curled a second time. Practice: say [pɔr] slowly, keep the tongue tip curled back, then add [tɚ], and finally put a light [rɪ] in front. Practice the ending together with quarter.

examples.en: The reporter asked the mayor three questions.
examples.zh: 記者問了市長三個問題。

examples.en: My cousin wants to be a TV reporter.
examples.zh: 我表哥想當電視記者。

restaurant.tip_zh: restaurant 重音在第一音節 [rɛs]，後面兩拍都輕。學生常照拼字把結尾 rant 唸成 [rænt]，或把重音移到最後。KK 的結尾是 [rɑnt]，其中 [ɑnt] 和 want 押韻：嘴巴張開唸 [ɑ]，再收 [n] 和 [t]。[t] 只要舌尖碰上齒齦停住，不要多唸一個母音。中間的 [tə] 輕輕帶過。
restaurant.tip_en: restaurant is stressed on the first syllable [rɛs]; the two beats after it are light. Learners often follow the spelling and say the ending rant as [rænt], or move the stress to the end. In the KK the ending is [rɑnt], whose [ɑnt] rhymes with want: open the mouth for [ɑ], then close with [n] and [t]. For [t] just touch the tongue tip to the gum ridge and stop; don't add a vowel. The middle [tə] is a light beat.

examples.en: Let's eat dinner at the new restaurant tonight.
examples.zh: 我們今晚去那家新餐廳吃晚餐吧。

examples.en: This restaurant makes the best noodles in town.
examples.zh: 這家餐廳的麵是鎮上最好吃的。

restaurant.variant_en: Often shortened to two syllables in speech: [ˈrɛstrɑnt].
restaurant.spelling_zh: 中間的 au 不唸 [ɔ]，只是很輕的 [ə]
restaurant.spelling_en: The au in the middle is not [ɔ]; it is only a light [ə].

river.tip_zh: river 開頭的 [r] 舌尖不要碰到上顎，嘴唇微圓；後面的 [ɪ] 短而放鬆，不要拉長成 [i]。第二音節的 [v] 要上齒輕碰下唇、聲帶振動，學生常唸成 [w] 或 [b]。練法：唸完 [rɪ] 就把上齒放到下唇上，從 [v] 滑進捲舌的 [ɚ]，像 never 的後半段。
river.tip_en: For the opening [r] of river, keep the tongue tip off the roof of the mouth and round the lips a little; the [ɪ] after it is short and relaxed, so don't stretch it into [i]. The [v] of the second syllable needs the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip with the voice buzzing; learners often say [w] or [b] instead. Practice: right after [rɪ], put the upper teeth on the lower lip and slide from [v] into the curled [ɚ], like the second half of never.

examples.en: We had a picnic by the river.
examples.zh: 我們在河邊野餐。

examples.en: Ducks are swimming in the river.
examples.zh: 鴨子在河裡游泳。

salad.tip_zh: 中文說「沙拉」，學生容易直接照唸：第一音節變成 [sɑ]，結尾的 [d] 也不見了。英文第一音節 [sæ] 要嘴角往兩旁拉、下巴往下放，像 apple 的開頭；第二音節 [ləd] 輕而短，最後舌尖頂住上齒齦停在 [d]，不要再多加一個母音。
salad.tip_en: Because Chinese says 「沙拉」, learners tend to read it the same way: the first syllable becomes [sɑ] and the final [d] disappears. In English the first syllable [sæ] needs the lip corners pulled sideways and the jaw dropped, like the start of apple; the second syllable [ləd] is light and short, ending with the tongue tip pressed on the gum ridge to stop at [d]. Don't add another vowel.

examples.en: I want a chicken salad for lunch.
examples.zh: 我午餐想吃雞肉沙拉。

examples.en: Mom made a big fruit salad for the party.
examples.zh: 媽媽為派對做了一大盆水果沙拉。

sandwich.tip_zh: 中文的「三明治」會讓學生把 [sæn] 唸成平平的 [sɑn]。[æ] 要嘴巴張大、嘴角往兩旁拉。第二音節 [wɪtʃ] 和 which 同音，[ɪ] 短而放鬆。結尾 [tʃ] 是無聲的，嘴唇微噘送氣就好，學生常在後面多加一個母音。中間的 [d] 輕輕帶過即可，美國人口語甚至常省略。
sandwich.tip_en: The Chinese word 「三明治」 leads learners to flatten [sæn] into [sɑn]. For [æ], open the mouth wide and pull the lip corners sideways. The second syllable [wɪtʃ] sounds the same as which, with a short, relaxed [ɪ]. The final [tʃ] is voiceless: just push the lips forward slightly and release air; learners often add a vowel after it. The [d] in the middle only needs a light touch, and Americans often drop it in everyday speech.

examples.en: I made a ham and egg sandwich for breakfast.
examples.zh: 我早餐做了一個火腿蛋三明治。

examples.en: Can I have half of your sandwich?
examples.zh: 可以分我一半你的三明治嗎？

sandwich.variant_zh: 口語常省略 d，唸成 [ˈsænwɪtʃ] 或 [ˈsæmwɪtʃ]
sandwich.variant_en: In speech the d is often dropped: [ˈsænwɪtʃ] or [ˈsæmwɪtʃ].

saturday.tip_zh: Saturday 重音在第一音節 [sæ]，嘴巴要張大。學生常照拼字把中間的 tur 唸得又重又長，其實 [tɚ] 只是輕輕一拍的捲舌音；最後的 day 也不要唸得像單字 day 那麼用力，KK 標的是輕的 [dɪ]。整個字的節奏是「重、輕、輕」，三拍裡只有第一拍用力。
saturday.tip_en: Saturday is stressed on the first syllable [sæ], with the mouth open wide. Learners often follow the spelling and make the middle tur heavy and long, but [tɚ] is just one light, curled beat; and the final day should not be as strong as the word day on its own, since the KK marks it as a light [dɪ]. The rhythm of the whole word is 'strong, light, light': only the first of the three beats is pushed.

examples.en: We go swimming every Saturday morning.
examples.zh: 我們每個星期六早上都去游泳。

examples.en: My birthday party is on Saturday.
examples.zh: 我的生日派對在星期六。

school.tip_zh: school 只有一個音節。學生常在 [s] 和 [k] 之間多加一個母音，唸成兩拍；也常把結尾的 [l] 省掉，只剩 [sku]。修正：[s] 直接接 [k]，而且 s 後面的 [k] 不送氣，聽起來接近 [g]；[u] 唸完後舌尖往上頂住上齒齦，發出暗 L，就像 cool 的結尾一樣。
school.tip_en: school has only one syllable. Learners often add a vowel between [s] and [k], making two beats, and often drop the final [l], leaving just [sku]. Fix: go straight from [s] into [k], and a [k] after s has no puff of air, so it sounds close to [g]; after [u], raise the tongue tip to the gum ridge to make a dark L, just like the end of cool.

examples.en: I walk to school with my sister.
examples.zh: 我和姊姊一起走路上學。

examples.en: Our school has a big library.
examples.zh: 我們學校有一間很大的圖書館。

school.spelling_zh: ch 在這裡唸 [k]，h 不發音
school.spelling_en: Here ch sounds like [k]; the h is silent.

science.tip_zh: science 有兩個音節：重的 [saɪ] 加上很輕的 [əns]。學生常把它擠成一拍，或漏掉 [n]，唸成 [ˈsaɪəs]；也常在字尾 [ns] 後面多加一個母音。修正：唸 [n] 時舌尖已經頂在上齒齦，舌頭保持不動，直接送出 [s] 的氣就收尾，不要再張嘴發出母音。
science.tip_en: science has two syllables: a strong [saɪ] plus a very light [əns]. Learners often squeeze it into one beat, or drop the [n] and say [ˈsaɪəs]; they also often add a vowel after the final [ns]. Fix: when you say [n] the tongue tip is already on the gum ridge, so keep the tongue still, push out the [s] air and stop there, without opening the mouth for another vowel.

examples.en: Science is my favorite subject at school.
examples.zh: 自然科學是我在學校最喜歡的科目。

examples.en: We did a fun science project about plants.
examples.zh: 我們做了一個關於植物的有趣科學專題。

science.spelling_zh: 開頭 sc 只唸一個 [s]，c 不發音
science.spelling_en: The opening sc makes just one [s]; the c is silent.

secretary.tip_zh: secretary 看起來是 secret 加 ary，但開頭母音不同：secret 是 [i]，secretary 是短的 [ɛ]，要唸 [sɛk]。重音在第一音節，第二音節 [rə] 很輕，第三音節 [tɛ] 稍微用力一點，最後 [rɪ] 和 very 的結尾一樣。美式要唸滿四拍，不要吞成三拍。
secretary.tip_en: secretary looks like secret plus ary, but the first vowel is different: secret has [i], while secretary has a short [ɛ], so say [sɛk]. The stress is on the first syllable; the second syllable [rə] is very light, the third syllable [tɛ] gets a little more push, and the final [rɪ] is the same as the end of very. American English says all four beats; don't squash it into three.

examples.en: The school secretary answered the phone.
examples.zh: 學校的秘書接了電話。

examples.en: My aunt works as a secretary in an office.
examples.zh: 我阿姨在一間辦公室當秘書。

see.tip_zh: 中文沒有「ㄙ＋ㄧ」這個組合，學生常把 see 唸成「西」：舌面抬高，聽起來偏向 she [ʃi]。修正：發 [s] 時舌面放平、舌尖靠近上排牙齒後方，嘴角往兩旁拉，發出細細的嘶聲，再接拉長的 [i]。可以對照練 see 和 she，也要讓 [i] 的嘴角保持拉緊，別滑成 say [se]。
see.tip_en: Mandarin has no ㄙ+ㄧ combination, so learners often say see like 「西」: the body of the tongue rises and it drifts toward she [ʃi]. Fix: for [s], keep the tongue flat with the tip near the back of the upper teeth and the lip corners pulled sideways, making a thin hiss, then add a long [i]. Practice see and she side by side, and keep the lip corners tight on [i] so it doesn't slide into say [se].

examples.en: Can you see the bird in the tree?
examples.zh: 你看得到樹上的那隻鳥嗎？

examples.en: I'm so happy to see you again!
examples.zh: 好高興再見到你！

september.tip_zh: September 重音在第二音節 [tɛm]，學生常把第一音節 [sɛp] 唸得最重。[sɛp] 的 [p] 只要雙唇閉上，不要放出母音，直接接 [tɛm]，否則會多出一拍。[tɛm] 和 [bɚ] 之間雙唇保持閉合，從 [m] 順勢推出 [b]。結尾和 November、December 一樣要捲舌。
september.tip_en: September is stressed on the second syllable [tɛm]; learners often make the first syllable [sɛp] the strongest. For the [p] in [sɛp], just close the lips without releasing a vowel and go straight into [tɛm], or an extra beat appears. Between [tɛm] and [bɚ] keep the lips closed and push from [m] straight into [b]. The ending is curled, just like November and December.

examples.en: The new school year starts in September.
examples.zh: 新學年在九月開始。

examples.en: My brother's birthday is in September.
examples.zh: 我哥哥的生日在九月。

serious.tip_zh: serious 有三個音節，重音在第一音節 [sɪ]。開頭 [s] 後面是放鬆的短音 [ɪ]，接著舌頭立刻捲成 [r]。學生常照拼字把 ser 唸成 service 開頭那樣的 [sɝ]，變成 [ˈsɝɪəs]。結尾的 ious 只唸輕的 [ɪəs]，兩個母音滑過去即可，不要每個字母都用力唸出來。
serious.tip_en: serious has three syllables, with the stress on the first syllable [sɪ]. After the opening [s] comes a short, relaxed [ɪ], and then the tongue curls straight into [r]. Learners often follow the spelling and say ser like the [sɝ] at the start of service, giving [ˈsɝɪəs]. The ending ious is just a light [ɪəs]: glide through the two vowels and don't push out every letter.

examples.en: Don't worry, it's not a serious problem.
examples.zh: 別擔心，這不是什麼嚴重的問題。

examples.en: Why do you look so serious today?
examples.zh: 你今天為什麼看起來這麼嚴肅？

service.tip_zh: service 重音在第一音節 [sɝ]，這是捲舌的長母音：舌頭往後捲、嘴唇微圓，跟 sir 的母音一樣，不要唸成沒有捲舌的 [sʌ]。第二音節的 [v] 要上齒碰下唇並振動聲帶，學生常唸成 [w] 或 [b]。結尾很輕，只有 [vəs]，不要照拼字唸成 [vaɪs]。
service.tip_en: service is stressed on the first syllable [sɝ], a long curled vowel: pull the tongue back and curl it, round the lips slightly (the same vowel as sir), and don't flatten it into an uncurled [sʌ]. The [v] of the second syllable needs the upper teeth on the lower lip with the voice buzzing; learners often say [w] or [b]. The ending is very light, just [vəs]; don't follow the spelling and say [vaɪs].

examples.en: The service at this restaurant is very good.
examples.zh: 這家餐廳的服務很好。

examples.en: Our school has a bus service for students.
examples.zh: 我們學校有提供學生搭乘的校車服務。

service.spelling_zh: 字尾的 ice 不唸 [aɪs]，只唸輕的 [əs]
service.spelling_en: The final -ice is not [aɪs]; it is just a light [əs].

seven.tip_zh: seven 的 [v] 夾在兩個母音中間，學生常偷懶唸成 [b] 或 [f]，變成 [ˈsɛbən]。修正：唸完 [sɛ]，上齒輕輕放到下唇，讓聲帶振動，再滑到 [ən]。結尾是舌尖頂上齒齦的 [n]，不是舌根的 [ŋ]，所以舌尖最後要碰到上排牙齒後方。可以跟 eleven 的結尾 [vən] 一起練。
seven.tip_en: The [v] in seven sits between two vowels, and learners often take a shortcut and say [b] or [f], giving [ˈsɛbən]. Fix: after [sɛ], rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip, keep the voice buzzing, then slide into [ən]. The ending is [n] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge, not [ŋ] at the back of the tongue, so the tongue tip must finish just behind the upper teeth. Practice it together with the [vən] ending of eleven.

examples.en: My little brother is seven years old.
examples.zh: 我弟弟七歲。

examples.en: We eat breakfast at seven every morning.
examples.zh: 我們每天早上七點吃早餐。

seventeen.tip_zh: seventeen 和 seventy 很容易聽錯，差別在最後一拍。seventeen 結尾的 [tin] 要唸清楚、拉長：[t] 送氣，母音是長的 [i]，最後舌尖頂住上齒齦收 [n]。單獨數數時 [tin] 也是重音。seventy 的結尾則是短而輕的 [tɪ]，沒有 [n]。中間 [vən] 的 [v] 別忘了上齒碰下唇。
seventeen.tip_en: seventeen and seventy are easy to mix up; the difference is in the last beat. The [tin] at the end of seventeen must be clear and long: aspirate the [t], make the vowel a long [i], and finish with the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n]. When counting on its own, [tin] is stressed too. seventy ends in a short, light [tɪ] with no [n]. In the middle [vən], don't forget the upper teeth on the lower lip for [v].

examples.en: My cousin is seventeen years old.
examples.zh: 我表姊十七歲。

examples.en: There are seventeen students in our class.
examples.zh: 我們班上有十七個學生。

seventy.tip_zh: seventy 重音在第一音節 [sɛ]，後面兩拍 [vən] 和 [tɪ] 都要輕而短。學生常把重音移到結尾 ty，或把 [tɪ] 拉成長音 [i]，結果聽起來像 seventeen。修正：用力唸 [sɛ]，[v] 上齒碰下唇，最後 [tɪ] 短短帶過、嘴巴放鬆，而且字尾沒有 [n]。
seventy.tip_en: seventy is stressed on the first syllable [sɛ]; the two beats after it, [vən] and [tɪ], are light and short. Learners often move the stress to the ending ty or stretch the vowel of [tɪ] into a long [i], so it sounds like seventeen. Fix: push hard on [sɛ], put the upper teeth on the lower lip for [v], and let the final [tɪ] pass quickly with a relaxed mouth; there is no [n] at the end.

examples.en: My grandpa is seventy years old.
examples.zh: 我爺爺七十歲。

examples.en: This storybook has seventy pages.
examples.zh: 這本故事書有七十頁。

seventy.variant_zh: 口語中 [n] 後面的 [t] 常弱化，聽起來像 [ˈsɛvənɪ]
seventy.variant_en: In casual speech the [t] after [n] often fades, so it sounds like [ˈsɛvənɪ].

several.tip_zh: several 重音在第一音節 [sɛv]。[v] 要上齒輕咬下唇並振動，學生常唸成 [b]；接著直接滑進 [r]，中間不必塞一個清楚的母音。最容易出錯的是結尾：[rəl] 的暗 L 常被省略或唸成 [o]，要在最後讓舌尖頂住上齒齦，舌根同時往後抬，聲音才會飽滿。
several.tip_en: several is stressed on the first syllable [sɛv]. For [v], bite the lower lip lightly with the upper teeth and keep it buzzing; learners often say [b]. Then slide directly into [r] without inserting a clear vowel. The ending is where it most often goes wrong: the dark L in [rəl] gets dropped or turned into [o]. Finish with the tongue tip on the gum ridge while the back of the tongue lifts, so the sound is full.

examples.en: I have several good friends in my class.
examples.zh: 我在班上有幾個好朋友。

examples.en: We waited at the bus stop for several minutes.
examples.zh: 我們在公車站等了幾分鐘。

several.variant_en: Also often said with three syllables: [ˈsɛvɚəl].

sheep.tip_zh: sheep 和 ship 只差在母音：sheep 是長而緊的 [i]，嘴角往兩旁拉、像在微笑，可以稍微拉長；ship 則是短而放鬆的 [ɪ]。學生常把兩個字唸成一樣。開頭 [ʃ] 嘴唇往前噘，不要讓舌頭先碰上顎變成 [tʃ]，否則就成了 cheap。結尾 [p] 雙唇閉上即可，不要再加母音。
sheep.tip_en: sheep and ship differ only in the vowel: sheep has a long, tense [i] (pull the lip corners sideways as if smiling and hold it a little longer), while ship has a short, relaxed [ɪ]. Learners often say both words the same way. For the opening [ʃ], push the lips forward and don't let the tongue touch the roof of the mouth first, or it becomes [tʃ] and turns into cheap. For the final [p], just close the lips; don't add a vowel.

examples.en: There are many sheep on the farm.
examples.zh: 農場上有很多綿羊。

examples.en: The little sheep has soft white wool.
examples.zh: 那隻小綿羊有柔軟的白色羊毛。

shopkeeper.tip_zh: shopkeeper 是 shop 加 keeper，重音在前面的 [ʃɑp]，keeper 只帶次重音。美式的 [ɑ] 下巴要往下放、嘴巴張大，不要唸成圓唇的 [o]。中間是最大的關卡：[p] 和 [k] 連在一起，學生常在 [p] 後面多加一個母音，變成四拍。修正：[p] 雙唇閉上但不放氣，直接接 [k]。
shopkeeper.tip_en: shopkeeper is shop plus keeper; the main stress is on the first part [ʃɑp], and keeper only gets secondary stress. For the American [ɑ], drop the jaw and open the mouth wide; don't make it a rounded [o]. The middle is the biggest hurdle: [p] and [k] sit together, and learners often add a vowel after [p], making four beats. Fix: close the lips for [p] without releasing the air, and go straight into [k].

examples.en: The shopkeeper gave me a small gift.
examples.zh: 店主送我一個小禮物。

examples.en: Our neighbor is a friendly shopkeeper.
examples.zh: 我們的鄰居是一位親切的店主。

singer.tip_zh: singer 的 ng 只唸一個 [ŋ]，沒有 [g]。學生常照 finger 的唸法多加 [g]，或把 [ŋ] 唸成 [n]。修正：唸 [sɪŋ] 時舌根抬起貼住軟顎，讓聲音從鼻子出來，然後舌根直接放開，滑進捲舌的 [ɚ]，中間不要有爆破的 [g]。可以想成 sing 後面加上 [ɚ]。
singer.tip_en: The ng in singer is just one [ŋ], with no [g]. Learners often add a [g] the way finger has one, or turn [ŋ] into [n]. Fix: for [sɪŋ], lift the back of the tongue against the soft palate so the sound comes out through the nose, then release the tongue straight into the curled [ɚ], with no [g] burst in between. Think of it as sing plus [ɚ].

examples.en: My sister wants to be a singer.
examples.zh: 我妹妹想當歌手。

examples.en: The singer sang my favorite song.
examples.zh: 那位歌手唱了我最喜歡的歌。

singer.spelling_zh: ng 只唸 [ŋ]，g 不另外發音（finger 才有 [g]）
singer.spelling_en: ng is just [ŋ]; the g is not said separately (finger does have [g]).

something.tip_zh: something 的難點在 [m] 接 [θ]：唸完 [sʌm] 雙唇是閉著的，要立刻張開，把舌尖輕放在上下齒之間吹氣。學生常省事唸成 [s]，變成 [ˈsʌmsɪŋ]。開頭的 [ʌ] 嘴巴半開、短促放鬆，不要唸成 [ɑ]。結尾 [ɪŋ] 用舌根收鼻音，不要唸成 [ɪn]。
something.tip_en: The hard part of something is [m] followed by [θ]: after [sʌm] the lips are closed, so open them right away and rest the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower teeth to blow air. Learners often take the easy way and say [s], giving [ˈsʌmsɪŋ]. The opening [ʌ] is half-open, short and relaxed; don't make it [ɑ]. The ending [ɪŋ] closes with the back of the tongue for the nasal; don't say [ɪn].

examples.en: I have something special for you.
examples.zh: 我有個特別的東西要給你。

examples.en: Do you want something to drink?
examples.zh: 你想喝點什麼嗎？

sometimes.tip_zh: sometimes 的結尾是 [aɪmz]：雙唇先閉上發 [m]，再讓聲帶繼續振動送出 [z]。學生常把字尾唸成無聲的 [s]，或在 [m] 後面多加一個母音，變成三拍。另外 some 和 times 之間的 [m] 要閉唇，直接接 [t]，不要停頓。可以先練 time，再加上會振動的 [z]。
sometimes.tip_en: sometimes ends in [aɪmz]: close the lips for [m] first, then keep the voice buzzing to push out [z]. Learners often turn the final sound into a voiceless [s], or add a vowel after [m], making three beats. Also, the [m] between some and times needs closed lips, going straight into [t] without a pause. Practice time first, then add a buzzing [z].

examples.en: Sometimes I ride my bike to school.
examples.zh: 我有時候騎腳踏車上學。

examples.en: My dad sometimes cooks dinner for us.
examples.zh: 我爸爸有時候會煮晚餐給我們吃。

sometimes.variant_zh: 也有人把 some 唸輕、重音放在後面：[səmˈtaɪmz]
sometimes.variant_en: Some speakers make some light and stress the second part: [səmˈtaɪmz].
sometimes.kk_flag: Given KK [səmˈtaɪmz] stresses the 2nd syllable with a weak [səm]; most US dictionaries list [ˈsʌmˌtaɪmz] (1st-syllable stress) first, and it is the more common General American form. Consider making it the main KK.

sorry.tip_zh: 第一音節 [sɑ] 的 [ɑ] 要把下巴放低、嘴巴張大，嘴唇不要圓；常見錯誤是嘟起嘴唇唸成 [so]，聽起來像 so 再加上 ry。接著舌尖往後捲發 [r]，舌頭不碰上顎，不要變成注音的ㄌ。重音在第一音節，字尾 [rɪ] 輕而短，不用拉長。
sorry.tip_en: In the first syllable [sɑ], drop the jaw and open the mouth wide for [ɑ], without rounding the lips; a common mistake is rounding the lips into [so], so it sounds like so plus ry. Then curl the tongue tip back for [r] without touching the roof of the mouth; don't turn it into Mandarin ㄌ. The stress is on the first syllable; the ending [rɪ] is light and short, not drawn out.

examples.en: Sorry, I forgot my homework today.
examples.zh: 對不起，我今天忘了帶作業。

examples.en: I'm sorry I was late for class.
examples.zh: 對不起，我上課遲到了。

sorry.variant_zh: 部分美國人唸成 [ˈsɔrɪ]，也是正確的。
sorry.variant_en: Some Americans say [ˈsɔrɪ]; that is also correct.

sound.tip_zh: 母音 [aʊ] 是滑動的雙母音：從嘴巴張大的 [a] 開始，再把嘴唇收圓滑向 [ʊ]，不能唸成扁平的單一母音。字尾 [nd] 兩個子音連在一起，學生常把 [d] 吞掉只剩 [saʊn]，或在後面多加母音唸成「桑的」。舌尖頂住上排牙齦發完 [n] 後，原地輕輕放開就是 [d]，不要再加母音。
sound.tip_en: The vowel [aʊ] is a gliding diphthong: start with a wide-open [a], then round the lips and slide toward [ʊ]; it can't be one flat vowel. The ending [nd] is two consonants together; learners often swallow the [d], leaving only [saʊn], or add a vowel and say something like 'sahng-duh'. After [n], with the tongue tip pressed on the upper gum ridge, simply release it in place and that is [d]; add no vowel.

examples.en: Can you hear the sound of the bell?
examples.zh: 你聽得到鐘聲嗎？

examples.en: Please turn down the sound on the TV.
examples.zh: 請把電視的聲音調小。

still.tip_zh: 開頭 [st] 兩個子音直接相連，不要在 [s] 後面多加母音，唸成「斯提歐」那樣的三拍；而且 [s] 後面的 [t] 不送氣，聽起來有點接近 [d]。母音 [ɪ] 短而放鬆，拉長成 [i] 就會變成 steal（偷）。字尾是暗 L：舌尖頂住上排牙齦，舌根同時往後抬，不要唸成「歐」或乾脆省略。
still.tip_en: The opening [st] is two consonants joined directly; don't add a vowel after [s] and turn it into three beats like 'si-ti-ou'. Also, the [t] after [s] has no puff of air, so it sounds a bit like [d]. The vowel [ɪ] is short and relaxed; stretch it into [i] and it becomes steal. The ending is a dark L: press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge while raising the back of the tongue; don't say it as an 'ou' sound or leave it out.

examples.en: I am still hungry after lunch.
examples.zh: 吃完午餐我還是很餓。

examples.en: Is your little brother still asleep?
examples.zh: 你弟弟還在睡嗎？

strawberry.tip_zh: 開頭 [str] 是三個子音連發，學生常在中間塞母音，唸成「斯特饒」好幾拍。練習時先拉長 [s]，再一口氣滑到 [tr]，[t] 和 [r] 黏在一起，嘴唇在發 [t] 時就先嘟起來。[ɔ] 下巴放低、嘴唇略圓。重音在第一音節 [strɔ]，後面的 [bɛrɪ] 較輕，不要把 berry 唸得比 straw 還重。
strawberry.tip_en: The opening [str] is three consonants in a row; learners often squeeze vowels in between and say several beats like 'si-te-rao'. To practice, stretch the [s], then glide straight into [tr] in one breath with [t] and [r] stuck together, rounding the lips already on [t]. For [ɔ], lower the jaw and round the lips slightly. The stress is on the first syllable [strɔ]; the following [bɛrɪ] is lighter, so don't say berry louder than straw.

examples.en: Mom made a strawberry cake for my birthday.
examples.zh: 媽媽為我的生日做了草莓蛋糕。

examples.en: This strawberry is big and sweet.
examples.zh: 這顆草莓又大又甜。

student.tip_zh: 美式第一音節是 [stu]，不要在 [t] 和 [u] 之間多加 [j] 唸成英式的 [stju]；[s] 後面的 [t] 也不送氣。第二音節 [dṇt] 中間沒有母音：舌尖發完 [d] 後留在上排牙齦不動，讓氣直接從鼻子出來變成 [ṇ]，最後舌尖停住收 [t]。常見錯誤是唸成清楚的「登」再加「特」。
student.tip_en: In American English the first syllable is [stu]; don't add [j] between [t] and [u] as in British [stju]. The [t] after [s] also has no puff of air. The second syllable [dṇt] has no vowel: after [d], keep the tongue tip still on the upper gum ridge and let the air go straight out through the nose for [ṇ], then stop the tongue there for [t]. A common mistake is saying a clear 'deng' followed by 'te'.

examples.en: She is a new student in our class.
examples.zh: 她是我們班的新同學。

examples.en: Every student gets a book today.
examples.zh: 今天每位學生都會拿到一本書。

successful.tip_zh: 重音在第二音節 [sɛs]，學生常把第一音節唸重。開頭 [sək] 要輕又短，[k] 發完馬上接 [s]，拼字的 cc 正是 [ks] 兩個音，[k] 不能吞掉。字尾 -ful 是 [fḷ]：上排牙齒碰下唇發 [f] 後，舌尖直接頂到上排牙齦發暗 L，中間沒有母音，不要唸成「佛」或省略 l。
successful.tip_en: The stress is on the second syllable [sɛs]; learners often stress the first. The opening [sək] is light and short, and [k] goes straight into [s]: the spelling cc is exactly the two sounds [ks], so don't swallow the [k]. The ending -ful is [fḷ]: after the upper teeth touch the lower lip for [f], the tongue tip goes straight up to the upper gum ridge for a dark L, with no vowel between; don't say it as 'fo' or drop the l.

examples.en: Our school play was very successful.
examples.zh: 我們學校的話劇非常成功。

examples.en: She worked hard and became a successful doctor.
examples.zh: 她很努力，成為一位成功的醫生。

successful.spelling_zh: cc 唸 [ks]；字尾 -ful 只有一個 l。
successful.spelling_en: cc is said [ks]; the ending -ful has only one l.

supermarket.tip_zh: 這個字有兩個捲舌音：[pɚ] 和 [mɑr]。學生常把 super 唸成沒有捲舌的「蘇趴」，mar 唸成「媽」，聽起來像英式。[pɚ] 舌頭往後捲、嘴巴半開；[mɑr] 先張大嘴發 [ɑ]，再把舌尖往後捲。重音在第一音節 [su]，最後的 [kɪt] 又輕又短，母音是 [ɪ] 不是 [ɛ]，字尾 [t] 輕輕停住，不要加「特」。
supermarket.tip_en: This word has two r-colored sounds: [pɚ] and [mɑr]. Learners often say super as an un-curled 'su-pa' and mar as 'ma', which sounds British. For [pɚ], curl the tongue back with the mouth half open; for [mɑr], open wide for [ɑ] first, then curl the tongue tip back. The stress is on the first syllable [su]; the last part [kɪt] is light and short, its vowel is [ɪ], not [ɛ], and the final [t] just stops, without an added 'te'.

examples.en: We buy milk at the supermarket.
examples.zh: 我們在超市買牛奶。

examples.en: The supermarket near my home opens at eight.
examples.zh: 我家附近的超市八點開門。

surprise.tip_zh: 重音在第二音節 [praɪz]，學生常把第一音節 sur 唸得又重又長。[sɚ] 要輕、快，舌頭微捲就好。[pr] 之間不要加母音，嘴唇發 [p] 時就先嘟起來準備 [r]。字尾的 s 其實是有聲的 [z]，喉嚨要像蜜蜂一樣嗡嗡震動，唸成 [s] 就少了這個震動。
surprise.tip_en: The stress is on the second syllable [praɪz]; learners often make the first syllable sur heavy and long. [sɚ] should be light and quick, with only a slight curl of the tongue. Add no vowel between [p] and [r]: round the lips for [r] already while making [p]. The final s is actually a voiced [z]: the throat should buzz like a bee; saying [s] loses that buzz.

examples.en: Let's surprise Dad with a birthday card.
examples.zh: 我們用生日卡給爸爸一個驚喜吧。

examples.en: Grandma likes to surprise us with snacks.
examples.zh: 奶奶喜歡拿點心給我們驚喜。

surprise.variant_zh: 說快時第一音節常不捲舌，唸成 [səˈpraɪz]。
surprise.variant_en: In quick speech the first syllable often loses its r: [səˈpraɪz].
surprise.spelling_zh: 第一個 r 唸得很輕，常被漏寫成 suprise。
surprise.spelling_en: The first r is very light, so it is often misspelled suprise.

surprised.tip_zh: 這個字只有兩個音節，-ed 不自成一拍，不要唸成 [sɚˈpraɪzɪd]。字尾 [zd] 都是有聲子音：發 [z] 時喉嚨震動，舌尖不離開上排牙齦，直接收成 [d]。常見錯誤是把結尾唸成無聲的 [st]，或在最後加母音變成「ㄗ的」。重音一樣在第二音節 [praɪzd]，第一音節 [sɚ] 輕輕帶過。
surprised.tip_en: This word has only two syllables; -ed is not a beat of its own, so don't say [sɚˈpraɪzɪd]. The ending [zd] is two voiced consonants: let the throat buzz on [z] and, without moving the tongue tip off the upper gum ridge, close straight into [d]. Common mistakes are saying the ending as a voiceless [st] or adding a vowel at the end, like 'z-duh'. The stress is still on the second syllable [praɪzd]; the first syllable [sɚ] passes lightly.

examples.en: I was surprised by the big gift.
examples.zh: 那份大禮物讓我很驚訝。

examples.en: Dad looked surprised when he saw the cake.
examples.zh: 爸爸看到蛋糕時一臉驚訝。

surprised.variant_zh: 說快時常唸成 [səˈpraɪzd]，第一音節不捲舌。
surprised.variant_en: In quick speech it is often [səˈpraɪzd], with no r in the first syllable.

talk.tip_zh: 拼字裡的 l 不發音，學生常照字母唸成 [tɔlk]，把舌尖抬起來發 l。正確是 [tɔ] 後直接接 [k]：下巴放低、嘴唇稍微圓，發完 [ɔ] 舌根往上頂住收 [k]，不要加「克」的母音。分辨 talk 和 tall：talk 結尾是舌根的 [k]，tall 結尾是舌尖的 [l]，舌頭位置完全不同。
talk.tip_en: The l in the spelling is silent; learners often follow the letters and say [tɔlk], raising the tongue tip for l. The right way is [tɔ] straight into [k]: lower the jaw and round the lips slightly, then after [ɔ] raise the back of the tongue to close for [k], without adding a 'ke' vowel. To tell talk from tall: talk ends with [k] at the back of the tongue, tall ends with [l] at the tongue tip, two completely different tongue positions.

examples.en: Let's talk about our weekend plans.
examples.zh: 我們來聊聊週末的計畫吧。

examples.en: Please don't talk during the test.
examples.zh: 考試時請不要說話。

talk.variant_zh: 許多美國人 [ɔ]、[ɑ] 不分，唸成 [tɑk] 也正確。
talk.variant_en: Many Americans merge [ɔ] and [ɑ]; [tɑk] is also correct.
talk.spelling_zh: al 裡的 l 不發音，跟 walk 一樣。
talk.spelling_en: The l in al is silent, just like in walk.

teenager.tip_zh: 可以把這個字拆成 teen、age、r 來記：中間的 [e] 就是 age 的母音，要唸飽滿，不要弱化成 [ə]。重音在第一音節 [ti]，第二音節次重。teen 的 [n] 直接連到 [e]，所以聽起來是 [ti·ne]。[dʒ] 要把嘴唇嘟出去，不是注音的ㄐ；最後 [ɚ] 舌頭往後捲，不要唸成「者」。
teenager.tip_en: Remember the word as teen + age + r: the middle [e] is the vowel of age and should be full, not reduced to [ə]. The stress is on the first syllable [ti], with secondary stress on the second. The [n] of teen links straight into [e], so it sounds like [ti·ne]. For [dʒ], push the lips forward; it is not Mandarin ㄐ. In the final [ɚ], curl the tongue back; don't say it as 'je'.

examples.en: My big sister is a teenager now.
examples.zh: 我姊姊現在是青少年了。

examples.en: The teenager next door plays the guitar.
examples.zh: 隔壁的青少年會彈吉他。

telephone.tip_zh: 三個音節輕重不同：重音在 [tɛ]，中間的 [lə] 只是很輕的弱母音，一帶而過，不要唸成三拍一樣重的「鐵樂風」。ph 唸 [f]，上排牙齒輕碰下唇吹氣。最後 [fon] 的 [o] 嘴唇從圓慢慢收小，結尾 [n] 用舌尖頂住上排牙齦，不要變成舌根的 [ŋ]，否則聽起來像 fong。
telephone.tip_en: The three syllables have different weights: the stress is on [tɛ], and the middle [lə] is just a very light weak vowel that passes quickly; don't say three equal beats like 'tie-le-feng'. ph is [f]: the upper teeth lightly touch the lower lip and blow. In the last part [fon], the lips start round and slowly close smaller for [o]; end [n] with the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge, not with [ŋ] at the back of the tongue, or it sounds like 'fong'.

examples.en: Mom is talking on the telephone.
examples.zh: 媽媽正在講電話。

examples.en: Our classroom has an old telephone.
examples.zh: 我們教室有一台舊電話。

telephone.spelling_zh: ph 唸 [f]；字尾的 e 不發音。
telephone.spelling_en: ph is said [f]; the final e is silent.

television.tip_zh: 最難的是 [ʒən] 的 [ʒ]：中文沒有這個音，學生常唸成無聲的 [ʃ]，或注音的ㄖ。先擺出 [ʃ] 的嘴型、嘴唇嘟出，再讓喉嚨震動，就是 [ʒ]。[v] 要上排牙齒輕咬下唇，不要唸成 [w] 或 [b]。重音在第一音節 [tɛ]，不在 [vɪ]，中間的 [lə] 輕輕帶過。
television.tip_en: The hardest part is the [ʒ] in [ʒən]: Mandarin has no such sound, so learners often say a voiceless [ʃ] or Mandarin ㄖ. Set the mouth for [ʃ] with the lips pushed forward, then add a buzz in the throat, and that is [ʒ]. For [v], the upper teeth lightly bite the lower lip; don't say [w] or [b]. The stress is on the first syllable [tɛ], not on [vɪ], and the middle [lə] passes lightly.

examples.en: We watch television after dinner.
examples.zh: 我們晚餐後看電視。

examples.en: Please turn off the television and read a book.
examples.zh: 請把電視關掉，去看書。

terrible.tip_zh: 第一音節是 [tɛ]，母音跟 bed 一樣，嘴巴半開，接著舌頭捲起發 [r]；不要把 ter 唸成捲舌的 [tɝ]，像 turn 的開頭。中間的 [rə] 輕而短。字尾 -ble 是 [bḷ]：雙唇發完 [b]，舌尖直接頂上排牙齦發 L，中間沒有母音，常見錯誤是唸成「波」或「伯」。
terrible.tip_en: The first syllable is [tɛ], with the same vowel as bed and the mouth half open, then the tongue curls for [r]; don't say ter as r-colored [tɝ] like the start of turn. The middle [rə] is light and short. The ending -ble is [bḷ]: after the lips make [b], the tongue tip goes straight up to the upper gum ridge for L, with no vowel between; a common mistake is ending with a 'bo' sound.

examples.en: The weather was terrible, so we played inside.
examples.zh: 天氣很糟，所以我們在室內玩。

examples.en: Don't worry, your drawing is not terrible at all!
examples.zh: 別擔心，你的畫一點也不糟！

than.tip_zh: than 和 then 只差一個母音，最容易混淆：than 的 [æ] 要把下巴往下拉、嘴角往兩邊張大；then 的 [ɛ] 嘴巴只半開。開頭 [ð] 是舌尖輕放在上下排牙齒之間、喉嚨震動，不要唸成 [d] 或 [z]。結尾 [n] 用舌尖頂住上排牙齦收，不要變成 [ŋ]。
than.tip_en: than and then differ only in the vowel and are the easiest to mix up: for the [æ] of than, pull the jaw down and spread the corners of the mouth wide; for the [ɛ] of then, the mouth is only half open. The opening [ð] puts the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower teeth with the throat buzzing; don't say [d] or [z]. Finish [n] with the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge; don't turn it into [ŋ].

examples.en: My brother is taller than me.
examples.zh: 我哥哥比我高。

examples.en: I like apples more than bananas.
examples.zh: 比起香蕉，我更喜歡蘋果。

than.variant_zh: 在句子裡通常弱讀成 [ðən]，例如 taller than me。
than.variant_en: In a sentence it is usually weak, [ðən], as in taller than me.

thank.tip_zh: 開頭 [θ] 是無聲的：舌尖輕輕伸到上下排牙齒之間吹氣，喉嚨不震動。常見錯誤是唸成 [s]，像「三Q」，thank 就變成 sank（下沉）。[æ] 下巴要往下拉，才不會跟 think 的 [ɪ] 混在一起。結尾 [ŋk]：舌根抬起頂住軟顎發 [ŋ]，再原地放開成 [k]，不要加「克」的母音。
thank.tip_en: The opening [θ] is voiceless: put the tongue tip lightly out between the upper and lower teeth and blow, with no buzz in the throat. A common mistake is saying [s], like 'san-Q', which turns thank into sank. Pull the jaw down for [æ] so it doesn't blend with the [ɪ] of think. For the ending [ŋk], raise the back of the tongue against the soft palate for [ŋ], then release it in place as [k], without adding a 'ke' vowel.

examples.en: Thank you for the lovely birthday card.
examples.zh: 謝謝你送我這張好可愛的生日卡。

examples.en: Don't forget to thank your teacher.
examples.zh: 別忘了謝謝你的老師。

that.tip_zh: 後半的 [æt] 和 cat、hat 完全押韻，難點在開頭的 [ð]。學生常唸成 [d] 或 [z]，聽起來像 dat 或 zat。先把舌尖放在上下排牙齒之間，喉嚨震動發出嗡嗡聲，再把舌頭收回接 [æ]，下巴張大。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住牙齦停住就好，不要加「特」的母音。
that.tip_en: The second half [æt] rhymes exactly with cat and hat; the hard part is the opening [ð]. Learners often say [d] or [z], so it sounds like dat or zat. Put the tongue tip between the upper and lower teeth, make a buzz in the throat, then pull the tongue back into [æ] with the jaw open. For the final [t], just stop with the tongue tip on the gum ridge; don't add a 'te' vowel.

examples.en: Is that your new backpack?
examples.zh: 那是你的新書包嗎？

examples.en: I like that song a lot.
examples.zh: 我很喜歡那首歌。

that.variant_zh: 當連接詞時常弱讀成 [ðət]，例如 I know that you can。
that.variant_en: As a conjunction it is often weak, [ðət], as in I know that you can.

theater.tip_zh: 開頭 [θ] 是舌尖放在上下排牙齒之間吹氣，不要唸成 [s]，否則前半聽起來像 sea。拼字的 ea 在這裡不是一個長音，而是 [i] 加 [ə] 兩個音節，學生常省掉 [ə]，把三拍唸成兩拍。重音在 [θi]，後面的 [ətɚ] 輕輕帶過，最後 [tɚ] 舌頭往後捲。
theater.tip_en: For the opening [θ], put the tongue tip between the upper and lower teeth and blow; don't say [s], or the first half sounds like sea. The spelling ea here is not one long sound but two syllables, [i] plus [ə]; learners often drop the [ə] and turn three beats into two. The stress is on [θi], the following [ətɚ] passes lightly, and in the final [tɚ] the tongue curls back.

examples.en: We saw a funny play at the theater.
examples.zh: 我們在劇院看了一齣很好笑的戲。

examples.en: The movie theater is next to the bookstore.
examples.zh: 電影院在書店旁邊。

theater.spelling_zh: ea 分成 [i]、[ə] 兩個音節；英式拼成 theatre。
theater.spelling_en: ea splits into two syllables, [i] and [ə]; the British spelling is theatre.

these.tip_zh: these 和 this 很容易唸混：these 是長母音 [i]，嘴角往兩邊拉、像在微笑，結尾是有聲的 [z]；this 是短而放鬆的 [ɪ]，結尾是無聲的 [s]。開頭 [ð] 舌尖要放在上下排牙齒之間並讓喉嚨震動，不要唸成 [d] 或 [z]。結尾的 [z] 要一路震動到最後。
these.tip_en: these and this are easy to mix up: these has the long vowel [i], with the corners of the mouth pulled back as if smiling, and ends with a voiced [z]; this has a short, relaxed [ɪ] and ends with a voiceless [s]. For the opening [ð], put the tongue tip between the upper and lower teeth and let the throat buzz; don't say [d] or [z]. Keep the final [z] buzzing all the way to the end.

examples.en: These cookies are for the class party.
examples.zh: 這些餅乾是班級派對要吃的。

examples.en: Are these your socks on the floor?
examples.zh: 地上這些是你的襪子嗎？

these.spelling_zh: 字尾 e 不發音，s 唸 [z]。
these.spelling_en: The final e is silent, and s is said [z].

thick.tip_zh: 開頭 [θ] 如果唸成 [s]，thick（厚的）就變成 sick（生病的），意思差很多。發 [θ] 時舌尖伸出一點點，放在上下排牙齒之間吹氣，喉嚨不震動。母音 [ɪ] 短而放鬆，不要拉長成 [i]。它的反義詞 thin 只差結尾：thick 用舌根頂住收 [k]，thin 用舌尖收 [n]。
thick.tip_en: If the opening [θ] is said as [s], thick turns into sick, a very different meaning. For [θ], stick the tongue tip out a little between the upper and lower teeth and blow, with no buzz in the throat. The vowel [ɪ] is short and relaxed; don't stretch it into [i]. Its opposite thin differs only at the end: thick closes with the back of the tongue for [k], thin with the tongue tip for [n].

examples.en: This book is very thick.
examples.zh: 這本書很厚。

examples.en: Wear a thick coat on cold days.
examples.zh: 冷天要穿厚外套。

thin.tip_zh: thin 和 thing 只差最後一個鼻音，台灣學生常把兩個唸成一樣。thin 的 [n] 是舌尖頂住上排牙齦；thing 的 [ŋ] 是舌根往上抬、舌尖放下。練習時唸完 thin 先不要放鬆，感覺一下舌尖是不是停在牙齦上。開頭 [θ] 舌尖輕放在上下排牙齒之間吹氣，不要唸成 [s]；母音 [ɪ] 短而放鬆。
thin.tip_en: thin and thing differ only in the final nasal, and Taiwanese learners often say them the same. The [n] of thin has the tongue tip pressed on the upper gum ridge; the [ŋ] of thing raises the back of the tongue with the tip down. When practicing, don't relax right after saying thin: feel whether the tongue tip is resting on the gum ridge. For the opening [θ], place the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower teeth and blow; don't say [s]. The vowel [ɪ] is short and relaxed.

examples.en: My pencil is thin and long.
examples.zh: 我的鉛筆又細又長。

examples.en: I like thin pizza with lots of cheese.
examples.zh: 我喜歡有很多起司的薄片披薩。

thing.tip_zh: 開頭 [θ] 如果唸成 [s]，thing 就變成 sing（唱歌）。舌尖放在上下排牙齒之間吹氣，再收回舌頭發 [ɪ]。結尾 [ŋ] 是舌根頂住軟顎、讓氣從鼻子出來，拼字 ng 合起來只有這一個音，不要在最後多加一個「格」；也不要收成舌尖的 [n]，不然會聽成 thin。
thing.tip_en: If the opening [θ] is said as [s], thing turns into sing. Put the tongue tip between the upper and lower teeth and blow, then pull the tongue back for [ɪ]. The final [ŋ] has the back of the tongue against the soft palate with the air going out through the nose; the spelling ng together is only this one sound, so don't add a 'ge' at the end. Don't close with the tongue-tip [n] either, or it will be heard as thin.

examples.en: What is your favorite thing to do on Sunday?
examples.zh: 你星期天最喜歡做什麼事？

examples.en: Put each thing back in the box.
examples.zh: 把每樣東西放回盒子裡。

thing.spelling_zh: ng 合起來只唸一個 [ŋ]，g 不另外發音。
thing.spelling_en: ng together is just one sound, [ŋ]; the g is not said separately.

think.tip_zh: 最常聽到的錯誤是把 [θ] 唸成 [s]，I think so 就變成 I sink so（我下沉）。對著鏡子說，應該看得到舌尖從上下排牙齒間露出一點點，然後吹氣。[ɪ] 要短，嘴巴比 thank 的 [æ] 小很多。結尾 [ŋk] 舌根先頂住發鼻音，再輕輕彈開成 [k]，不要加母音。
think.tip_en: The most common mistake is saying [θ] as [s], so I think so becomes I sink so. Say it in front of a mirror: you should see the tongue tip peek out a little between the upper and lower teeth, then blow. [ɪ] is short, with the mouth much less open than for the [æ] of thank. For the ending [ŋk], the back of the tongue first presses up for the nasal, then lightly springs open for [k], with no added vowel.

examples.en: I think it will rain today.
examples.zh: 我覺得今天會下雨。

examples.en: What do you think of my drawing?
examples.zh: 你覺得我的畫怎麼樣？

third.tip_zh: 這個字舌頭要連走三個位置：[θ] 舌尖在上下排牙齒之間吹氣，接著馬上往後捲成 [ɝ]，最後舌尖頂住上排牙齦收 [d]。拼字 ir 只是一個捲舌母音 [ɝ]，不是 [ɪ] 加 [r]，和 bird 的母音一樣。常見錯誤是開頭唸成 [s]，或把結尾的 [d] 吞掉。
third.tip_en: The tongue moves through three positions in this word: for [θ] the tip is between the upper and lower teeth blowing air, then it immediately curls back for [ɝ], and finally the tip presses the upper gum ridge to close with [d]. The spelling ir is just one r-colored vowel [ɝ], not [ɪ] plus [r], the same vowel as in bird. Common mistakes are starting with [s] or swallowing the final [d].

examples.en: My classroom is on the third floor.
examples.zh: 我的教室在三樓。

examples.en: Tom came in third in the race.
examples.zh: 湯姆賽跑得了第三名。

thirsty.tip_zh: thirsty（口渴的）和 thirty（三十）只差一個 [s]，學生常把中間的 [s] 吞掉，I'm thirsty 就變成 I'm thirty（我三十歲）。舌頭的路線是：開頭 [θ] 舌尖在齒間，[ɝ] 往後捲，再把舌尖移到上排牙齒後面發 [s]，緊接著 [t]。[st] 之間不加母音，結尾 [ɪ] 短而輕。
thirsty.tip_en: thirsty and thirty differ by only one [s]; learners often swallow the middle [s], so I'm thirsty becomes I'm thirty. The tongue's route: the opening [θ] with the tip between the teeth, curl back for [ɝ], then move the tip behind the upper teeth for [s], followed right away by [t]. Add no vowel between [s] and [t]; the final [ɪ] is short and light.

examples.en: I'm thirsty. Can I have some water?
examples.zh: 我好渴，可以喝點水嗎？

examples.en: Playing soccer makes me very thirsty.
examples.zh: 踢足球讓我很口渴。

thirteen.tip_zh: thirteen 最容易和 thirty 聽錯。單獨唸時重音在第二音節 [tin]：母音拉長，字尾 [n] 用舌尖頂住上排牙齦收住，不能省略。開頭 [θ] 常被唸成 [s]，要把舌尖輕放在上下牙齒之間吹氣，接著馬上捲舌唸 [ɝ]。thirty 則是第一音節重、字尾沒有 [n]，兩個字可以一組練習。
thirteen.tip_en: thirteen is the word most easily confused with thirty. Said on its own, the stress falls on the second syllable [tin]: stretch the vowel and close with a clear final [n], tongue tip on the upper gum ridge; don't drop it. The opening [θ] is often said as [s]: rest the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower teeth and blow, then curl the tongue right away for [ɝ]. thirty, by contrast, is stressed on the first syllable and has no final [n]; practice the two as a pair.

examples.en: My sister turns thirteen next week.
examples.zh: 我姊姊下週就滿十三歲了。

examples.en: There are thirteen kids in my art class.
examples.zh: 我的美術班上有十三個小朋友。

thirteen.kk_flag: Two primary-stress marks. The General American citation form is [ˌθɝˈtin], main stress on -teen (it shifts to the first syllable only before a stressed noun, e.g. THIRteen kids), so stressed_syllable = 1 will mislabel the page and blur the thirteen/thirty contrast.

thirty.tip_zh: thirty 的重音在第一音節 [θɝ]，要唸得又重又長；第二音節 [tɪ] 輕輕帶過，字尾沒有 [n]，這樣才不會被聽成 thirteen。中間的 t 在美式發音中會變成很快的 [d]，舌尖輕點上排牙齦一下就好。開頭 [θ] 別唸成 [s]，先把舌尖放在牙齒之間吹氣，再捲舌接 [ɝ]。
thirty.tip_en: thirty is stressed on the first syllable [θɝ], said strong and long; the second syllable [tɪ] is light and quick, with no final [n], so it won't be heard as thirteen. In American English the middle t becomes a very quick [d]: the tongue tip just taps the upper gum ridge once. Don't turn the opening [θ] into [s]: put the tongue tip between the teeth and blow first, then curl the tongue for [ɝ].

examples.en: There are thirty students in our class.
examples.zh: 我們班上有三十個學生。

examples.en: We waited thirty minutes for the school bus.
examples.zh: 我們等校車等了三十分鐘。

thirty.variant_zh: 美式口語中間的 t 常變成很快的閃音，聽起來像 [ˈθɝdɪ]。
thirty.variant_en: In everyday American speech the middle t often becomes a quick flap, sounding like [ˈθɝdɪ].
thirty.kk_flag: The secondary-stress mark on -ty is unusual: GA thirty has only first-syllable stress, [ˈθɝdi] / [ˈθɝti] (the [d] stands for the flapped t).

this.tip_zh: 開頭 [ð] 常被唸成 [d] 或 [z]，聽起來像 dis 或 zis。舌尖要輕輕放在上下牙齒之間，同時讓喉嚨振動，手摸喉嚨會感覺到嗡嗡聲。母音 [ɪ] 要短而放鬆，不要拉長成 [i]，否則會像 these。字尾是無聲的 [s]，像蛇的嘶嘶聲，不是 these 結尾的 [z]。
this.tip_en: The opening [ð] is often said as [d] or [z], so it sounds like dis or zis. Rest the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower teeth while the throat vibrates; with a hand on the throat you can feel a buzz. The vowel [ɪ] is short and relaxed; don't stretch it into [i], or it will sound like these. The ending is a voiceless [s], like a snake's hiss, not the [z] at the end of these.

examples.en: This is my favorite book.
examples.zh: 這是我最喜歡的書。

examples.en: Can you help me carry this box?
examples.zh: 你可以幫我搬這個箱子嗎？

those.tip_zh: those 和 these 只差中間的母音：those 是 [o]，嘴唇先圓再慢慢收小，跟 nose 的母音一樣；these 是 [i]，嘴角往兩邊拉。開頭 [ð] 舌尖放在牙齒之間、喉嚨振動，不要唸成 [d]。字尾 [z] 常被唸成 [s] 或乾脆不發，要讓聲音嗡嗡地延續一下再停，跟 nose、rose 的結尾相同。
those.tip_en: those and these differ only in the middle vowel: those has [o], lips rounded and then slowly closing, the same vowel as nose; these has [i], with the corners of the mouth pulled sideways. For the opening [ð], put the tongue tip between the teeth and let the throat vibrate; don't say [d]. The final [z] is often said as [s] or dropped altogether; let the buzzing sound carry on a moment before stopping, the same ending as nose and rose.

examples.en: Those shoes are too big for me.
examples.zh: 那雙鞋子對我來說太大了。

examples.en: Can I have one of those cookies?
examples.zh: 我可以吃一塊那些餅乾嗎？

though.tip_zh: though 的 gh 完全不發音，整個字只有兩個音：[ð] 加 [o]。常見錯誤是把 gh 唸成 [f]（像 enough），或跟 through、thought 混在一起。開頭 [ð] 要有聲，舌尖輕碰上排牙齒、喉嚨振動，不是 [d]，也不是無聲的 [θ]；接著嘴唇變圓唸 [o]，唸起來和 go、no 押韻。
though.tip_en: The gh in though is completely silent; the whole word has just two sounds, [ð] plus [o]. Common mistakes are reading gh as [f] (as in enough) or mixing it up with through and thought. The opening [ð] is voiced: the tongue tip lightly touches the upper teeth and the throat vibrates; it is neither [d] nor a voiceless [θ]. Then round the lips for [o]; it rhymes with go and no.

examples.en: Even though it was cold, we played outside.
examples.zh: 雖然天氣很冷，我們還是在外面玩。

examples.en: Though I was tired, I finished my homework.
examples.zh: 雖然我很累，我還是寫完了功課。

though.spelling_zh: gh 不發音，though 和 go 押韻。
though.spelling_en: The gh is silent; though rhymes with go.

thousand.tip_zh: 開頭 [θ] 常被唸成 [s]，聽起來像 sousand；舌尖要放在上下牙齒之間吹氣，再把嘴巴張大滑到 [aʊ]，跟 house 的母音一樣。中間的 s 其實是有聲的 [z]，喉嚨要振動。字尾 [nd] 要連在一起收：舌尖頂住上牙齦唸 [n]，在原地輕輕放出 [d]，不要多加一個母音。
thousand.tip_en: The opening [θ] is often said as [s], so it sounds like sousand; put the tongue tip between the upper and lower teeth and blow, then open the mouth wide and glide into [aʊ], the same vowel as house. The s in the middle is actually a voiced [z]; the throat should vibrate. Close the final [nd] together: tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n], then release a soft [d] from the same spot, without adding an extra vowel.

examples.en: A thousand people came to the school concert.
examples.zh: 有一千個人來參加學校的音樂會。

examples.en: This book has more than a thousand pages.
examples.zh: 這本書有一千多頁。

thousand.variant_zh: 口語中字尾的 [d] 常幾乎聽不到：[ˈθaʊzən]。
thousand.variant_en: In casual speech the final [d] often drops: [ˈθaʊzən].
thousand.spelling_zh: 中間的 s 唸有聲的 [z]，不是 [s]。
thousand.spelling_en: The s in the middle is voiced [z], not [s].

three.tip_zh: three 常被唸成 tree、free，甚至 sree，因為中文沒有 [θ]。先把舌尖放在上下牙齒之間輕輕吹氣，然後舌頭迅速往後縮、捲起唸 [r]，[θr] 要黏在一起，中間不要插入母音。最後嘴角往兩邊拉，唸長長的 [i]。可以把 three、tree、free 排成一組，對比開頭的差別。
three.tip_en: three is often said as tree, free, or even sree, because Mandarin has no [θ]. First rest the tongue tip between the upper and lower teeth and blow gently, then pull the tongue back quickly and curl it for [r]; [θr] stick together with no vowel slipped in between. Finally pull the corners of the mouth sideways for a long [i]. Line up three, tree, and free and compare how each one starts.

examples.en: The baby is three years old.
examples.zh: 這個寶寶三歲了。

examples.en: I have three pencils in my bag.
examples.zh: 我的書包裡有三枝鉛筆。

through.tip_zh: through 拼字很長，但只有三個音：[θ]、[r]、[u]。ou 唸 [u]，gh 不發音，所以它和 threw 唸起來完全一樣。常見錯誤是 [θ] 變成 [t]，聽起來像 true，或跟 though 搞混。舌尖先在牙齒之間吹氣，馬上捲舌接 [r]，最後嘴唇嘟成小圓圈，把 [u] 拉長。
through.tip_en: through has a long spelling but only three sounds: [θ], [r], [u]. The ou is said [u] and the gh is silent, so it sounds exactly like threw. A common mistake is turning [θ] into [t], so it sounds like true, or mixing it up with though. Blow between the teeth with the tongue tip first, curl the tongue straight away for [r], then purse the lips into a small circle and stretch out [u].

examples.en: The train goes through a long tunnel.
examples.zh: 火車穿過一條很長的隧道。

examples.en: We walked through the park after school.
examples.zh: 放學後我們穿過公園。

through.spelling_zh: ough 在這裡唸 [u]，gh 不發音；和 threw 同音。
through.spelling_en: ough says [u], gh is silent; same sound as threw.

thursday.tip_zh: Thursday 常被唸成 Sursday，或跟 Tuesday 混在一起。開頭先咬舌吹出 [θ]，緊接著捲舌唸 [ɝ]：舌頭往後捲、不碰上顎，跟 bird 的母音一樣。中間的 s 要唸有聲的 [z]，喉嚨振動。重音在第一音節，後面的 [de] 唸得輕一點、短一點。
thursday.tip_en: Thursday is often said as Sursday, or mixed up with Tuesday. Start by blowing out [θ] with the tongue between the teeth, then curl the tongue right away for [ɝ]: tongue curled back, not touching the roof of the mouth, the same vowel as bird. The s in the middle is a voiced [z]; the throat vibrates. The stress is on the first syllable; say the following [de] a little lighter and shorter.

examples.en: We have art class every Thursday.
examples.zh: 我們每個星期四都有美術課。

examples.en: My piano lesson is on Thursday afternoon.
examples.zh: 我的鋼琴課在星期四下午。

thursday.variant_en: The ending -day is often reduced to [dɪ]: [ˈθɝzdɪ].
thursday.spelling_zh: 中間的 s 唸有聲的 [z]。
thursday.spelling_en: The s in the middle is voiced [z].

tiger.tip_zh: tiger 的難點在字尾 -er：常被唸成沒有捲舌的 [gə]，聽起來像英式發音或中文的輕聲。美式要唸 [gɚ]：舌根往上頂一下發出 [g]，接著舌頭立刻往後捲起、不碰任何地方，帶著捲舌的聲音收尾。第一音節 [taɪ] 是重音，嘴巴從大開滑向 [ɪ]，要唸得比 [gɚ] 長而有力。
tiger.tip_en: The hard part of tiger is the ending -er: it is often said as an r-less [gə], sounding British or like a Mandarin neutral-tone syllable. American English needs [gɚ]: raise the back of the tongue once for [g], then curl the tongue back right away without touching anything, ending with an r-colored sound. The first syllable [taɪ] carries the stress: open the mouth wide and glide toward [ɪ], longer and stronger than [gɚ].

examples.en: The tiger is sleeping under a tree.
examples.zh: 老虎正在樹下睡覺。

examples.en: My little brother drew a tiger in art class.
examples.zh: 我弟弟在美術課畫了一隻老虎。

together.tip_zh: together 的第一音節是很輕的 [tə]，常被唸成重重的 [tu]，把重音放錯在第一音節。正確重音在 [gɛ]，嘴巴半開。接下來的 [ð] 不能唸成 [d] 或 [z]，舌尖輕碰上排牙齒、喉嚨振動，然後馬上捲舌唸 [ɚ]。後半段 [gɛðɚ] 和 weather 的 [wɛðɚ] 押韻，可以放在一起練。
together.tip_en: The first syllable of together is a very light [tə]; it is often said as a heavy [tu], putting the stress wrongly on the first syllable. The real stress is on [gɛ], with the mouth half open. The following [ð] must not become [d] or [z]: the tongue tip lightly touches the upper teeth and the throat vibrates, then curl the tongue right away for [ɚ]. The second half [gɛðɚ] rhymes with [wɛðɚ] in weather, so practice them side by side.

examples.en: Let's play together after lunch.
examples.zh: 午餐後我們一起玩吧。

examples.en: My family eats dinner together every night.
examples.zh: 我們家每天晚上都一起吃晚餐。

tomato.tip_zh: tomato 常被唸成每個音節一樣重的 [tomɑto]，第二音節也張得太大。美式重音在第二音節 [me]，跟 May 的唸法一樣，嘴角往兩旁拉；第一音節只是輕輕的 [tə]，嘴巴幾乎不用動。最後一個音節 [to] 輕一點，嘴唇變圓收小；說快時這個 t 常變得像輕輕的 [d]。
tomato.tip_en: tomato is often said as [tomɑto], with every syllable equally strong and the second syllable opened too wide. In American English the stress is on the second syllable [me], said like May, with the corners of the mouth pulled sideways; the first syllable is just a light [tə], with the mouth barely moving. The last syllable [to] is lighter, the lips rounding and closing; in fast speech this t often sounds like a soft [d].

examples.en: I put a slice of tomato in my sandwich.
examples.zh: 我在三明治裡放了一片番茄。

examples.en: Mom cut a tomato for the salad.
examples.zh: 媽媽切了一顆番茄做沙拉。

tomato.variant_en: British and a few US speakers say [təˈmɑto].

tomorrow.tip_zh: tomorrow 的重音在第二音節 [mɑ]，第一音節是輕輕的 [tə]，不要唸成重重的 [tu]。拼字是 o，但美式 [mɑ] 的母音要把下巴往下拉、嘴巴張大，跟 hot 的母音一樣，不是圓唇的 [o]。拼字有兩個 r，其實只發一個 [r]：舌頭往後捲，再把嘴唇變圓，滑到最後的 [o]。
tomorrow.tip_en: tomorrow is stressed on the second syllable [mɑ]; the first syllable is a light [tə], not a heavy [tu]. The spelling has o, but the American vowel in [mɑ] needs the jaw dropped and the mouth open wide, the same vowel as hot, not a rounded [o]. There are two r's in the spelling but only one [r] sound: curl the tongue back, then round the lips and glide into the final [o].

examples.en: We have a spelling test tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我們明天有拼字考試。

examples.en: See you tomorrow at school!
examples.zh: 明天學校見！

tooth.tip_zh: tooth 的難點在字尾 [θ]：常被唸成 [s]，聽起來像 toos，或乾脆省略只剩 too。唸完拉長的 [u] 之後，舌尖要往前伸到上下牙齒之間，輕輕吹氣收尾，可以照鏡子確認看得到舌尖。[u] 嘴唇要嘟圓、拉長，不要唸成短促的 [ʊ]。複數 teeth 的結尾也是同一個 [θ]。
tooth.tip_en: The hard part of tooth is the final [θ]: it is often said as [s], sounding like toos, or dropped so only too is left. After the long [u], push the tongue tip forward between the upper and lower teeth and blow gently to finish; check in a mirror that you can see the tongue tip. For [u], round and push out the lips and hold it long; don't make it a short [ʊ]. The plural teeth ends with the same [θ].

examples.en: My little sister lost her first tooth today.
examples.zh: 我妹妹今天掉了第一顆牙。

examples.en: The dentist gave me a sticker after checking my tooth.
examples.zh: 牙醫檢查完我的牙齒後，送我一張貼紙。

turtle.tip_zh: turtle 的兩個音節各有一個難點。第一音節 [tɝ] 要捲舌，舌頭往後捲、不碰上顎，不要唸成平平的 [tʌ]。第二音節 [tḷ] 是成音節的 l：舌尖碰上牙齦發出 [t] 後就停在原地，直接轉成 [l]，中間不加母音，字尾也不要多出 [o] 的聲音。美式說快時，這個 t 會變得像輕輕的 [d]。
turtle.tip_en: Each of turtle's two syllables has its own trap. The first syllable [tɝ] needs a curled tongue, pulled back without touching the roof of the mouth; don't flatten it into [tʌ]. The second syllable [tḷ] is a syllabic l: after the tongue tip touches the gum ridge for [t], keep it there and turn straight into [l], with no vowel in between and no [o]-like sound added at the end. In fast American speech this t becomes like a soft [d].

examples.en: The turtle walks very slowly.
examples.zh: 烏龜走得很慢。

examples.en: We saw a big turtle at the beach.
examples.zh: 我們在海邊看到一隻大海龜。

umbrella.tip_zh: umbrella 一般美式重音在第二音節 [brɛ]，第一音節只是輕輕的 [əm]，常見錯誤是把 um 唸得又重又長。[br] 兩個子音要緊緊相連：雙唇先閉住發 [b]，馬上捲舌接 [r]，中間不要多加母音。[brɛ] 的 [ɛ] 嘴巴半開，跟 bread 的母音一樣；最後的 [lə] 舌尖碰一下上牙齦，輕輕帶過。
umbrella.tip_en: In standard American English, umbrella is stressed on the second syllable [brɛ]; the first syllable is only a light [əm], and a common mistake is making um heavy and long. The two consonants [br] must be joined tightly: close the lips for [b], then curl the tongue right away for [r], with no extra vowel between them. The [ɛ] in [brɛ] has the mouth half open, the same vowel as bread; the final [lə] is a quick touch of the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge, said lightly.

examples.en: Don't forget your umbrella today.
examples.zh: 今天別忘了帶雨傘。

examples.en: I shared my umbrella with my friend.
examples.zh: 我和朋友一起撐我的雨傘。

umbrella.variant_zh: 美國南方有些人重音放在第一音節：[ˈʌmˌbrɛlə]。

uncle.tip_zh: uncle 的 n 其實唸 [ŋ]：因為後面接 [k]，舌根要抬起頂住上顎後方，接著在同一個位置放出 [k]。開頭 [ʌ] 要短而放鬆，嘴巴微開，不要唸成張得很大的 [ɑ]。字尾 [kḷ] 是成音節的 l，舌尖往上碰牙齦就收，不要多加母音唸成 [ko]。
uncle.tip_en: The n in uncle is actually [ŋ]: because [k] follows, raise the back of the tongue against the back of the roof of the mouth, then release [k] from the same spot. The opening [ʌ] is short and relaxed, with the mouth slightly open; don't open it into a wide [ɑ]. The final [kḷ] is a syllabic l: lift the tongue tip to the gum ridge and stop there, without adding a vowel to make [ko].

examples.en: My uncle lives in Taichung.
examples.zh: 我叔叔住在台中。

examples.en: My uncle taught me how to ride a bike.
examples.zh: 我叔叔教我騎腳踏車。

uncle.spelling_zh: n 在 k 前面唸 [ŋ]；字尾的 e 不發音。
uncle.spelling_en: The n before k is said [ŋ]; the final e is silent.

understand.tip_zh: understand 的主要重音在最後一個音節 [stænd]，常見錯誤是把重音放在開頭的 un。中間的 [dɚ] 要輕而捲舌。[st] 之間不要加母音，舌尖從 [s] 直接滑到 [t]；[æ] 要下巴往下拉、嘴角往兩邊開，跟 stand、hand 一樣。字尾 [nd] 舌尖頂住上牙齦收住，不要把 [d] 吞掉，也不要多加母音。
understand.tip_en: The main stress of understand is on the last syllable [stænd]; a common mistake is stressing the opening un. The middle [dɚ] is light and r-colored. Don't add a vowel between [s] and [t]; the tongue tip slides straight from [s] to [t]. For [æ], drop the jaw and spread the corners of the mouth, as in stand and hand. Finish [nd] with the tongue tip pressed on the upper gum ridge; don't swallow the [d] or add a vowel.

examples.en: I don't understand this math problem.
examples.zh: 我不懂這題數學題。

examples.en: Do you understand the story?
examples.zh: 你看懂這個故事了嗎？

unhappy.tip_zh: unhappy 的重音在第二音節 [hæ]，下巴要往下拉、嘴巴張大，[æ] 不要唸成較窄的 [ɛ]，否則會像 heppy。un 後面的 [h] 常被吃掉，連成 u-nappy；唸完 [n] 要先吐一口氣發出 [h]，再接 [æ]。字首的 [ʌn] 是次重音，唸清楚但比 [hæ] 輕，最後的 [pɪ] 短而輕，跟 happy 的結尾一樣。
unhappy.tip_en: unhappy is stressed on the second syllable [hæ]: drop the jaw and open the mouth wide; don't narrow [æ] into [ɛ], or it sounds like heppy. The [h] after un is often swallowed, so the word runs together as u-nappy; after [n], breathe out for [h] before [æ]. The prefix [ʌn] takes secondary stress: say it clearly but lighter than [hæ], and the final [pɪ] is short and light, just like the end of happy.

examples.en: The puppy looks unhappy in the rain.
examples.zh: 小狗在雨中看起來不太開心。

examples.en: Don't be unhappy; we can play again tomorrow.
examples.zh: 別不開心，我們明天可以再玩。

unhappy.kk_flag: In GA the prefix normally keeps a full vowel with secondary stress, [ˌʌnˈhæpɪ]; [ən] is only a fast-speech reduction.

uniform.tip_zh: uniform 開頭的 u 要唸 [ju]，跟 you 一樣，前面有一個 [j] 的滑音，不能只唸 [u]。重音在第一音節，中間的 [nə] 要輕而短，不要照拼字唸成清楚的 [ni]。最後一音節 [fɔrm]：上排牙齒輕碰下唇發 [f]，嘴唇變圓唸 [ɔ] 再捲舌接 [r]，最後雙唇閉上收 [m]，不要在 [m] 後面多加母音。
uniform.tip_en: The u at the start of uniform is said [ju], like you, with a [j] glide in front; don't say just [u]. The stress is on the first syllable; the middle [nə] is light and short, not a clear [ni] as the spelling suggests. For the last syllable [fɔrm], touch the upper teeth to the lower lip for [f], round the lips for [ɔ], curl the tongue for [r], and finally close the lips for [m], with no extra vowel after [m].

examples.en: We wear a uniform to school on Mondays.
examples.zh: 我們星期一要穿制服上學。

examples.en: My new soccer uniform is blue and white.
examples.zh: 我的新足球制服是藍白色的。

usually.tip_zh: usually 中間的 [ʒ] 是中文沒有的音，常被唸成 [ʃ] 或 [dʒ]。做法是先擺出 [ʃ] 的嘴形：嘴唇往前嘟、舌頭靠近但不碰上顎，再讓喉嚨振動，就是 [ʒ]；舌頭全程不碰上顎，所以不會變成 [dʒ]。重音在第一音節 [ju]，後面的音節都要又輕又快。
usually.tip_en: The [ʒ] in the middle of usually is a sound Mandarin lacks, and it is often said as [ʃ] or [dʒ]. Set up the mouth for [ʃ]: lips pushed forward, tongue close to but not touching the roof of the mouth; then add voice from the throat, and that is [ʒ]. The tongue never touches the roof of the mouth, so it doesn't become [dʒ]. The stress is on the first syllable [ju]; the syllables after it are all light and quick.

examples.en: I usually walk to school with my brother.
examples.zh: 我通常和哥哥一起走路上學。

examples.en: We usually eat noodles on Sunday.
examples.zh: 我們星期天通常吃麵。

usually.variant_zh: 說快時常縮成三個音節：[ˈjuʒəlɪ]。
usually.variant_en: In fast speech it often shrinks to [ˈjuʒəlɪ].
usually.kk_flag: The [w] is a CMU glide artefact; Taiwan KK dictionaries write [ˈjuʒʊəlɪ] (careful) and fast speech gives [ˈjuʒəlɪ].

vacation.tip_zh: vacation 開頭的 [v] 常被唸成 [w] 或 [b]，因為中文沒有這個音；上排牙齒要輕放在下唇上，喉嚨振動，讓氣從縫隙擠出來。重音在第二音節 [ke]，它和第一音節 [ve] 都是 [e]，嘴角往兩邊拉，跟 cake 的母音一樣。字尾 [ʃən] 的 [n] 要舌尖頂住上牙齦，不要唸成 [ŋ]，和 station 的結尾相同。
vacation.tip_en: The opening [v] of vacation is often said as [w] or [b], because Mandarin has no such sound; rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip, let the throat vibrate, and push air through the gap. The stress is on the second syllable [ke]; it and the first syllable [ve] both have [e], with the corners of the mouth pulled sideways, the same vowel as cake. For the [n] in the final [ʃən], press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge; don't turn it into [ŋ]. It ends the same way as station.

examples.en: We went to the beach for summer vacation.
examples.zh: 暑假我們去了海邊。

examples.en: What did you do on winter vacation?
examples.zh: 你寒假做了什麼？

vegetable.tip_zh: vegetable 照拼字常被唸成四個音節，但美式通常只有三拍：[vɛdʒ]、[tə]、[bḷ]，第二個 e 不發音。開頭 [v] 要上排牙齒輕咬下唇、喉嚨振動，不要唸成 [b] 或 [w]。重音在第一音節，[dʒ] 後面直接接 [t]。字尾 [bḷ] 是成音節的 l，雙唇放開 [b] 後，舌尖直接頂上牙齦唸 [l]，不要多加母音。
vegetable.tip_en: Going by the spelling, vegetable is often said in four syllables, but American English usually has just three beats: [vɛdʒ], [tə], [bḷ]; the second e is silent. For the opening [v], rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and let the throat vibrate; don't say [b] or [w]. The stress is on the first syllable, and [dʒ] goes straight into [t]. The final [bḷ] is a syllabic l: after the lips release [b], the tongue tip goes straight up to the gum ridge for [l], with no vowel added.

examples.en: Broccoli is my favorite vegetable.
examples.zh: 花椰菜是我最喜歡的蔬菜。

examples.en: We made vegetable soup for lunch.
examples.zh: 我們午餐煮了蔬菜湯。

vegetable.spelling_zh: 第二個 e 通常不發音：三個音節，不是四個。
vegetable.spelling_en: The second e is usually silent: three syllables, not four.

very.tip_zh: very 常被唸成 berry 或 wery，因為 [v] 被換成了 [b] 或 [w]。上排牙齒輕放在下唇上，喉嚨振動，讓聲音從縫隙中嗡嗡地出來，雙唇不要合起來。接著 [ɛ] 嘴巴半開，馬上捲舌接 [r]，舌尖不碰上顎、不要彈舌。可以把 very 和 berry 排成一組練習，聽出開頭的差別。
very.tip_en: very is often said as berry or wery, because [v] is replaced by [b] or [w]. Rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and let the throat vibrate so the sound buzzes out through the gap; don't close the lips. Then open the mouth halfway for [ɛ] and curl the tongue right away for [r]; the tongue tip doesn't touch the roof of the mouth and doesn't flap. Practice very and berry as a pair to hear the difference in how they start.

examples.en: Thank you very much for the gift.
examples.zh: 非常謝謝你的禮物。

examples.en: The soup is very hot, so be careful.
examples.zh: 湯很燙，要小心。

video.tip_zh: video 開頭的 [v] 常被唸成 [w] 或 [b]，上排牙齒要輕咬下唇，並讓喉嚨振動。重音在第一音節 [vɪ]，[ɪ] 短而放鬆，不要拉長成 [i]。後面兩個音節 [dɪ] 和 [o] 要輕一點，[dɪo] 跟 radio 的結尾完全一樣；最後的 [o] 嘴唇由圓慢慢收小。
video.tip_en: The opening [v] of video is often said as [w] or [b]; rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and let the throat vibrate. The stress is on the first syllable [vɪ], with a short, relaxed [ɪ]; don't stretch it into [i]. The next two syllables [dɪ] and [o] are lighter; [dɪo] is exactly the end of radio. For the final [o], the lips start round and slowly close.

examples.en: We watched a funny video in English class.
examples.zh: 我們在英文課看了一部好笑的影片。

examples.en: Can I watch one more video, please?
examples.zh: 拜託，我可以再看一部影片嗎？

violin.tip_zh: 重音在最後一個音節 [lɪn]，不在開頭的 [vaɪ]；常見錯誤是把重音放在前面，或把中間的 [ə] 吞掉，變成只有兩拍的 [vaɪlɪn]。開頭 [v] 要用上排牙齒輕碰下唇再出聲，喉嚨震動，不是 [w]，也不是無聲的 [f]。字尾 [n] 用舌尖頂住上排牙齦收住，不要滑成 [ŋ]。
violin.tip_en: The stress is on the last syllable [lɪn], not on the first syllable [vaɪ]. Common mistakes are stressing the front, or swallowing the middle [ə] so the word has only two beats, [vaɪlɪn]. For the opening [v], rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and voice it, with the throat vibrating; it is not [w], and not a voiceless [f]. Finish the final [n] with the tongue tip pressed on the upper gum ridge; don't let it slide into [ŋ].

examples.en: My sister practices the violin every evening.
examples.zh: 我姊姊每天晚上練小提琴。

examples.en: Can you play the violin at the school concert?
examples.zh: 你可以在學校音樂會上拉小提琴嗎？

visitor.tip_zh: 中間的 s 在這裡要唸有聲的 [z]，喉嚨要震動，跟 zoo 的開頭一樣；常見錯誤是照拼字唸成 [s]。開頭 [v] 上排牙齒輕碰下唇，不要發成 [w]。字尾 -or 不唸 [ɔr]，而是輕輕捲舌的 [tɚ]。重音只在第一音節 [vɪ]，後面兩拍要又輕又快。
visitor.tip_en: The s in the middle is the voiced [z] here, with the throat vibrating, like the start of zoo; a common mistake is following the spelling and saying [s]. For the opening [v], rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip; don't turn it into [w]. The final -or is not [ɔr] but a light, curled [tɚ]. Only the first syllable [vɪ] is stressed; the other two beats should be light and quick.

examples.en: We had a visitor from Japan in our class today.
examples.zh: 今天我們班上來了一位從日本來的訪客。

examples.en: The visitor brought a gift for my grandma.
examples.zh: 那位訪客帶了一份禮物給我奶奶。

visitor.spelling_en: The s here is said [z], not [s].

walk.tip_zh: 拼字裡的 l 不發音，常見錯誤是照字母唸成 [wɔlk]。母音 [ɔ] 嘴巴張大、嘴唇微圓，舌頭平放不捲；一捲舌就變成 work [wɝk]（工作），意思完全不同。可以跟 talk 一起練，兩個字只差開頭的子音。字尾 [k] 用舌根輕輕收住，不要在後面多加一個母音。
walk.tip_en: The l in the spelling is silent; a common mistake is reading every letter and saying [wɔlk]. For the vowel [ɔ], open the mouth wide with the lips slightly rounded and keep the tongue flat, not curled; if you curl it, the word becomes work [wɝk] (job), with a completely different meaning. Practice it together with talk: the two words differ only in the first consonant. Close the final [k] lightly with the back of the tongue, and don't add a vowel after it.

examples.en: I walk to school with my brother every day.
examples.zh: 我每天和哥哥一起走路上學。

examples.en: Let's walk the dog after dinner.
examples.zh: 我們晚餐後去遛狗吧。

walk.variant_zh: 不少美國人唸 [wɑk]，嘴唇不圓、嘴巴張更開，兩種都正確。
walk.variant_en: Many Americans say [wɑk], lips unrounded; both are correct.
walk.spelling_zh: l 不發音，跟 talk 一樣。
walk.spelling_en: The l is silent, just as in talk.

water.tip_zh: 美式發音中，[t] 夾在兩個母音之間會變成輕彈的音：舌尖快速碰一下上排牙齦就離開，聽起來像很輕的 [d]；用力送氣的 [t] 聽起來比較像英式發音。字尾 [ɚ] 一定要捲舌，不能唸成沒捲舌的 [ə]。重音在第一音節 [wɔ]，嘴巴張開、嘴唇微圓。
water.tip_en: In American English, a [t] between two vowels becomes a light tap: the tongue tip quickly touches the upper gum ridge and leaves, sounding like a very light [d]; a strongly aspirated [t] sounds more British. The final [ɚ] must be curled; don't say it as an uncurled [ə]. The stress is on the first syllable [wɔ], with the mouth open and the lips slightly rounded.

examples.en: Please drink some water after you play outside.
examples.zh: 在外面玩完之後，請喝點水。

examples.en: Can I have a glass of water, please?
examples.zh: 可以給我一杯水嗎？

water.variant_zh: 不少美國人第一音節唸 [wɑ]，即 [ˈwɑtɚ]，嘴唇不圓。
water.variant_en: Many Americans say [ˈwɑtɚ], with unrounded lips.

watermelon.tip_zh: 這個字有四拍：主重音在 [wɔ]，[mɛ] 是次重音，其他兩拍要輕。最後的 -on 不要照拼字唸成 [ɑn]，而是輕輕的 [lən]，母音弱到幾乎聽不見，再用舌尖頂住牙齦收 [n]。中間的 [tɚ] 要捲舌，美式的 t 在這裡會輕彈，像很快的 [d]。可以先分成 water 和 melon 兩段練，再連起來。
watermelon.tip_en: This word has four beats: the main stress is on [wɔ], [mɛ] has secondary stress, and the other two beats are light. Don't read the final -on as [ɑn]; it is a light [lən], with a vowel so weak it is almost inaudible, then close the [n] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge. The middle [tɚ] must be curled, and the American t here is a light tap, like a quick [d]. Practice it in two parts, water and melon, then join them.

examples.en: We ate cold watermelon at the beach.
examples.zh: 我們在海邊吃了冰涼的西瓜。

examples.en: This watermelon is big and very sweet.
examples.zh: 這顆西瓜又大又甜。

weather.tip_zh: 中間的 th 是有聲的 [ð]：舌尖輕輕伸到上下排牙齒之間，一邊送氣一邊讓喉嚨震動。中文沒有這個音，所以常被唸成 [z] 或 [d]。第一音節 [wɛ] 重讀，嘴巴半開；字尾 [ɚ] 要捲舌。weather 和 whether 唸法完全一樣，靠句子分辨意思。
weather.tip_en: The th in the middle is the voiced [ð]: put the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower teeth, and let the throat vibrate as you push air out. Mandarin has no such sound, so it is often said as [z] or [d]. The first syllable [wɛ] is stressed, with the mouth half open; the final [ɚ] must be curled. Weather and whether sound exactly the same; the sentence tells you which is meant.

examples.en: The weather is sunny and warm today.
examples.zh: 今天天氣晴朗又溫暖。

examples.en: What is the weather like in Taipei?
examples.zh: 台北的天氣怎麼樣？

weather.spelling_zh: ea 在這裡唸短的 [ɛ]，不是 eat 的 [i]。
weather.spelling_en: Here ea is the short [ɛ], not the [i] of eat.

wednesday.tip_zh: 常見錯誤是照拼字唸成三拍的 [wɛd·nɛs·de]。第一個 d 和中間的 e 都不發音，整個字只有兩拍：[wɛnz] 和 [dɪ]。注意 s 唸有聲的 [z]，[n]、[z]、[d] 三個子音要緊緊相連，中間不要加母音。重音在 [wɛnz]，可以先唸 when [wɛn]，再加上 [zdɪ]。
wednesday.tip_en: A common mistake is following the spelling and saying three beats, [wɛd·nɛs·de]. The first d and the middle e are both silent, so the word has only two beats: [wɛnz] and [dɪ]. Note that the s is the voiced [z], and the three consonants [n], [z], [d] must be tightly joined with no vowel between them. The stress is on [wɛnz]; start by saying when [wɛn], then add [zdɪ].

examples.en: We have art class every Wednesday.
examples.zh: 我們每個星期三都有美術課。

examples.en: My piano lesson is on Wednesday afternoon.
examples.zh: 我的鋼琴課在星期三下午。

wednesday.variant_zh: 字尾也常唸成 [de]，即 [ˈwɛnzˌde]，兩種都很普遍。
wednesday.variant_en: The ending is often [de] too: [ˈwɛnzˌde]; both common.
wednesday.spelling_zh: 第一個 d 和 nes 裡的 e 都不發音。
wednesday.spelling_en: The first d and the e in nes are silent.

what.tip_zh: KK 的母音是 [ʌ]，嘴巴輕鬆半開、舌頭平放，跟 but、cut 同一個音。字尾 [t] 是重點：美式英語常把舌尖頂住上排牙齦就停住、不爆開，不要在後面多加一個母音唸成兩拍。在 What is 這類句子裡，t 夾在母音之間會輕彈，聽起來像很快的 [d]。
what.tip_en: The KK vowel is [ʌ]: mouth relaxed and half open, tongue flat, the same sound as in but and cut. The key is the final [t]: in American English the tongue tip often just presses on the upper gum ridge and stops without releasing; don't add a vowel after it and make two beats. In phrases like What is, the t sits between vowels and becomes a light tap that sounds like a quick [d].

examples.en: What is your favorite color?
examples.zh: 你最喜歡什麼顏色？

examples.en: What time does the movie start?
examples.zh: 電影幾點開始？

what.variant_zh: 也常聽到嘴巴較開的 [wɑt]；少數人開頭帶 [h]，唸 [hwʌt]。
what.variant_en: Also often [wɑt], mouth wider; a few say [hwʌt].
what.spelling_zh: wh 通常只唸 [w]，h 不發音。
what.spelling_en: wh is usually just [w]; the h is silent.

where.tip_zh: 母音是 [ɛ]，嘴巴半開，不要滑成 way 的 [e]；接著舌頭往後捲成 [r]，整個字只有一拍。常見錯誤是把 [ɛ] 和 [r] 分開唸成兩拍，或字尾完全不捲舌。where 跟 hair、chair、care 押韻，可以一起練；它和 wear（穿）的唸法也一樣。
where.tip_en: The vowel is [ɛ], with the mouth half open; don't let it glide into the [e] of way. Then curl the tongue back for [r]; the whole word is one beat. Common mistakes are splitting [ɛ] and [r] into two beats, or not curling at the end at all. Where rhymes with hair, chair and care, so practice them together; it also sounds the same as wear.

examples.en: Where is my pencil case?
examples.zh: 我的鉛筆盒在哪裡？

examples.en: Where do you want to eat lunch?
examples.zh: 你想去哪裡吃午餐？

where.spelling_zh: wh 的 h 不發音，跟 wear 同音。
where.spelling_en: The h in wh is silent; it sounds the same as wear.

whether.tip_zh: whether 跟 weather 唸法完全相同，只能從句子判斷意思。關鍵在第二音節開頭的 [ð]：舌尖放在上下排牙齒之間，喉嚨震動；唸成 [z] 會聽起來像 [wɛzɚ]，唸成 [d] 會像 [wɛdɚ]。字尾 [ɚ] 是輕輕的捲舌音，舌頭往後捲但不碰上顎。開頭的 wh 只唸 [w]，嘴唇先嘟圓。
whether.tip_en: Whether sounds exactly like weather; only the sentence shows which one is meant. The key is the [ð] that starts the second syllable: tongue tip between the upper and lower teeth, throat vibrating. Said as [z] it sounds like [wɛzɚ]; said as [d] it sounds like [wɛdɚ]. The final [ɚ] is a light curled sound: the tongue curls back without touching the roof of the mouth. The opening wh is just [w]; round the lips first.

examples.en: I don't know whether it will rain today.
examples.zh: 我不知道今天會不會下雨。

examples.en: Ask your mom whether you can come to my party.
examples.zh: 問問你媽媽你能不能來參加我的派對。

whether.spelling_zh: wh 的 h 不發音，所以和 weather 同音。
whether.spelling_en: The h in wh is silent, so it sounds the same as weather.

which.tip_zh: 母音是短的 [ɪ]：嘴巴放鬆、舌頭比 [i] 稍低，時間很短；拉長成 [i] 就會變成 [witʃ]，聽起來不對。字尾 [tʃ] 要把嘴唇往前嘟，舌尖先頂住牙齦再放開送氣，但後面不要加母音變成兩拍。which 和 witch（女巫）同音，跟 rich 押韻，可以一起練。
which.tip_en: The vowel is the short [ɪ]: mouth relaxed, tongue a little lower than for [i], and very short; stretch it into [i] and it becomes [witʃ], which sounds wrong. For the final [tʃ], push the lips forward, press the tongue tip on the gum ridge, then release with a puff of air, but don't add a vowel afterward and make two beats. Which sounds the same as witch and rhymes with rich, so practice them together.

examples.en: Which color do you like better?
examples.zh: 你比較喜歡哪一個顏色？

examples.en: Which book did you read last week?
examples.zh: 你上星期讀了哪一本書？

which.spelling_zh: wh 只唸 [w]，和 witch 同音。
which.spelling_en: wh is just [w]; it sounds the same as witch.

who.tip_zh: wh 在這裡只唸 [h]，w 不發音；常見錯誤是照拼字唸成 [wu]。[h] 只是輕輕呼出一口氣，喉嚨不要摩擦，跟注音ㄏ那種從喉嚨後方擠出來的聲音不同。接著嘴唇嘟圓往前推，發長的 [u]，跟 do、new、blue 押韻。
who.tip_en: Here wh is just [h]; the w is silent. A common mistake is following the spelling and saying [wu]. [h] is only a light breath with no friction in the throat, unlike Mandarin ㄏ, which is squeezed out from the back of the throat. Then round the lips and push them forward for a long [u]; it rhymes with do, new and blue.

examples.en: Who is your English teacher?
examples.zh: 你的英文老師是誰？

examples.en: Who wants to play tag with me?
examples.zh: 誰想跟我玩鬼抓人？

who.spelling_zh: w 不發音，wh 在這裡唸 [h]。
who.spelling_en: The w is silent; wh is said [h] here.

why.tip_zh: 母音 [aɪ] 是雙母音：先把嘴巴張大發 [a]，再往 [ɪ] 滑，嘴巴慢慢合起來。如果嘴巴張得不夠大、滑得不完整，容易跟 way [we] 混淆。開頭 [w] 嘴唇要先嘟圓再放開，不要直接從 [a] 開始。why 跟 buy、cry、dry 押韻，可以一起練。
why.tip_en: The vowel [aɪ] is a diphthong: open the mouth wide for [a], then glide toward [ɪ] as the mouth closes. If the mouth doesn't open wide enough or the glide is incomplete, it is easily confused with way [we]. For the opening [w], round the lips first and then release; don't start straight from [a]. Why rhymes with buy, cry and dry, so practice them together.

examples.en: Why are you late for class today?
examples.zh: 你今天上課為什麼遲到？

examples.en: Why don't we go to the park?
examples.zh: 我們何不去公園呢？

why.spelling_zh: wh 唸 [w]，h 不發音；y 在這裡唸 [aɪ]。
why.spelling_en: wh is said [w] with a silent h; the y here is [aɪ].

will.tip_zh: 字尾 [l] 是暗 L：舌尖頂住上排牙齦，舌根同時往後抬。常見錯誤是省略不發，或收成一個像「喔」的母音。母音 [ɪ] 短而放鬆，拉長成 [i] 會變成 wheel 的音。跟 fill、hill、still 押韻，可以一起練。在句子裡常縮成 'll，例如 I'll、we'll。
will.tip_en: The final [l] is a dark L: the tongue tip presses on the upper gum ridge while the back of the tongue lifts. Common mistakes are dropping it, or ending on a vowel like Mandarin 喔 (o). The vowel [ɪ] is short and relaxed; stretching it into [i] makes it sound like wheel. It rhymes with fill, hill and still, so practice them together. In sentences it often contracts to 'll, as in I'll and we'll.

examples.en: I will help you with your homework.
examples.zh: 我會幫你寫功課。

examples.en: We will go to the zoo on Sunday.
examples.zh: 我們星期天會去動物園。

will.variant_zh: 在句子裡不重讀時常弱讀成 [wəl]。
will.variant_en: When unstressed in a sentence it is often weakened to [wəl].

with.tip_zh: 字尾 th 在這個 KK 是有聲的 [ð]：舌尖伸到上下排牙齒之間，喉嚨震動，然後把音收住。常見錯誤是唸成 [s]、[z]，或乾脆把 th 吞掉，只剩 [wɪ]。前面的 [ɪ] 要短，不要拉成 [i]。with 跟 which、will、wish 只差最後一個子音，可以拿來對照練習。
with.tip_en: In this KK the final th is the voiced [ð]: put the tongue tip between the upper and lower teeth, let the throat vibrate, then end the sound. Common mistakes are saying [s] or [z], or swallowing the th and leaving only [wɪ]. Keep the [ɪ] before it short; don't stretch it into [i]. With differs from which, will and wish only in the last consonant, so use them for contrast practice.

examples.en: I go to school with my best friend.
examples.zh: 我和我最好的朋友一起上學。

examples.en: Can you help me with this math problem?
examples.zh: 你可以幫我解這道數學題嗎？

with.variant_zh: 也常唸成無聲的 [wɪθ]，兩種都正確。
with.variant_en: Also often said with voiceless th, [wɪθ]; both correct.

wonderful.tip_zh: 開頭 [wʌn] 跟數字 one 的發音一樣，o 唸 [ʌ]，不要照拼字唸成 [wɑn] 或 [won]。中間的 [dɚ] 要捲舌。最後的 -ful 只是很輕的 [fḷ]：上排牙齒輕碰下唇後，舌尖馬上頂到上排牙齦，不要唸成完整的 full [fʊl]，也不要把 [l] 省掉。重音在第一音節。
wonderful.tip_en: The opening [wʌn] sounds exactly like the number one: the o is [ʌ], so don't follow the spelling and say [wɑn] or [won]. The middle [dɚ] must be curled. The final -ful is just a very light [fḷ]: after the upper teeth lightly touch the lower lip, the tongue tip goes straight up to the upper gum ridge; don't say it as the whole word full [fʊl], and don't drop the [l]. The stress is on the first syllable.

examples.en: We had a wonderful time at the beach.
examples.zh: 我們在海邊玩得很開心。

examples.en: What a wonderful picture you drew!
examples.zh: 你畫的圖好棒喔！

wonderful.spelling_zh: won 的 o 唸 [ʌ]，跟 one 同音。
wonderful.spelling_en: The o in won is [ʌ]; it sounds like one.

word.tip_zh: 拼字是 or，但這裡唸捲舌的 [ɝ]，跟 bird、third 押韻；常見錯誤是照 for 的 or 唸成 [wɔrd]，聽起來會像 ward。嘴巴不用張大、嘴唇微圓，舌頭往後捲並一直保持到 [d]。字尾 [d] 舌尖頂住牙齦輕輕收，不要在後面加母音。
word.tip_en: The spelling is or, but here it is the curled [ɝ], rhyming with bird and third. A common mistake is reading it like the or in for and saying [wɔrd], which sounds like ward. Don't open the mouth wide; round the lips slightly, curl the tongue back and hold it until [d]. Close the final [d] lightly with the tongue tip on the gum ridge, and don't add a vowel after it.

examples.en: Can you spell this word for me?
examples.zh: 你可以幫我拼這個字嗎？

examples.en: I learned a new English word today.
examples.zh: 我今天學了一個新的英文單字。

word.spelling_zh: wor 的 or 唸 [ɝ]，不唸 for 的 [ɔr]。
word.spelling_en: The or in wor is [ɝ], not the [ɔr] of for.

work.tip_zh: work 和 walk 常被搞混：work 的 [ɝ] 要捲舌，舌頭往後縮、嘴巴半開；walk 的 [ɔ] 不捲舌、嘴巴張大。如果照拼字把 or 唸成 [ɔr]，聽的人可能以為你說的是 walk。練習時可以兩個字輪流唸，感覺舌頭捲與不捲的差別。字尾 [k] 用舌根頂住上顎收住，不要多加母音。
work.tip_en: Work and walk are often mixed up: the [ɝ] in work is curled, with the tongue pulled back and the mouth half open; the [ɔ] in walk is not curled and the mouth opens wide. If you follow the spelling and say or as [ɔr], listeners may think you said walk. Practice by saying the two words in turn and feel the difference between a curled and a flat tongue. Close the final [k] with the back of the tongue against the roof of the mouth, and don't add a vowel.

examples.en: My dad goes to work by bus.
examples.zh: 我爸爸搭公車去上班。

examples.en: I finished my work before dinner.
examples.zh: 我在晚餐前把作業做完了。

work.spelling_zh: w 後面的 or 唸 [ɝ]，不唸 [ɔr]。
work.spelling_en: After w, or is said [ɝ], not [ɔr].

world.tip_zh: 難點在字尾連續三個音：捲舌的 [ɝ] 之後，舌尖要往前頂到上排牙齦發 [l]，再直接接 [d]。常見錯誤是省掉 [l]，聽起來就變成 word；或在 [ɝ] 和 [l] 中間多加一個母音，唸成兩拍。練習時可以先唸 word，再慢慢在 [d] 前面加入 [l]，整個字仍然只有一拍。
world.tip_en: The hard part is the three sounds at the end: after the curled [ɝ], the tongue tip moves forward to the upper gum ridge for [l], then goes straight into [d]. Common mistakes are dropping the [l], which makes it sound like word, or adding a vowel between [ɝ] and [l] so it becomes two beats. To practice, say word first, then slowly add [l] before the [d]; the whole word is still one beat.

examples.en: I want to travel around the world someday.
examples.zh: 我希望有一天能環遊世界。

examples.en: There are many languages in the world.
examples.zh: 世界上有很多種語言。

write.tip_zh: 開頭的 w 不發音，write 和 right 唸法完全一樣。[r] 開頭時嘴唇微微嘟起，舌頭往後捲但不碰上顎，不要唸成 [l] 或注音的ㄖ。[aɪ] 從張大的嘴滑向 [ɪ]，最後的 [t] 舌尖頂住牙齦停住就好，不要在後面多加一個母音。
write.tip_en: The opening w is silent; write sounds exactly like right. To start [r], round the lips slightly and curl the tongue back without touching the roof of the mouth; don't say it as [l] or as Mandarin ㄖ. [aɪ] glides from a wide-open mouth toward [ɪ], and the final [t] just stops with the tongue tip on the gum ridge; don't add a vowel after it.

examples.en: Please write your name on the paper.
examples.zh: 請在紙上寫下你的名字。

examples.en: I like to write stories about my cat.
examples.zh: 我喜歡寫關於我家貓咪的故事。

write.spelling_zh: w 不發音，跟 right 同音。
write.spelling_en: The w is silent; it sounds the same as right.

writer.tip_zh: w 不發音，開頭直接是 [r]，嘴唇微嘟、舌頭往後捲。美式發音中，[t] 夾在 [aɪ] 和 [ɚ] 之間會變成舌尖輕彈一下的音，聽起來接近很輕的 [d]，所以 writer 和 rider 聽起來很像，差別主要在 writer 的 [aɪ] 比較短。字尾 [ɚ] 要捲舌，重音在 [raɪ]。
writer.tip_en: The w is silent, so the word starts directly with [r]: lips slightly rounded, tongue curled back. In American English, the [t] between [aɪ] and [ɚ] becomes a light tap of the tongue tip that sounds close to a very light [d], so writer and rider sound very similar; the main difference is that the [aɪ] in writer is shorter. The final [ɚ] must be curled, and the stress is on [raɪ].

examples.en: My aunt is a writer of children's books.
examples.zh: 我阿姨是童書作家。

examples.en: The writer read his new story to our class.
examples.zh: 那位作家為我們班朗讀了他的新故事。

writer.spelling_zh: wr 的 w 不發音，只唸 [r]。
writer.spelling_en: The w in wr is silent; only [r] is said.

yellow.tip_zh: 第一音節 [jɛ] 重讀，嘴巴半開；第二音節 [lo] 較輕。中間的 [l] 舌尖要確實碰到上排牙齦，否則會聽起來像 [jɛo]。字尾 [o] 是嘴唇由圓慢慢收小的滑音，跟 hello 的結尾一樣，不要唸成短短的「喔」就停住。可以先唸 yes 的開頭 [jɛ]，再接 [lo]。
yellow.tip_en: The first syllable [jɛ] is stressed, with the mouth half open; the second syllable [lo] is lighter. For the middle [l], the tongue tip must really touch the upper gum ridge, or it will sound like [jɛo]. The final [o] is a glide in which the rounded lips slowly close smaller, the same as the end of hello; don't cut it off as a short Mandarin 喔 (o). Start with the [jɛ] at the beginning of yes, then add [lo].

examples.en: My favorite color is yellow.
examples.zh: 我最喜歡的顏色是黃色。

examples.en: She has a yellow umbrella for rainy days.
examples.zh: 她有一把下雨天用的黃色雨傘。

yesterday.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [jɛs]，最後的 [de] 是次重音，不要把 day 唸得比開頭還重。中間的 [tɚ] 要捲舌，而且 [s] 和 [t] 要緊緊相連，中間不能多加母音。可以先唸 yes，接著輕輕帶出 [tɚ]，最後再唸 [de]，三拍是重、輕、再稍微回升。
yesterday.tip_en: The stress is on the first syllable [jɛs]; the final [de] has secondary stress, so don't say day louder than the beginning. The middle [tɚ] must be curled, and [s] and [t] must be tightly joined with no extra vowel between them. Start by saying yes, then lightly add [tɚ], and finally [de]: the three beats go strong, light, then slightly up again.

examples.en: I played basketball with my friends yesterday.
examples.zh: 我昨天和朋友一起打籃球。

examples.en: Yesterday was my little brother's birthday.
examples.zh: 昨天是我弟弟的生日。

yesterday.variant_zh: 字尾也可唸成較輕的 [dɪ]，即 [ˈjɛstɚdɪ]。
yesterday.variant_en: The ending can also be a lighter [dɪ], as in [ˈjɛstɚdɪ].

zero.tip_zh: 開頭 [z] 是可以拉長的震動音：舌尖靠近上排牙齦但不碰到，讓氣流摩擦，像蜜蜂嗡嗡叫。常見錯誤是唸成注音ㄗ那種先頂住再放開的音，或唸成無聲的 [s]。[ɪ] 之後馬上捲舌接 [r]，字尾 [o] 嘴唇收圓。重音在第一音節 [zɪ]。
zero.tip_en: The opening [z] is a buzzing sound you can stretch out: the tongue tip comes close to the upper gum ridge without touching it, letting the air rub through, like a bee buzzing. Common mistakes are saying it like Mandarin ㄗ, which presses and then releases, or as a voiceless [s]. Right after [ɪ], curl the tongue for [r], and round the lips for the final [o]. The stress is on the first syllable [zɪ].

examples.en: Ten minus ten is zero.
examples.zh: 十減十等於零。

examples.en: I made zero mistakes on my spelling test!
examples.zh: 我的拼字考試一題都沒錯！

zoo.tip_zh: [z] 和 [s] 的嘴型完全一樣，只差在喉嚨要震動；把手放在喉嚨上，摸到震動才對。常見錯誤是唸成無聲的 [s]，聽起來像人名 Sue，或像注音ㄗ一樣先把舌頭頂住再放開。後面的 [u] 要把嘴唇嘟圓往前推，聲音拉長，跟 blue、new 押韻。
zoo.tip_en: [z] uses exactly the same mouth shape as [s]; the only difference is that the throat vibrates. Put your hand on your throat: you should feel the buzz. Common mistakes are saying a voiceless [s], which sounds like the name Sue, or pressing the tongue and then releasing it like Mandarin ㄗ. For the [u] that follows, round the lips, push them forward and hold the sound; it rhymes with blue and new.

examples.en: We saw pandas at the zoo.
examples.zh: 我們在動物園看到了貓熊。

examples.en: My class is going to the zoo next Friday.
examples.zh: 我們班下星期五要去動物園。
